The TODO asks for a cap on consecutive forced continuations. maxStopContinuations (default 3) counts them per turn; past the cap Stop hooks are not asked, and the driver's turn budget bounds the turn in any case.

The TODO asks for per-session discovery of a project-local hook file. With discoverProject the component looks in each session's workspace and runs the file only after an owner approved its exact content by digest.
The same TODO as in the Claude Code bridge: continue false needs a run-level halt. Both dialects share the listener that cancels the turn with cause extension.
The TODO notes that Codex supplies stop_hook_active so a Stop hook can limit itself. The payload now reports the real value, and the component caps forced continuations itself.
The TODO asks for per-session project-local discovery of the Codex hook file. Project discovery is dialect-independent and gated by the same trust digest.
The marker is about renaming an npm package before a tagged release; in Go the deadline is a stage of the pipeline and has no package of its own to name.

The release decision leaves the tool: package delegate/steer keeps one subscription per agent and closes a channel when a message of source kind user is queued for the current step. The spec also asks the agent area to reserve the user kind to carrier entry points, so a component cannot label its own input as a steer.

The steer watch is shared: Registry.Wait takes a context, and job_output and any other blocking wait (the subagent area's wait tools) select on the same per-agent channel instead of each copying the release logic.
The shared transport keeps the original transport error as the cause of the failure value, so classification uses the status and the cause instead of matching words in a flattened message.
The open question is answered: Controls is logged with each request, and provider-specific request options are route configuration, not call configuration.
Exists only because Node could replace an npm package version inside a running process, which would make cached manifest identities stale; Go never replaces code in a running process.

The marker notes a gap between checking that a source is inside the workspace and opening it; the Go provider reads the source through the filesystem seam, whose rooted handle resolves and opens in one operation.
The marker asks for redeclaration warnings in the scoped REPL evaluator; the guest runtime and its evaluators are dropped by DH-ADR-8 and DH-ADR-PTC-1.
The Go contract defines the result for a request without a held session: no field is attached and no acceptance is recorded, which a test asserts.
The writer commits whenever batches are queued, without a batching window, so the acceptance record becomes durable at once and no separate lightweight checkpoint is needed.
The marker asks to evaluate persistent shell state. The Go design has persistent bash and pwsh tools on the terminal seam, and the one-shot executor stays stateless by decision.
The marker asks for built-ins in list(). In Go the built-in variables are the first contributor, so the list is complete before any consumer treats it as a catalog.
The clipping notice no longer advises a file search; it says how much was cut and how to read the rest, because command output is not a file.
The result reports the recorded stop cause, a timeout, and no longer guesses at an out-of-memory condition the signal does not establish.
The marker asks for an explicit infrastructure-failure outcome on the process handle. The Go execution has a Failed outcome distinct from a kill and from a non-zero exit, and it maps to a failed job.

The marker says deployment policy belongs in the tool pipeline and in confinement. In Go policy listeners sit in the guarded pipeline and every spawn for an agent carries a launch plan, so the tool holds no policy.
The clipping notice of the persistent pwsh tool is the same shared notice as the bash twin and no longer advises a file search.
The persistent pwsh tool reports the recorded stop cause, a timeout, without the unsupported out-of-memory guess.
As for the bash tool, the explicit Failed outcome of an execution replaces the signal-less kill that hid a start failure.
The watch code is not ported: the provider uses the harness watch service specified in libs/chokidar.md and keeps only skill filtering and invalidation, which is the extraction the marker asks for.

The final answer of a local child is read backwards from the end of its log and stops at the first non-empty assistant message after the run's start; the text-stream fallback is folded only when no such message exists. The whole suffix is never folded at settlement.
The outer abort race around session start-up does not exist in Go: start-up runs inside the session under one context, and cancelling it rolls the session back.
The per-send fields the marker wants consolidated become one send-state value owned by the session's pump goroutine, so there is no shared mutable send state to coordinate.
The marker asks for a generation boundary so a delayed prompt cannot settle a later send. Each bracketed command carries its own nonce and completes only on the end line with that nonce.
The marker asks for an explicit ordinal for concurrent child sessions; replay binds a child by its recorded lineage (parent script and creating tool call ordinal), which is that explicit key.

The marker asks for a replacement that syncs the file and its directory and keeps owner-only permissions on Windows; fsx.Replace does both (the Durable and KeepPerm options), in the package area A08 owns.
The Go Add operation takes no title parameter; the title defaults to the directory name and Rename changes it, so the unused parameter does not exist.

The event graph under-reports Client listeners because one TypeScript program cannot hold both the Host and Client context declarations; the Go design has one program and generates catalogs from the running registries, so the split does not exist.

The FIXME says the status event should carry richer fiber information than the previous state alone. The Go port's status notification is a typed callback that receives the fiber, the old state and the new state (Internal.OnStatus, src/go/cordis/tree.go:133), and DH-D-CORDIS-6 gives it a form owned by the subscribing fiber.

The TODO exists because JavaScript distinguishes synchronous validators from promise-returning ones and cordis rejects the latter. A Go schema is an ordinary function that may block, and the port calls it outside the tree lock (src/go/cordis/fiber.go:762-773), so there is no async case to add.

The TODO is a poor error from the mixin forwarder when the source service is missing. The Go design has no mixins or proxy context; a failed lookup returns a ServiceError that names the service and says whether it was undeclared or unavailable.
The FIXME marks the unmerged inject-mapping config; in Go an entry's inject is a list of names only and per-service config uses intercept, read in a fixed layer order, so nothing needs merging.

The harness neither ships nor edits OAR, so there is no distributed file to patch. The three fixes (an explicit permission mode is not overridden by skip-all, a failed start waits for the process to exit, installation probes use the run's environment) are requirements DH-LIB-OAR-R1 to R3. The bridge meets them from outside OAR, by owning the child process tree and its environment and by refusing an instance that states no permission posture; the two product providers meet them in their own code. Each has a test.

The patch stops the library re-parsing accumulated tool arguments on every fragment and keeps a Gemini tool-call signature the library dropped. The Go harness owns the stream decoder, so fragments are forwarded unparsed and unknown provider fields are kept as raw JSON; there is no third-party file to patch.

The patch stops the macOS signer from following symbolic-link aliases inside Electron's framework bundles; the Go release has no bundle and no directory walk, the files to sign are an explicit list of binaries, and never following a link while signing is a stated requirement.

The patch escapes copied cell values, hides canvas freeze lines and fixes read-only trackpad scrolling in a third-party grid. The Go design has no grid widget: cell text is escaped by the host template engine, and a table has sticky rows and native scrolling, so nothing remains to patch.

The patch stops a render loop on sheet switching, writes formula text as text instead of markup, keeps the selection of each sheet and fixes tab scroll buttons in the React component. With a server-rendered table a sheet switch is a fragment request and formula text is escaped by the template engine, so the causes are gone.

The patch removes child-process rewriting, makes native-addon extraction atomic, adds typed directory listing and a size check to the virtual filesystem and lowers Brotli quality; a compiled Go binary has none of these mechanisms, and the atomic-write lesson is kept as a requirement.
The patch adds the LZMA disk-image format to the builder's validator; the Go release builds no disk image and uses no packaging engine, so no third-party validator can reject a format.

The 35 KB patch makes ExcelJS find parts through relationships, match XML names by namespace, decode UTF-16 parts, keep CDATA and plain-text comments, and fail on missing worksheets. The causes are properties of ExcelJS: the Go reader uses excelize and encoding/xml, which resolve relationships and namespaces natively; the cases not established from source are a requirement with its own test, and no patched dependency is carried.

The 648 KB patch carries a two-line fix for the caret hiding behind an on-screen keyboard, inflated because it rewrites two minified one-line builds. In the Go design vendored browser files must be byte-identical to a published release and may not be patched, so the patch does not exist; the behaviour it protected stays a requirement, met by a release that contains the fix or by the island's own code outside the vendored files, and shown on a touch device by a real-browser scenario.

The patch repeats the same bare-URL rule in a second package that finds URLs again after parsing. goldmark recognises a bare URL in one place, so one configured pattern covers it and the two copies cannot disagree.

The patch makes a bare URL end before non-ASCII punctuation in the tokenizer. goldmark takes the bare-URL pattern as an option, so the rule is one configured regular expression with a test and no third-party file is edited.

Part 1 of the patch redirects node-pty's spawn-helper path for single-file executables; Go has no helper, because the runtime sets the session and controlling terminal itself between fork and exec. Part 2 releases node-pty's Windows output worker at kill; the underlying ConPTY rule also applies to Go and is met by design: output is drained by its own goroutine and close is ordered and bounded (DH-LIB-NODEPTY-R10).

The exemption lets subprocess-local run a postinstall script that restores the executable bit on node-pty's macOS spawn-helper. The Go PTY code has no helper file and Go modules run no install scripts, so there is nothing to exempt.

The entry denies an npm install script, which pnpm requires to be reviewed. Go never runs module code when it downloads a module, and the package is not in the Go design because no multi-provider library pulls it in.
This is an npm install-script policy entry for a Squirrel.Windows helper that electron-builder pulls in; Go modules run no install scripts and the package has no place in the Go design.

The entry lets esbuild's npm install script run so that it can select its prebuilt native program. Go has no install scripts: go mod download fetches source and executes nothing, and every dependency is compiled from source, so there is nothing to allow.

The entry allows koffi's install script, which compiles from source when no prebuilt binary is present, and records an exact pin to 3.1.1 in nine manifests because the 3.3.2 source build fails under GCC 13; golang.org/x/sys is plain Go source compiled by the Go compiler for every target, so there is no install script, no source-build fallback and one go.mod line instead of nine pins.
It is an entry in pnpm's allow-list of dependencies permitted to run npm install scripts; downloading a Go module never runs code, so there is no install-script allow-list.

The override forces every request for the package to the vendored folder so the npm install tree holds one copy. Duplicate package copies are a property of npm and pnpm resolution; a Go build has exactly one copy of a package, and these helpers come from the Go standard library.
The override forces every consumer onto a vendored, locally modified schema library; the Go design vendors and forks no schema library because config shapes are Go types.
A transitive dependency is forced to one version with no stated reason; the Go module policy requires a reason comment on every replace, exclude, version floor and tool pin, checked by a test.

Both causes are JavaScript mechanisms that the Go design does not have: the Loader unwrapping a module to its default export and losing the dependency list, and a property proxy whose service lookup walks ancestors only. Go components are compiled in and declare dependencies by type (DH-ADR-4), and the process gap that let 178 tests miss it is closed by requiring tests through the real loader path (DH-ADR-SECURITY-11 b).

The cause was a YAML expression object accepted where a boolean was expected and read as truthy, plus a snapshot check that accepted an unknown-tool result. Strict configuration decoding makes a non-boolean disabled value a load error and an independent check rejects calls to unregistered tools (DH-ADR-SECURITY-11 c, d); file and shell tools share one sandbox policy, so no permission preset governs only half of them (DH-ADR-SECURITY-1).

The agent did not know which URL and process served its session and mistook a bare Vite development server returning HTTP 200 for the application. The Go host renders and serves the UI from one binary with no separate client development server (DH-ADR-3), and it publishes its single canonical origin to the model context and tool environment (DH-ADR-SECURITY-7 d).

The cause was attributing launcher failure from the confined command's stderr text and exit code, an in-band channel shared with the child. The Go launcher reports its status on a separate inherited pipe that closes at exec, so a child's exit code or output can never be read as launcher failure (DH-ADR-SECURITY-3), and each backend needs a deterministic fake at the OS boundary plus a real-kernel scenario that is not allowed to count as passed when skipped (DH-ADR-SECURITY-11 a).

The always-on guarantee that no reader can rewrite history is kept, but Go cannot deep-freeze. The committed payload is encoded once and held as an immutable Go string; readers decode their own copy, and no exported function returns memory the session still uses.

Kept: the session is an append-only log, the only source of truth, and model history is derived from it. Appends still do not wait for a disk sync; the Go session additionally holds folds instead of the event list.

The three roles (contract, provider, consumer) are the seam of the Go design: a contract package holding a Go interface and its typed service key, provider components that implement it, and model-facing tools that import only the contract, with an import-direction test that fails when a consumer imports a provider. That is decision DH-ADR-ARCH-6, and outcome DH-O-10 is the observable result.

The second adapter for the same vendor was the npm library the Go design removes; its purpose is kept as a conformance rule: one table for four drivers, no vocabulary element that fewer than two protocol families produce, and fixtures recorded from real providers.
Kept in full: an ordered surface maintained by append and replace operations with cited sources, validated by a plan before commit and applied after, as pure functions in session/surface.
Failures stay serialisable facts without policy and a listener decides retry within bounds; the Go design adds a failure class per code, removes the unlimited mode and caps attempts per step.

Kept: one web seam whose providers register capabilities and never tools, with one package owning both model-facing tools and enablement-based registration. The note's refusal of an availability query is reversed in a small way, because Check returns a reason the settings page needs.

The Go design keeps the three event domains and the boundary rule that a fact which must survive a restart is a session event (design.md section 4.6). DH-ADR-PERSISTENCE-1 makes the session log the single source of truth, and DH-ADR-ARCH-4 separates live events, declared as typed keys by their owner, from durable event types, which are registered.
Kept: a tool describes its call and result card through a closed View interface on its declaration, which gives the server-side HTML templates one switch over a closed set.
Kept: every prompt fact has one owner, interpolation is strict, the persona is an ordinary section and assembly takes a per-agent input.
Kept: admission is one logged batch after the model call is bound, the request is built from the log alone, and no hook can change a request between admission and dispatch.
summary: Anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log and the objects it references.

reason: Final verdict: change the mechanism, keep the split. Go's context package already gives deadlines, fused cancellation and a recorded cause, so no timeout library is written; the rule that each capability keeps its own hard kill and that there is no central timeout service is kept, and the idle watchdog becomes egress.IdleBody.

Changed: the around-dispatch hook is kept, but the deadline is no longer an optional plugin for tools that ask; the pipeline gives every call a budget and enforces it, because an optional safety check is a composition mistake away from being absent.

The three roles (storage interface, local backend, policy) and the bounded preview with a locator the model reads later are kept. Three things change: a failed save still bounds the result, the reference is a structured field and not recognised text, and the store gains read, delete and reference-aware retention.

The goal (one executable per platform that needs no runtime installed and serves the SDK protocol) stands, but a Go binary is already a single file, so the pkg tool, its virtual filesystem and its patch are not needed; composition comes from configuration over compiled-in components.
summary: The Python SDK ships a single-file executable built with the pkg tool in Node single-executable mode. It serves JSON-RPC over standard input and output, and the plugins it starts are chosen by a configuration file supplied from outside.

reason: The provider id selects the adapter, a route has one owner and a duplicate fails; the generic library backend becomes harness-owned drivers and keyed routes.
Go has no AsyncLocalStorage. The initiating agent is a reference value in context.Context, which needs no drain bookkeeping at teardown; explicit identity stays authoritative at every boundary.
summary: The agent that started an operation is carried implicitly through asynchronous calls with AsyncLocalStorage.

reason: Kept: every call carries the caller's cancellation as a context and the result codes record whether the body started. Changed: a started body is awaited for a bounded grace period and then detached, instead of without bound.

Kept as decided: the window is a fact of the exact route, read from area A04's catalogue; measurement stays model-agnostic; thresholds, retention and the summariser target are per-route policy of the compaction provider. One change: headroom defaults to the smaller of 65,536 tokens and a fifth of the window, so a small-window route does not silently lose automatic compaction.

Final verdict after reading the note: keep its four answers in host form, drop the mechanism. Who may render into a place is enforced at load by Declare and Contribute; a component stays a pure function because a view gets typed data and no service; lifetime is the cordis effect; view state moves to the four named places. The single register call, the four props shares and the store seat exist for React and are not carried.

Final verdict: the first verdict stands. The note gives the browser a module system and the vendored loader so that client plugins load, unload and hot-reload like host plugins. No plugin code runs in a Go page; the host loader already governs every component, and what users saw of it (features come and go without a reload) is kept by contributions as effects and the composition epoch.
Kept: Inject is the only way to add context, it logs a splice and opens no turn, and a turn means one run of the model loop.
summary: inject() is the only way to add supplementary model-facing input, and a turn means exactly one execution of the model loop.

reason: Final verdict: keep. One resolver, the homedir leaf package, decides the home in the order explicit path, DSH_HOME, ~/.dsh, with a blank variable counted as unset and all user data under one root; three documents had named three different owners for it and this specification settles it.

The principle is kept and the mechanism replaced: one canonical model that every output is derived from, and an emitter that fails instead of degrading a type, are provided by the reflected schema of each Go type; the compiler-based extraction, the two faces and the type graph have no Go counterpart.

Final verdict: keep the rule that browser trust is enforced once for every route, with one change the first verdict missed. The authority fence (Host must be loopback, the bind address or a trusted host) is kept by area A18. The media-type fence (every POST must be JSON) cannot be kept, because an HTML form posts content types that a cross-site page may send without a preflight; the cross-site defence is therefore the origin check, SameSite=Strict and the standard library's cross-origin protection on state-changing methods.
Every message gets its id at creation and keeps it through every representation; Go enforces immutability through constructors and ownership instead of a run-time freeze.

Final verdict after reading the note: keep. The filesystem and subprocess services define one execution world, the terminal primitive belongs to the subprocess provider and readiness to the consumer; this is what lets an SSH provider replace the world without second shell or terminal packages.

The note chooses how Node runs the launcher from TypeScript source (the tsx ESM hook, after Node 26 removed a flag). It exists only because of TypeScript and Node: a Go program is compiled, so there is no source launch, transform hook or path mapping to decide.

Billed usage and context occupancy stay projections of the whole log, counting failed attempts and retries once each, and occupancy stays a reference figure; the request-context event belongs to the agent-loop area.
The runtime stays the one place that turns an adapter failure into a terminal chunk, and a consumer's own error never becomes a model failure; Go adds recovery from a panic and from a missing finish.

Final verdict: the stored document belongs to the store alone and is never loaded into the process environment, and the gap against the model's own tools is stated plainly; the keychain the note records as the deferred real answer is built. The note's route-registration half belongs to the model area.
Kept: a send only queues and returns a receipt that proves admission; a result exists only for a caller that owns the interval from receipt to idle, which the SDK and command-line areas define.
summary: Sending a follow-up only enqueues the message; no single message owns the activity that follows.

reason: Read in full. Kept: goal state is its own whole-value goal/change event appended by the goal service, the fold reads only that event for lifecycle state, a goal-sourced user message only advances the round count, and arming is never persisted.
summary: Goal state is a durable goal/change event carrying the whole snapshot, not something encoded in an inbox message.

reason: Final verdict after reading the note: drop the mechanism, keep its purpose. Decorators, the generated client projection and the two-faced gateway exist because host and browser are separate TypeScript programs. The purpose, an explicit allowlist of what a browser may call with validated input, is kept by the route registry: only a declared route exists and its form is decoded strictly.

Kept: one precedence order (launcher layer, overlays, home layer, profile layer, bundles, then the environment a value's expression reads, then the Go default) and the rule that a discovered .env may not set launch-only names, with proxy and endpoint names accepted from the home file only. Changed: the snapshot is never written into the process environment, which the note itself lists as not solved. The note's settings.yaml tier is already superseded upstream; credential ordering belongs to area A17.

Read in full. Kept: every launch mode is a profile, layers are an explicit ordered list applied over an empty root, only directly listed bundles contribute, and boot and the config dump share one composition function. Changed: a bundle is a named list of layer files embedded in the binary, not an npm package, and a profile is a compiled-in definition plus one layer file. Dropped with npm: pnpm-managed profile dependencies, two-anchor module resolution and the template copy.

Final verdict after reading the note: keep its model and move it to the host. Identity taken from the event's own data, one start per (kind, id), a pure fold in sequence order and a definition that owns its node are what make a replay equal the live view, and they do not depend on React. Not carried: contexts held in the browser, pending contexts for a start outside the loaded window (the host has the whole log and an index of starts), predecessor readers, publication cadences and keyed React snapshots.
Kept: a cancelled stream commits the delivered text and reasoning as an interrupted assistant message, leaves tool calls out, and records an attempt when nothing was delivered.
summary: When a model stream is cancelled, the text the user already saw is committed as an assistant message marked interrupted.

reason: Kept: a fork child has its creator's tool list and prompt head and receives its task after the inherited history. Go removes two of the note's listed ways to break the prefix (no generated SDK, no restored overrides) and one more by validating structured output in the manager instead of adding a child-only tool; a test compares the request head byte for byte.
summary: A forked child keeps its parent's tool list and system prompt prefix and gets its task after the inherited history, so the provider can reuse the cached prefix.

reason: Read in full. The ownership rule is kept: a service whose state is per process, or that a component outside the preset reads, belongs to the host plane, and the token meter is one. It becomes a check: a preset child that would write to a shared registry breaks the revision. The note's second decision is changed: joining a preset is part of agent creation in every profile, so an agent without a preset is an error instead of a silent agent with no tools.

Read in full. Its refusal rules are kept from the first release: a newer layout or payload refuses with the direction named, and an unknown type refuses unless marked ignorable. The single integer for the whole log is replaced by a payload version per event type, because one integer forces a rewrite of every event when one type changes.

Final verdict: the second key space of owner-scoped records, flows that own the write and success only after an observed commit are kept. Two parts change: prompts become registry items addressed to the starting peer so a reload re-attaches, and a flow can declare revocation. The pi-ai translations named in the first verdict do not exist in Go.

Final verdict differs from the first: not applicable, not replaced. The note defines four build layers and what a JavaScript bundler may inline or keep external so that module identities are shared. It exists only because of the npm build and run-time module loading; the Go UI has one layout template, embedded files and no bundler.

Final verdict: keep the three recovery rules (journal by cursor, state as whole snapshots, notifications that may be lost) and the split that the transport owner knows nothing about a feature's content. The carrier changes to server-sent events carrying fragments, and resume moves from a client journal to the host, which reads from the store by sequence number.

Kept: a reader of projected state requires the registry, a missing registry or key is an error and never a default, and one change event is raised per committed event. Go adds an explicit behind and pending state so that 'not ready' is also never a default.

Final verdict: the layering controller, adapter, renderer, component collapses because the host holds the state and renders it. Two rules are kept: each kind of state has one owner, and presentation receives data and never a service or the cordis context. They become the view contract (typed data in, HTML out) and the rule that a contribution closes over its own component's services.

The prepare-then-accept mechanism is kept as a transport service, but every contribution is off until the user opts in per route, which the owner's decision on data leaving the machine requires, and any route may use it.

Read in full: every application process starts through dsh and one named profile, protocol profiles reserve standard output and route end of input and signals through bounded disposal, and no package may ship its own application binary. All of that is kept and is simpler with one Go binary. Changed: the profile is selected for programs with the explicit --profile form, and the entry-point scan the note enforces is unnecessary because the module has one main package.

Final verdict: keep the rule, move the place. The note's point is that reading history must not run presenters, restore scopes or depend on the tool registry, and that a card is derived from the raw call, result and meta where it is drawn. That holds: the store never runs a presenter, and the host's UI layer derives the card at render time from logged facts, by tool name, without a step view or a live agent. The first verdict said the same in outline; the addition is that cards are registered globally so a cold session draws them.

Final verdict differs from the first in kind: ported. All four rules are kept as written: the catalogue owns every product-written string including accessibility names; shared building blocks take their text from the caller and have no built-in language; display text is never an identity; and a source check enforces it. The check becomes a test over templates, and text is resolved per request on the host.

Kept: every request is authenticated by a signed, audience-bound cookie obtained from a random launch token, after the Host and origin checks, with a durable signing secret so that a restart does not sign browsers out. Changed after reading the note: the token is one-time and short-lived instead of valid for the process lifetime, each browser has its own peer, sign-out and revoke-all exist, and the /connect handshake the note delegates to is not built.

Read in full. The first verdict assumed a Go webview shell; the owner removed it (DH-ADR-18), so no shell, no reserved desktop profile and no bundled pnpm exist. The note's goals are met differently: nothing has to be installed because the host and the UI are one binary; the release identity rule (shell, client and host qualified as one version) holds by construction because the UI is embedded (DH-ADR-WEBAPP-1); and the one update flow is dsh update (DH-ADR-ELECTRONUPDATER-3). Two lessons are kept: a release build ignores development resource overrides, and a release is signed or it is not a release (DH-ADR-ELECTRONBUILDER-2).

The rule is kept: every exact read is one observation with one cut, and values shown to clients come only from registered folds. The mechanism changes: a read transaction replaces the prepared-session cache and its leases, and a read may name keys.

Kept: one send_message operation in every direction, always delivered as a steer, with one durable source that names the sender, and no separate report tool. The receipt is durable in Go because the inbox is a logged queue.
summary: Agents use one send_message operation in both directions; it always steers the target and records one durable sender attribution.

reason: Read in full. Service methods that return per-session handles, with ownership carried by the handle and repair outside storage, map directly to Go interfaces with Close. Two changes: readers and writers are separate types, and no listener routes session events into storage.

Final verdict: keep the policy, change the mechanism. The policy is still resolved once from the launch environment and a project file may not choose the proxy, but nothing is installed globally: the egress service builds every client, which also covers the WebSocket and telemetry traffic upstream's dispatcher missed.

One failure type with a domain/reason code and typed details, declared once by the package that owns the failure and discriminated by code, is kept as jsonrpc.Error and the single error table of every stdio surface; unclassified failures fold to rpc/internal. The browser-only parts (fixed host facts on ctx.remote, cross-realm markers) are not carried.

The ignorable marker and the plugin: namespace are kept. The lint rule that limits the writer to experimental packages is replaced: plugin processes write records under their own owner segment by capability, and compiled-in experimental components declare ignorable types instead.

Read in full. There is no format 0 to migrate, but the rule itself is kept in the one place the Go design converts between formats: the upstream import refuses every unknown event type, also one marked ignorable, because an opaque payload may hold sequence references that a translation invalidates. The first verdict of dropped missed that.
Kept: setup receives the scope and the agent as separate parameters, events carry their agent, and a scope context has no reverse accessor for its agent.
summary: Agent identity is passed explicitly wherever it is needed; a context owns registrations and cleanup only.

reason: Read in part (problem and decision). The streaming stage chain is not built because the store reads only its own format. Its lesson, that any conversion must run in bounded memory, binds the layout migrations, the export and the importer, which all stream.

The note's aim is kept: the creation fact is recorded where it is known, and nothing scans all sessions. Its mechanism changes. When the note was written a parent owned its children; upstream later moved runtime ownership to the tree root. Go therefore keeps one ledger of starts and settlements in the root's log, which lists a tree in one read, holds the outcome that the catalog lacks, and still ignores records inherited through a fork.
summary: Each parent session records its direct children in its own catalog events, which are the authority for finding children.

reason: Kept: one settlement event per model attempt and no per-chunk events. The raw timed stream becomes the cold part of the payload so history reads stay small, and token usage stays in the hot part so no fold needs the stream.

Kept: the system prompt is an ordinary surface event at node 0, changed with the same append and replace operations, and the fold protects the head from any replacement that is not a system message over exactly that node.

Read in full. Kept: one ring per job, a model cursor and offset reads, one projection, one filtered event stream, caller-scoped operations. Two changes: pull sources and their pump are replaced by pushed appends, and the notice ledger's held read moves into the registry as Peek and Commit.
summary: One output ring, one projection and one event stream per background job, with two cursors over one storage.

reason: Final verdict: feedback as log-only events in the canonical session log with per-item versions and fork isolation is kept. The note's delivery half, feedback riding on a default-on session-log contribution and an upload triggered by feedback, is replaced by an explicit, previewed and confirmed send with a local export alternative.

Final verdict: the constraint behind the note is kept (a tab record or link holds only an address, and a view rebuilds itself from it). An address is now the URL of a fragment route; sharing one stream per address and pinning become interests of the host's tab record; the live helper makes every such region able to fetch itself. The browser registry, the hook and its page-lifetime records are not carried.

The consent rule is kept (only a new, own, explicit feedback submission authorises an upload; inherited feedback does not) and tightened by the owner's decision: off by default, a preview confirmed per submission, and one off-switch.

Read in part (decision). The rule that a read open converts in memory and never writes is kept in a simpler form: upcasters run when a row is read and stored rows are never rewritten by any open, so no publication step exists.

Final verdict: keep. A dedicated service keyed by session, with bounded line pages, byte reads and a change feed, and no file code in the session controller, is what the Go UI needs too. The client provider half and the dual-face packaging are not carried.

Kept from the first Go version: one spelling per fact, required placement on surface events and none on log-only events. A typed envelope makes most alternative spellings unrepresentable and the remaining rules are checked at append and at open.

The goal of the decision, that installing the harness never compiles anything, is kept and is met by Go itself; the mechanism, a family of prebuilt native packages with a Node-API addon and a static launcher, is not carried, because the binary makes the Landlock and flock system calls directly and the addon's asynchronous machinery exists only for JavaScript's single thread.

The note materialises the npm production graph in the application so that nothing is installed at first start, and keeps user plugins in the profile across upgrades. In Go there is no package graph: the binary is the runtime (DH-ADR-WEBAPP-1). The part worth keeping holds without a mechanism: plugins are local directories outside the binary (DH-ADR-13), disabling one keeps its files and configuration, and an update replaces one file and never touches the harness home.

The separate native welcome window with its own React bundle and blurred material is not built. First run is a setup page rendered by the host in the same UI (DH-ADR-WEBAPP-3, DH-D-WEBAPP-3). The note's hard-won rules are kept: credential onboarding has exactly one owner so that a skip is not followed by a second dialog; a skip is valid for one process and is never stored; and the setup path uses the product's real callbacks, not a preview. The native blur is a recorded loss.

The note separates watching a file (a shared observation by address) from reading it (bounded host reads), and takes the session only from the file address (note lines 13-17). Both rules stand. The host half is the workspace-file routes, where the session is a path segment; observation is no longer a client resource hook but an interest of the browser tab that replaces the preview region or flags it as changed. Renderer registration by extension is kept on the host. The first verdict stands.
Kept: Created is an ordered, awaited dispatch whose failure fails creation. One change: waiting for the agent or disposing it from inside its own creation returns an error instead of deadlocking.
summary: Agent creation runs its initialization listeners one at a time and waits for each; a failure fails creation.

reason: Kept with one tightening: the application, not the framework, owns the required entry ids (a Required list on each built-in profile definition, built from one shared spine list plus the profile's carrier set), a failing disabled expression is a failure and not a skip, and the audit runs only at boot. Changed so that it fails closed: a required id must also be present and enabled, and a layer that removes or disables one is a static issue, where upstream ignores an absent id and so lets a profile lose its carrier. A settle deadline is added because a Go component can block forever while loading.

Adopted fully instead of as a deprecation: the Go session interface never offers synchronous access to arbitrary history, state after resume comes from checkpointed folds, and old events are read in pages.
A message's source kind names its producer in the Go vocabulary; the conversion table for older session formats is not built because upstream files are not read.

The note computes one immutable table from package names to npm package directories and installs it into Node's resolvers. Node resolution does not exist in Go. Its goal, one immutable and inspectable answer to what code each configured name means, is met by the build catalogue that the loader uses as its resolver.

Final verdict: keep. Named reads follow the session filesystem backend's read authority and listing and watching stay inside the workspace. The stated exposure is restated: a file view can show any file the user can read. The preview of an HTML file with scripts is the UI area's to decide.

Final verdict: a factory exists because separately compiled packages cannot pass React components to each other with types. In Go a reusable assembly whose caller chooses inner parts is a view whose data struct has fragment fields, called like any function, so no second registry is needed. Global contributions inside it still use ordinary regions.

The first verdict (ported, as the wrapper of DH-ADR-3) no longer holds: DH-ADR-18 removed the native shell that would have wrapped the web application. The note's rule, that there is one composition and one serving path and never a second backend for a second client, is satisfied by construction because the browser on the HTTP path is the only kind of UI client. Its native directory dialog is replaced by the host's directory browser; the duty table records each remaining native control.

Kept: a log-only image/offload event names exact image occurrences and a pure function applies it to every later request, so the visible image set is rebuilt from the log. Two changes: the function is bound statically to the event type and payload version (area A01), and where a route declares its image budget the offload is planned before the request is sent.

Final verdict: change. One documented manifest is kept, but it is a Go struct for a local plugin directory, owned by area A22 and validated by the schema package, so the note's rule that every reader parses and validates for itself no longer applies.

Purity and ownership by the event's owner are kept, but registration as an unloadable effect is replaced: the rewrite function is declared statically with its event type and payload version, so it cannot be missing, needs no hand-over to offline readers, and old logs keep deriving the same history.

Kept: an operator-owned OpenSSH alias, an installed helper that runs local providers on the remote host, a lease, and no replay after loss. Changed: forwarded sockets and TLS pre-shared keys are replaced by a multiplexer over the one channel, and the helper is the dsh binary.

Final verdict: change. Kept: model-written code runs in a fresh child process confined by the same sandbox seam as shell commands, owned by the process service, and is never replayed after a denial or a failure. Not built: the Node guest, its control pipe, its bindings and its heap and message limits, because the owner decided there is no embedded interpreter. The first verdict (ported, with a guest runtime to be chosen) predates that decision.

Final verdict: change. The fixed descriptor 7 and the C-runtime descriptor table exist for a Node child, and the consumer of the channel, the program guest, is not built. The remaining need, a private inherited byte channel such as the launcher status pipe, is met by generic extra channels in the spawn spec.

Final verdict after reading the note: keep the exclusive provider slot and browser ownership by one live session; change the central choice of a name-only registry with no common action interface. The note rejects a unified interface because no consumer needs interchangeable methods; outcome DH-O-10 is that consumer, and with the Stagehand AI layer dropped (DH-ADR-24) every backend offers the same plain actions. The Stagehand, worker and private-model parts of the note are dropped by DH-ADR-24; MCP client start-up at agent creation is replaced by opening a browser on the first tool call.

Final verdict after reading the note: keep the exclusive provider slot; change the rest. A harness-owned tool catalogue in which the application is always an argument replaces provider-owned catalogues, because application grants can be enforced only where the harness can read the target. The in-process native provider the note adds is ruled out by DH-ADR-19, leaving the external MCP server as the only route. The session ownership broker the note rejects is adopted as a desktop lease held for one turn.

Kept: one service owns one logged directory per session, the header keeps the original project as identity and recovery destination, and the directory reaches the model as user context and never through the system prompt.

Final verdict: change. Kept: workflows get no second launcher and no second sandbox path; a workflow script starts through the one process starter under the session's standing policy, and no in-language fence is treated as a security boundary. Changed: the script is run by a named interpreter instead of a vm context in a PTC process, and the explicit no-deadline choice is replaced by a run budget counted in the host.

Kept: the command line, the web page and the tool call the same operations under one profile lock; profile files remain the persisted state; a toggle edits only the disabled field; saved state and activation are reported separately. Replaced: pnpm operations and build-script approvals are gone, and the queue shared with module replacement is the layer source's serial loop.

Final verdict: system-browser sign-in, authoritative local cancellation, success only after the grant is stored and sign-out that removes the local grant first are kept. The Electron embedding and per-desktop client identity in the note are dropped with the desktop application.

Final verdict after reading the note: replace. The note keeps the engine in its own repository and consumes it as an exact npm version with packaging and redistribution duties. The Go harness consumes no engine package at all: the engine is the LibreOffice the operator installed, found on disk and run as a child process, so there is nothing to version, package or redistribute; the harness owns only the adapter, the limits and the lifetime, as the note already assigns to it.

Read in full. The default is reversed by the owner: upload is off until the user opts in. The first verdict of ported for parity is overruled by DH-ADR-9. Reading the switch for each request and resuming from the accepted watermark when re-enabled are kept.

Kept as written: one base element per page, references and the token redirect relative to the document, no configured base URL and no forwarded-prefix header as a routing input, so one binary works at the origin root and under a prefix-stripping proxy. The rule for the page shell is requested from area C1; the redirect and the proxy scenario are this area's.

Final verdict after reading the note: keep. Admission before source bytes are read, bounds on readers, queue, source bytes and conversions, identity by exact content digest plus engine generation, a bounded transient cache that never bypasses authorisation, and the rule that only the last reader cancels shared work all carry over. Changed: no foreground and background priorities, bytes are spooled to files instead of held in memory, and the wait in the queue has its own bound.

The note gives each view or operation its own counted reference to a client session object and forbids a global current session (note lines 7-17). With no session objects in the browser there is nothing to count: a page names its session in the URL, a fragment route binds it as a path parameter, and the one UI status read interface the note asks for is reading.Status on the host. The rule that no global current session exists is kept. The first verdict stands.

There is no native dialog. The goal, a recovery path that does not depend on the component that failed, is met by one diagnostic on standard error with a crash-report file from the web host area, and in the browser by a host-not-reachable state shown from markup the page already holds (DH-ADR-WEBAPP-4, DH-D-WEBAPP-5). Lessons kept: the first report claims the presentation and later ones go to the log; recovery never resets configuration by itself. Two gaps are reported in the spec: no finished specification defines the start without plugins, and upstream's option to set the profile patch aside with its exact bytes has no counterpart yet.
The Go format stores a tool result as its own tool-role message from the first version and keeps the closed set of five surface types; the upstream conversion from the wrapper form has no subject.

Kept: the host inspects before anything is added and reports a specific problem, and a failed operation leaves no half-installed state. The mechanism differs: inspection reads a local directory through area A22's inspector, A22 makes the approved copy before the entry is written, and because the management operation itself is one write of one file there are no profile files to snapshot and restore and no run to cancel; a copy whose entry was never written is unreferenced and is removed by retention.

The goal is kept for one session and no longer for the profile: an agent adds a capability mid-conversation by attaching a local plugin directory it authored to its own session through plugin_manager, after one consent from an owner, and the plugin runs as a confined process, not host code. The persistence is dropped on purpose: area A22 (DH-ADR-EXT-8) rules that no tool call can make a plugin durable or host-wide, which applies DH-ADR-16; a durable installation is an owner's action in the command line or the plugins page. The cordis_inspect tool the note mentions belongs to area A22.

Final verdict after reading the note: keep its rules and change its packaging. Kept: providers selected by exact id with no fallback, so a local failure can never upload speech; recordings and transcripts transient until the user submits ordinary text; no turn and no session event; insertion only against an unchanged draft; nothing heavy allocated by enabling the feature. Changed: the native runtime is not installed with the product and models are not downloaded by it, the operator installs a recognition program; five packages become three components and one island. The note's rejection of browser-native recognition is kept for the same reason.

Read in full. Kept: schedules are host storage that outlives sessions, storage is authoritative and a failure is never read as no tasks, inbox persistence precedes the receipt. Changed: the whole-unit document becomes typed rows, fail closed applies per row, a retry policy exists, and version 1 reading is not needed.
summary: Scheduled messages live in host-owned storage, survive restart, and an unreadable store is a load failure.

reason: Final verdict: keep. A terminal a person types into runs with the operating-system user's permissions, outside the agent sandbox, with the scrubbed environment, asks no approval, survives a change of the agent's mode and writes no session event. Consequence kept in view: UI access is command execution, so the routes are owner only.
Two routes keep two credential sources with no fallback, and sign-out cancels running work that used the account, found from the logged request header and not from a second provider field.
Kept: a change to the visible tool set is a developer/message surface event whose additions are bound by headerSeq to an earlier request/header, checked when the append is planned.

Final verdict after reading the note; the first verdict (ported) is overruled by the owner. The note chooses a locally owned object library over a Swift helper and rejects depending on the complete upstream driver because that does not meet the requirement for locally owned implementation. DH-ADR-19 reverses that requirement: the driver is external and nothing native is locally owned. The note's one surviving idea, that every operation goes through the normal tool path for authorization, logging and image admission, holds for A16's eight plain tools.

Read in full. The mandatory check before a session is exposed is kept and split: the store checks structure (contiguous order, registered or ignorable type, known payload version), and the pass over relationships between events needs their meaning, so it belongs to the session of area A01 and runs once before publication. An unfinished tail may stay open.

The fingerprint policy exists for TypeScript union types. In Go the raw payload string is authoritative and decoding from the log tolerates unknown fields and kinds, so a new attribution kind is additive without a policy. Request-only input can enter a request only through a logged event that declares a builder.

Final verdict: keep acquire-then-use and no stored process identity. Simplified: the host, not the browser, picks the candidate blank session of a workspace, takes its lease, re-checks it under the lease and creates a new session when another process holds it. Several processes share one home (DH-ADR-12), so the race is real in Go.

Read in full. Kept: targets session, new_once and new; the session id reserved before each create attempt; latest-only catch-up; the 60 second floor; one execution slot for a reused target. Change notices become derived at turn start instead of pushed to loaded agents only.
summary: Three delivery targets, session ids reserved before creation, latest-only catch-up and a per-task delivery floor.

reason: Final verdict: the goal stands (no base64, ranged reads, one authorisation path) and the mechanism goes. Bytes are an ordinary HTTP response with Range from a route that names the session, so it shares routing, access and errors with every other route; the multipart byte codec of the typed call is not needed.

Read in full. Kept: a preset is ordinary loader configuration, the registry owns each revision, activation is eager, a failed declaration stays listed and rejects new bindings without stopping start-up, agents and children retain the revision they joined, and the session log records the preset identity. Changed: an override merges into a keyed child map instead of replacing the list, the isolated realm is built automatically, edits go through the one config edit path, and each binding is logged with a digest.

The note plans npm registries and mirrors for pnpm installs. DH-ADR-13 excludes download, so there is no registry to plan. The first verdict expected its goals to carry to a Go download source; none exists, and the rule that a private source never falls back to a public one is recorded in DH-ADR-BOOT-11 for a later registry.

The outcome is kept: a config value can change without restarting its component. The mechanism changes: a component that can take new config in place registers the port's update hook and receives the new typed config, so no schema volatility metadata and no shared reference is needed (DH-ADR-LOADER-7); a field is marked live with a tag that the harness schema package turns into a helper called inside that hook (DH-ADR-SCHEMA-5). The reference type itself is not built (DH-ADR-COSMOKIT-2, a recommended default the owner may overturn).

Kept as written: one concrete IPv4 or IPv6 literal, loopback by default, the unspecified address refused in every spelling at load, the bind literal accepted as Host on any port, every other name only from trusted hosts, and a public URL required for a zoned non-loopback bind. The Go parser is net/netip and the listener is opened from the parsed value.

Kept: every value is declared once in its component's config type, settings only lists live fields and writes to the one writable layer, and an edit a higher layer would shadow fails before saving. The loader's merge operation removes the note's side effect that an edit pins the entry's other fields, and the legacy settings.yaml import has nothing to import.

Exists only because of Node module resolution and the npm package layout: it defines the ancestor node_modules search inside a profile. Go components are linked at build time and plugin processes share no modules with the host.

Both rules of the note repair a cache that is a different store with its own sequence space. A checkpoint row keyed by session in the session's own database needs no identity witness or fork cut, and every seq it carries is the log's, so there is no cached-versus-sequenced distinction to keep.

Final verdict: the generated duplex stream is not the Go transport. Updates flow down on one event stream and input goes up as ordinary requests. Kept: an explicit per-request context with the caller's principal and a cancellation signal, and resume owned above the transport. The one duplex channel is the terminal socket, with acknowledgements in both directions; the SDK has its own protocol.

Final verdict: the two settlements are kept (pending at the deadline, a later answer as a durable user message, never an approval); the client claim stream is replaced by a host-owned deadline with a hold tied to the view's connection, and the legacy and timed schemas become one.

Final verdict differs from the first, which assumed a Go desktop shell: dropped. The note governs which rows of a macOS desktop window can be dragged. The owner removed the desktop application, so there is no window chrome to declare.

Final verdict: keep the web half. Overrides are stored per device in the browser because one host serves devices with different keyboards and reserved keys; a binding is active only after it was saved; an unreadable or newer record blocks editing and is never rewritten; simultaneous writes from two tabs are last-writer-wins. The desktop file store is gone with the desktop application.

Kept: request headers record the active tools and the session keeps a capability-independent tool-history fold that resolves additions through their historical header. Projecting it for each provider route belongs to area A04.

The note keeps a tab's DOM ancestors connected through session switches, pane moves and floating, because Electron's webview resets its guest when detached (note lines 9-13). The webview and the browser tab are gone. The goal that remains, that switching does not lose a live thing, is met without DOM retention: the terminal's screen lives in the host emulator and is redrawn from a snapshot, and a preview restores its position from the per-tab store. The first verdict's reference to a system webview no longer applies.

Final verdict: keep the separation the note argues for (a business grouping rule apart from a generic assembler, one grouping result for every display density) and drop the React identity constraints that shaped its API. In the Go design the rule is area C3's pure reading plan; this area's renderer draws each node into the container the plan names and replaces a group's shell once when the plan closes it.

The first verdict (ported to a Go shell) no longer holds. The note exists because on Windows closing the last window quits the host, so a close shortcut with a stale target must never fall back to the window. In the Go product the browser owns its close-tab key and a page cannot take it, and closing a tab or every tab stops nothing (DH-ADR-WEBAPP-4), so the danger is gone. The lesson is kept as a rule for UI shortcuts: a command whose target is stale does nothing.

Final verdict: change. The goal (an experimental capability is visible and one switch away) is kept; with every component compiled in, an optional bundle is a default-off loader entry on area A27's optional list, and the admission test of npm install cost has no subject.

Kept: an uncaught failure is fatal, reported once and never resumed, with a release hook under a fixed bound; boot owns that one exit path and area A18 owns the diagnostic's content and file. The best-effort spill rule is area A07's. The desktop crash-report dialog has no subject under DH-ADR-18 and becomes the diagnostic file; the client batch retry has no subject under DH-ADR-3.

The note partitions Electron browser storage per account for embedded vendor Platform pages. The owner dropped embedded sign-in and account pages (DH-ADR-18): they open in the system browser, whose own profile keeps a site's preferences. There is no embedded view whose storage could be partitioned.

Read in full. Kept: delete removes the row and its delivery records with no deleted state, and history is bounded by age (30 days) and count (200) on the only write path, always keeping the latest record.
summary: Hard delete of schedules and delivery history bounded by age and count.

reason: Final verdict after reading the note: keep. One row per call id passes through preparing, start and result, and the preparing stage changes no event and no dispatch timing. In the Go design the reading plan gives the three stages one row, the preparing stage is drawn from the live frame and the other two from durable events, and area C4 draws the card.

Final verdict: drop. The decision keeps one Node REPL process per agent so JavaScript variables survive between programs. With no interpreter there is nothing to retain: a script keeps state in files and the persistent shell tool is the stateful form. The note's rule that programs are never re-run after restart, resume or fork is kept by DH-ADR-PTC-6. The first verdict (ported) assumed a JavaScript engine would be chosen.

There is no window to hide and no tray. The outcome the note wanted is kept: closing the UI never stops running work, because the host is a separate process from every tab, and stopping the host asks first when agents, queued input, jobs or armed schedules would be interrupted (DH-ADR-WEBAPP-4, DH-D-WEBAPP-5, with the command-line area's stop function). Lessons kept: an inspection that does not answer in two seconds counts as work running; a second request joins the open question; an operating-system shutdown never waits for an answer. The tray icon is a recorded loss.

Kept: optional TLS on the one listener from a certificate and key file, bad material fails start-up with no fallback to HTTP, the listener's own protocol decides the Secure attribute, and the harness issues no certificate. Changed: a non-loopback listener without TLS is refused unless an explicit flag is set, where upstream warns, and replaced certificate files are picked up without a restart.

Read in full. The byte cap per request, the longest run that fits, and the rule that an oversized event blocks the upload without failing the model request are kept, because an unbounded request body is wrong in any runtime.

The account listing, the row-by-row decoding and the locally evaluated version gate are kept; the last good listing is now stored and a refused model is shown as unavailable. The gate's version key is an owner question because the Go build does not share upstream's version numbers.

Final verdict: keep. A lazy reader over streamed argument text avoids re-parsing a growing JSON text on every delta; it is the jsonscan leaf package, used by the host that renders the preparing row, and the rule that short descriptive fields are declared first carries because schema properties follow struct declaration order.

Read in full. Kept: the model tools are a separate component mounted per preset over a host-wide service, so a preset without them pays no tokens. The note's host-wide reach of the tools is narrowed to the caller's own schedules.
summary: Schedule tools are a preset-level consumer; the schedule service stays host-wide.

reason: Kept as a composition rule: a contributor component is mounted in the presets whose tools use its message, and a contributor mounted in a preset serves only that preset's agents. The clock ships in presets that carry the schedule tools and not in the minimal one.

Read in full. Kept: a fixed origin line and no instruction to distrust the payload. Refined: the line says who wrote the prompt (the user, or the assistant in a named session), and the message's source kind is schedule and never user, so authority checks cannot mistake it for a person.
summary: A delivered reminder opens with a fixed line stating it is a scheduled message; the untrusted wording was removed.

reason: Final verdict: keep. One vocabulary for instants, zones and recurrence, with parsers that return a stable reason and callers that own their error text, is the caltime and recur packages; the Duration class is replaced by time.Duration and zone names are no longer rewritten.

Kept: caller-owned independent channels, a request bounded by uncompressed bytes as well as count, one event per record, an oversized record rejected whole with one diagnostic and never truncated, one request in flight. Changed: the byte bound applies to every channel, a record is encoded once, the request deadline really ends the request, and each batch reports its outcome. The record shape for session events is area A06's.

Final verdict after reading the note: the rule is kept and the mechanism replaced. Kept: the user consents per target application before any observation or input, enforced at every dispatch and separate from general tool approval and from operating-system permissions. Replaced: the question is A16's policy listener asking through the interaction registry with an application scope, the grant is A17's session grant, and nothing is saved across sessions (DH-ADR-16). The system-permission buttons and launch continuation are not built.

The skill structure is kept: a short router plus three authoring skills that the model loads by name, so ordinary edits do not pay for rendering guidance. The note's shell-execution and mounting parts were already superseded upstream by the Office tools and the cross-deployment note; in Go the skills name area A16's tools.

Kept: a web tool is offered per step only while the selected provider has a credential for that step's route, with no network call. Go needs no separate synchronous availability method, and a credential the service rejected counts as not usable until it changes.

Final verdict differs from the first: not ported. The rule guards a slow per-session format migration that writes a new generation. The Go store has no such step: payloads are converted per event type on read and the layout migrates once, when the store is opened, after a backup. A rule with no subject is not carried; if a per-session migration is ever added, its area decides.

The goal stands: a running host follows plugin adds, switches and removals without a restart. The mechanism (publishing a module-resolution generation and expiring Node's package caches) has no Go counterpart; a plugin is an entry, so reconciliation starts or stops the fiber that owns its process.

Final verdict: keep the product behaviour (a new session may be prefilled, an existing draft is kept, replaced or appended to by an explicit rule, and prefilling never sends or runs a command) and replace the mechanism, which is about input-model objects and React mount order. The draft is a host record that the composer fragment is rendered from, so the initial content is in the first response; area C3 designs it.

Kept: all recomposition goes through one exclusive path, and replacing a plugin is a stop followed by a start. Replaced: Node module eviction is gone; a replaced plugin directory takes effect when its entry is restarted, and an entry whose manifest changed refuses to start until it is inspected and granted again.

Kept: translation is for display only and never replaces stored output or enters model input; the provider is explicit and a failure never picks another receiver; only an expanded body starts translation. Changed: enabling the bundle is no longer consent and Bing is no longer preselected. The web endpoints are a registered sender that needs a permit, its own setting and an explicit provider choice, because the text is model output sent to a third party (DH-ADR-9).

Final verdict: change. Heavy integrations stay discoverable without being paid for by everyone, but nothing is installed on demand: the integration code is compiled in and its catalog entry reports whether the operator-installed external runtime is present.

The rules are kept: one fresh text-only request per fragment with no history and no tools, the exact request written to the session before it is sent, and no fallback. The mechanism changes: instead of two built-in vendor routes and one exact model id, the model provider uses a configured route whose default is the session's own logged route, so by default the text returns to the provider that produced it; and the call gets exactly one outcome event with usage.

Kept: requests and results live in the session they belong to, the request is durable before dispatch and the result before display, and a result is reused only for the same text, languages, provider and recipe. Changed: they are declared ignorable event types instead of plugin records, the host reads the source text from the committed event instead of trusting the browser, a fold replaces the log scan, and nothing activates a session to write a record.

Kept: two ordered user-global files, the harness home's and the shared agents root's, de-duplicated by content so the common linked layout renders once. Two changes: de-duplication covers the whole chain, and an unreadable file keeps its own last-good state instead of sharing its group's fate.

The note keeps npm package names and config row ids stable when packages move into the experimental directory, so that installed Web and Desktop profiles keep working. Go has no npm names and is not required to load upstream profiles (DH-ADR-2). The lesson is kept as a rule: ids in config and names in the log carry no maturity marker, so promoting a feature renames nothing a user or a session refers to.

The shell's own settings file existed because the shell had to work before the host started. With one process the split collapses: the update channel is ordinary host configuration and a flag of dsh update (DH-ADR-ELECTRONUPDATER-3), and the test-authentication switch disappears with the mandatory-update service. The note's rule is kept where it still bites: a function that must work without a composed tree (dsh update, the fatal diagnostic) reads flags or one file directly and never component configuration.

Final verdict: change. The invariant is kept for the one long-lived child this area owns: a workflow run never outlives the policy it was launched under (a narrowing sandbox/mode change or write-root removal cancels it), and approval of the hosting call covers the spawn only. The retained-environment mechanics (one policy per owner, a fresh environment for an escalated program) are dropped with the retained interpreter, and the workflow tool offers no escalation.

Final verdict: keep the behaviour (a recognised command is one atomic unit at the start of the draft, deleting it releases the claim and undo restores it) because the note records that styled text looped inside the editor library. The node model belongs to the composer island, which area C3 designs; the host parses the command from the canonical text either way.

Final verdict after reading the note; the first verdict (ported) is overruled by the owner. The note elects one signed helper per user by file locks and launches it through the system launcher so that it holds its own privacy permissions. No helper exists in the Go design. The operating-system fact the note records, that permissions and capture identity follow the launched application, is why the external driver has its own daemon, which this spec classes as a shared resource the harness never owns.

Final verdict: replace the mechanism, keep the reuse. Four image slots filled by one gallery factory become one gallery partial called by the views of user messages, assistant output, tool results and trajectory rows. Replacement of the gallery by a client plugin is not offered, because there is no client plugin runtime.

Final verdict differs from the first: the connect endpoint is not ported. It gives scripted callers their own peer on the browser API; in Go a program drives the harness through the SDK protocol or ACP on stdio and UI routes serve browsers only. The security rule is kept in another form: a caller that holds no event stream is never an answerer of approvals, and area A17 registers answerers per channel.

There is no retained program process to clean up; each nested call resolves policy for its agent when it arrives, so it never runs under stale authority. Whether a running sandboxed command is stopped on a mode change belongs to area A09.

Final verdict: replace. The note separates where the reasoning body goes from the default way to draw it, so that a wrapper such as translation can reuse the default. On the host the same split is a declared region plus a shared partial; the slot priorities and factory registration are React mechanics. The reasoning node itself belongs to area C4.

Final verdict: kept as written. A stored value wins over the launch environment and the two .env files for every provider, a save always takes effect, and Describe reports which layer supplied the value; a one-run override uses a separate harness home.

Final verdict differs from the first one, which kept the algorithm. The note's evaluator recognises references again each time sent text is shown and caches queries so that a change of facts refreshes little. The Go design does not recognise twice: mention spans are recorded when a message is sent and area C3's usertext view draws them, with credentials masked; a transcript node of this area prints user text only through that view. With nothing re-evaluated there is no cache, no facts dependency and no UTF-16 offset question.

Final verdict: replace. The exchange rule exists so that a turn started by a notice does not fold the previous turn when folding waits for the next message. The Go design folds a process group once, at its own turn's end, so no later turn can fold it and the rule has nothing left to decide; the plan keeps the row positions input, process, reply and turn-level.

Final verdict: keep as written. A node definition may claim an event so that a generic definition does not also draw it; all matches of an event are evaluated before any is accepted, so the result does not depend on registration order; two claims on one event fail and name both kinds. The shipped use is the same: the reply to a question is drawn by the question-reply node and not also as a plain user message.

Read in full. Kept as written: the headless layer limits the secret store to environment sources and disables the authorization entry, so a job never reads, migrates or changes saved keys and sign-ins, and the other profiles keep the stored-first order. With merge the layer states one field instead of disabling three rows.

Final verdict: keep the model whole (a principal on every peer, no implicit fallback, resources declared per operation, one decision point, roles and bindings, a disposed peer always refused). Go declares resources in the route declaration and refuses to register a route without one, which turns upstream's review rule into a load error.

Typed handles returned by registration are kept. Readers that survive unregistration and the callable-promise compatibility shim are not: the Go cordis port unloads dependents before their provider, and registration needs no asynchronous step.

Final verdict: replace. The single frame clock removes a visible jump between two script-driven fold paths. A fold in the Go UI is one replacement of a process group at a durable event, with the browser's scroll anchoring holding the reading line, so there is no script motion to coordinate; the goal of no jump is checked in a real-browser scenario.
Projection state keeps only system prompts and a running total, and that bound is applied to every meter projection in the Go design.

Final verdict after reading the note: its hover operation is not in A16's catalogue and the helper that implemented it is not built. Its second rule, no ownership of an application across calls, is changed by A16: the note rejects a cross-call reservation because it would block other tasks during model inference, while A16's desktop lease lasts one turn and never makes a caller wait. Tasks that need hover are listed as unsupported.

Final verdict after reading the note: two rules are kept in another form and the rest is dropped. Kept: the user's real pointer is not disturbed by default, which the adapter does by always requesting the driver's background delivery and never foreground; and the host, not the model, converts screenshot pixels to window points, which the adapter does by scaling a point by the size of the image stored for the model, as the note warns that capture dimensions alone miss later resizing. Dropped: the accessibility hover route, the system-pointer approval and the relative 0 to 999 coordinate mode.

Kept: an agent's own name, its creator's and the root's are required runtime context derived from the live tree at each request, so identity survives compaction and is right after an ordinary fork. The control-tool component contributes it; it needs required context entries from area A03.
summary: A subagent's identity is supplied as required runtime context derived from the live tree, not written into its first task message.

reason: Each region keeps its own list of hidden entries and draws its own More menu, and one package supplies the shared menu content (note lines 15-25). The feature stands for the navigation column and the start page: each owner filters its entries by a stored host preference, so the choice survives a reload, which the shipped package does not achieve. Sharing the menu content through three slot registrations is React-specific. The first verdict stands.

The note adds host-owned updates from npm registries and Git. DH-ADR-13 excludes updates: the operator replaces a directory by hand. The first verdict expected a Go version source and rollback; none is designed until a registry is.

Final verdict after reading the note: it decides how the browser Preview boots (from the shipped profile, with lazy chunks fetched on demand and Node's internal module interfaces emulated in the worker).
