Every part of it presupposes a JavaScript host running in a Web Worker. The owner dropped the in-browser runtime, so there is nothing for the decision to apply to; the first verdict is confirmed and now links to the owner's decision.
Kept: a teammate is an ordinary subagent identified by its session id, there is no roster, and every root with its descendants is the team. The team component adds only the board and its policy text.
summary: A team member is an ordinary subagent; there is no separate roster, and the team feature adds only tasks and task policy.

reason: Kept and extended: each chain is guaranteed its own byte budget so a large project chain cannot evict the user's rules, and the bytes one chain does not use are lent to the other, which removes the waste the note accepted. The note's objection to a shared budget (one chain starving the other) does not apply because the floor is guaranteed.

Final verdict: replace. The precomputed batch start keeps a reserved slot stable while React re-renders local steering echoes. There are no local echoes: waiting input, steering included, is drawn by the host from the inbox projection in the host's order, so the order is known when the region is rendered.

Kept: listing and messaging span the whole tree, the sender must be a live member of it, delivery re-checks that, only the target is resumed, and the root owns runtime instances while creators keep the lineage. Go makes the root's ownership structural: activations are fibers under a tree fiber of the root's scope.
summary: Listing and messaging work across the whole subagent tree under one root, with authority from tree membership.

reason: Kept as a field: a definition says whether list rows carry it (Summary), and list reads take only those keys. The type-level exclusion mark is a TypeScript device with no Go counterpart.

Final verdict differs from the first: nothing is redone for the new transport. The decision tunes compression of the multiplexed socket; that socket is gone, the event stream is never compressed (a compressor would delay small frames) and the terminal socket is uncompressed by default. Bandwidth over a tunnel is not addressed and is stated as a limit.

Final verdict: the goal is kept (an image is a file fetched when shown and cached by a content-derived name, not base64 inside script). First-party assets are embedded in the binary, addressed by content hash and referenced relative to the page's base. There is no client plugin bundle, and a plugin process contributes no static assets in this design.

Final verdict after reading the note; the first verdict (ported) is overruled by the owner. The note stores long-term grants and per-conversation decisions in profile storage and uses file locks and revocation generations so that another process cannot use a revoked grant. DH-ADR-16 stores nothing across sessions: a grant lives in the memory of the one process that holds the session, so the cross-process problem the note solves does not arise.

Final verdict: replace. The note moves retained drag files out of a React ancestor into one plugin, because the original must survive its source unmounting and a failure must outlive its panel. A drag in the Go UI carries a reference to a host object, so nothing is retained in the page, and a failure is a host-rendered notice. The measured finding that a browser File does not survive a same-page drop is the reason the reference is used.
The rule that the driver adapts and the log stays truthful is kept: on a model without mid-conversation system support a later system message is sent as a user-role reminder by the driver.

Kept: the team owns task storage, dependencies and compare-and-set commands only; identity, discovery, messaging, interruption and waiting are the ordinary subagent tools; no task notice is written into any inbox.
summary: The team feature owns only tasks; everything else comes from the ordinary subagent tools, and task state lives in the task journal.

reason: New Session reuses the workspace's first blank session so that an unsent draft is not lost, and a request that names a preset skips a blank that lists another preset (note lines 17-22). The rule is kept and moves from the client's navigation code into the host's create route, which checks the blank under its lease; this area's form sends the workspace, the preset and a request id. The first verdict stands.

Final verdict: drop. programFormat and retainsState describe how a JavaScript evaluator accepts syntax and retains memory, and the vm Script evaluator needs an await-lowering transform built on a JavaScript parser. The Go host neither parses nor evaluates script text, so neither setting has a subject. The first verdict (ported as two independent settings) assumed a runtime exists.

Kept: Team mode is a saved choice on the root session, default off, read by the whole tree; turning it off keeps tasks and children; a deployment default is applied once at creation and never at resume. The profile migration the note describes has no Go counterpart.
summary: Team mode is a saved per-session choice on the root, default off, not a switch in the shared profile.

reason: Tree state is kept per pane because the dock mounts only the selected tab's body, hidden trees hold no host watch, and the plugin that mounts the tree decides where a file opens (note lines 15-33). In the Go design the expansion set belongs to the session's side state on the host, so it survives any redraw and is the same in every browser tab; a watch is a stream interest that exists only while the directory is on a page; where a file opens is decided by the side surface's Open call. The first verdict left the placement of the state to this area.

Final verdict after reading the note: keep the model, change the carrier. Kept: typed target families, providers registered by the feature that owns the target, plain presentation fields, capture of the target at the gesture, cancellation on dismissal and withdrawal on unload. Changed: resolution runs on the host, and an action's browser callback becomes a request to a declared route, which is where the note's rule that an action must recheck mutable resources is enforced. Not carried: React slot contributions and the hook injected into every slot scope.

Final verdict: keep and extend. One symbol per glyph and weight drawn with a use element, inheriting text colour and tokens and replaceable by a theme, is plain SVG and CSS. The sprite becomes an embedded file referenced by address, which removes the note's two stated consequences (no icon without the theme plugin or inside a frame) and lets file-type, site and artwork symbols be replaced too. The registration checks on replacement markup are kept.

Read in full. Kept: one schedule store, seven timing kinds evaluated normally, cron and recurrence rules authoritative in their stored text, parsing and arithmetic in the shared time package. Not carried: version 1 read compatibility, because the Go store reads no upstream data.
summary: One schedule storage domain in which cron and recurrence rules are ordinary timing kinds.

reason: Final verdict: keep the separation of snapshot and observation for history, projections and state, and the rules that subscribing forces no read and no read wakes an agent. In Go the snapshots are area A06's query and projection reads, the observations are the store's Follow and projection.Changed, and the hub composes them for a page.

Final verdict: client registrations that follow access have no counterpart, because the host decides per request what to render. What must be designed instead is designed: an access change raises access.Changed and the hub re-sends baselines or ends streams, so an open page loses what was revoked.

The official route still follows the listing only on the official origin, but the rule that a customised catalogue stops following it is replaced by a keyed overlay, which removes the comparison with the built-in list and the four limitations it causes.

Kept: a user prompt or interrupt names only the child session, that session is the access resource, and access to a parent does not imply access to a child. Extended: the host resumes the root first when it is not resident, so the note's requirement of an already live root is no longer an error path.
summary: A user prompt or interruption for a subagent addresses only that child session, which is its access resource.

reason: Kept: the control-tool component owns the guidance about reporting to the delegating agent and emits it as runtime context only when its tool is visible in the step; the manager owns result delivery and promises a notice only for parent delivery.
summary: The messaging tool component owns the reporting guidance and emits it only when its tool is available; the manager owns result delivery.

reason: The rule that copied history is not delegation is kept: Creator and Origin are set only for subagents. The choice to record no source is changed: a fork records ForkSource and ForkThrough in separate fields, which avoids the misclassification that made upstream drop the link and makes a branch tree possible. No behaviour may depend on those fields.

Final verdict differs from the first: changed, not kept. Upstream dropped the session-membership check because proving it meant scanning history. Area A07 keeps a reference row per session and object, so the check is one indexed lookup, and an attachment is served only when the session in the URL references it. The store-wide read of any image by any authorised caller is therefore not carried.

Final verdict after reading the note: the helper's identity rule (hash of the bundle identifier, executable path as fallback) is not built. The adapter takes an application's identity from the driver's own listing, a stable identifier where the listing has one and otherwise the process id, so a grant names what third-party software reported. The fallback fails closed, because a grant keyed by a process id ends with that process.

The outcome is kept by other means. Office skills are available in every composition because they are embedded in the binary instead of read from a package directory. The bundled Python environment and its pythonEnvironment switch are not built, since nothing is bundled; the skills name the user's Python or one configured interpreter. Locating the engine and reporting it unavailable belong to area A16 under DH-ADR-20.

Kept as decided: an extra write root is an effect owned by the registering component for one live session, is never restored from history, does not revoke what a running process started with, and an invalid path stops the call.

Kept: the model is told a vendor CLI's absolute path in required runtime context and the harness changes no command environment. The text is rendered for each shell dialect the agent has, and a hint follows a failed bare-name command.

Changed: the pin and the verification of kept files are kept, but a component load no longer downloads anything; an operator runs an explicit install command or supplies a local directory, in line with the owner's rule that the harness downloads no plugin.

Final verdict after reading the note; the first verdict (ported) is overruled by the owner. The note gives source builds of the helper a separate Dev bundle identifier and an optional developer certificate so that macOS grants survive rebuilds. The Go project builds no helper from source, and the signing guide it refers to is contributor workflow that DH-ADR-10 also drops.

Final verdict: change. The order is kept as the stop sequence of a workflow run: revoke the call token first, ask the process to stop, kill the tree after a bounded grace, then settle members and record. The part about reporting whether retained variables survived has no meaning without a retained interpreter and is dropped.

Kept: search and fetch providers are chosen independently from the registered lists, search follows the model route by default, and a selection is never replaced at run time. The route preference moves from constants to a configuration list.

Reversed: the Go host builds the Windows token per start, so each write root carries its own identifier and processes honour extra roots; the journal supplies the grant bookkeeping whose cost made upstream defer this.

Final verdict after reading the note: keep three host tools behind the shared service, declared only after an Office skill loads, with rendered images stored as attachments and a route without image input refused. Changed three things. The engine runs as a confined child process and not in the host, because the Go design starts it under a profile written for it. Outputs are written through the filesystem operation service instead of a private store plus a shell copy, because that service governs every write in Go. Activation is a fold over the log instead of a WeakSet plus the last request header, the option the note rejected for cost.

Kept: the same name rule, the default agent-N, paths from the root with lead for the root, synchronous reservation, and the session id as the only execution identity. The name is now a field of the start record in the root's ledger, and a start that never published frees its name.
summary: Each child gets a short name unique among its creator's children; the session id stays the only identity.

reason: Final verdict: the need is kept (a feature becomes an ancestor of content it does not own). The registry's Wrap kind nests each contribution around the owner's fragment, lowest order outermost, with an optional key. Because nesting happens in one render on the host there is no remounting, and a wrapper that fails renders its inner content, which keeps upstream's containment rule.

Kept: only host operations move the directory, no model tool does, there is one read, and each move is a workspace-root/change event. The sandbox resolver reads that directory as the workspace root, which is why a model-chosen move is not allowed.
This is an npm package naming rule enforced by an upstream repository script. Go packages are identified by import path inside one module, and moving a package is a compiler-checked refactor.
summary: New experimental packages are published as `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>` without an `experimental` prefix, so promoting one to a product group does not rename it; a constraints script keeps the list of legacy prefixed packages shrinking.

reason: Final verdict: the principle is kept (a stylesheet belongs to the document and is not a side effect of loading script; one failing sheet must not block the page). Stylesheets are link elements in the page head, contributed through a region, and an island names its sheet in the island table. Module metadata and renderer-side caches are not carried.

Final verdict after reading the note; the first verdict (ported) is overruled by the owner. The note structures an object API (one shared surface, application and window objects on top) and splits keyboard input into pressKey and single key-down or key-up events. The object API is not built. A16's flat catalogue takes an application and a window on every call and one chord per key call, so a modifier cannot be held across calls; that is listed as a limitation.

Final verdict: keep, simplified. The error base stays in a package with no dependencies (herr) so that any package can return a coded failure without importing the model runtime; the re-export that kept one class identity is unnecessary because errors.As matches by type.

Final verdict: replace. Rendering a fenced block by its language (mathematics, diffs, later diagrams) stays a requirement, but Markdown is rendered on the host, so the dispatch by language belongs to the host renderer of area C4 and not to a keyed client slot that the chat view passes down. This area passes nothing to it.

Final verdict after reading the note: keep its rule, drop its mechanism. The rule (the host decides phase, text, buttons and confirmations; the browser only displays and opens the authorization page) is what every server-rendered page does. The registry, its remote and the shared browser half exist because client plugins cannot share code; area A15's account view is the host-computed display, and the page renders it. The one browser duty left, opening the authorization page, becomes a link the person clicks.

Final verdict: keep. The note shows how a credential implementation registers a verifier and owns its peer, while route owners receive the admitted peer and never a token. Area A18's listener keeps that seam as the listen.Authenticate key with the peer in the request context; pages, fragments, streams and this area's routes all pass it.

Final verdict: keep the separation (a reachable address never establishes identity; authentication is its own service; refusal is 401 and a missing verifier is 503). Area A18 implements it with one cookie scheme and a per-browser peer; the first-accepting order among several providers has one member today. The stream client of this area relies on the 401 answer to show the signed-out state.

The adapter service is folded into the fleet: an account view is a read-only projection of server status, attempts and saved grants, and authorisation operations stay host methods that only a person's action calls.

Final verdict after reading the note; the first verdict (ported) is overruled by the owner. The note serves cua_run_code to other harnesses from a standalone profile so that training data can come from several harnesses, with consent granted unattended or forwarded as an elicitation. With no first-party provider (DH-ADR-19) and no program runtime (DH-ADR-8) the harness has nothing to serve, and a harness that wants desktop control can start the external driver directly. Area A15 keeps the general ability to serve MCP on stdio.

Final verdict after reading the note: bounding a tree read by node count and depth under the provider's own ceiling is kept, as configuration of the adapter (snapshotMaxNodes, snapshotMaxDepth) passed to the driver on every read. The per-read override is not available, because A16's snapshot tool and provider method take no options; the spec asks A16 for such an argument.

Final verdict after reading the note; the first verdict (ported) is overruled by the owner. The note gives agents outside the programmatic preset a cua_run_code tool backed by one retained Node runtime per agent. DH-ADR-8 removes every guest runtime and DH-ADR-19 removes the provider it wrapped. Registration by agent scope, which the note also decides, is how every Go tool component already works.
The inspect function belongs to the JavaScript guest; in Go the script's standard output is the selection of what the model sees, and the attach flag selects images from a nested result.

Final verdict: drop. The scoped evaluator exists so that a later JavaScript program may redeclare a const, let or class name left in a retained V8 scope. That problem cannot occur without a retained JavaScript scope. The first verdict (ported, carried inside a runtime helper for as long as programs stay TypeScript) does not hold: programs do not stay TypeScript.

Final verdict: one owner of the credential choice that hands out ready headers bound to an origin and a revocation signal is kept, inside the account package. The note's auto billing order, which takes the first kind that has a credential, is not carried: the Go authoriser uses the kind of the conversation's route or the configured default and never tries a second kind, so who is billed never changes silently.

Final verdict after reading the note; the first verdict (ported) is overruled by the owner. The note extends cua_run_code to agents that join no preset so that the default configuration has an effect in SDK, headless and ACP hosts. There is no program tool in the Go design, and the problem does not arise: A16's computer tools are an entry that any profile mounts, with one tool form for every agent.
The rule is kept: a size or count bound shortens one result or refuses one nested call and never cancels work that has started, because cancelling hides which actions ran.

Final verdict: the two guarantees are kept and the channel is not. A config change shows in open pages without a reload because views render from current config and a component whose output depends on a live field calls Shell.Touch, which refreshes regions. A secret never reaches the browser because nothing is projected to it: a view shows only what it chooses and the secret type prints a redaction.

Final verdict: retained client objects and facets do not exist. Returning to a session is one page request: a range read of the tail by sequence number plus stored projections, with no agent woken. A host-side cache of rendered fragments is not designed until a budget test shows that this read is too slow.
This is upstream npm release tooling and CI hygiene. A Go release produces binaries and has no packed-install verifier.
summary: The release script that verifies a packed npm install passes its own `--cache` directory to npm and deletes it together with the temporary consumer, so repeated release rehearsals do not fill the shared runner's disk.

reason: Final verdict after reading the note: keep. Authentication is the identity boundary and locality selects nothing, so every admitted browser and every process on the home reads and writes one settings document, arbitrated by a revision. The note's one locality-dependent control, opening the configuration file in a native editor, is not built; the page shows the file's path.

Final verdict: the fix repairs a browser mirror that races the host's list. With one source the cause is gone, provided the host marks a session as not blank when a prompt is accepted (the first inbox insertion), before the turn starts; this is asked of area A06's list summary.

Final verdict: both halves lose their cause. The cache identity token works around proxy access to a service, and the waiting rule orders independent client requests. In Go one handler reads the page at one cut, and the completion routes are declared not to wake a session, so nothing competes for a cold read.

The rule is kept as requirement DH-LIB-ZOD-R13 of the schema specification: an optional argument that does not affect the requested operation is accepted, null decodes as absent, and every value that is used is still validated; test DH-T-ZOD-11 proves it. The first tool that applies it is str_replace_editor, whose null placeholders are treated as omitted (DH-D-FS-8). Which empty strings mean absent in grep, subagent and update_goal is each tool owner's declaration and is requested of areas A08, A12 and A13.

Final verdict: keep, narrowed. The two-chunk prompt delivery comes from the Windows console layer, so the setting is kept with default zero. It now matters only for raw sends, because a bracketed command completes on its end line without waiting for the prompt.

Final verdict: change. The note bundles a console host because older system hosts repaint the prompt in another byte form and readiness compared bytes. The Go design compares the emulated screen, where both forms are equal, and uses the system ConPTY; a different host is operator configuration.

Final verdict: keep. A reused blank session runs the preset the request asks for, or the default, never the one its log recorded, and a candidate that fails a check is left unchanged; the checks run under the lease.

Read in full. Kept: job/registered and job/settled facts with owner, kind, label, tool call and a UUID-based id; producerReported; a failed append never blocks cleanup. Extended: settlement is appended before the owner's final flush, and a resumed session closes jobs the host lost with cause host-exit instead of leaving them incomplete.
summary: Owned jobs append registered and settled facts to the session log; a failed journal append never blocks cleanup.

reason: Final verdict: cooperative time slicing exists only because Node runs host work on one thread. Kept as ordinary Go behaviour, not as a mechanism: the list is cancelled through the request context and never returns a partial page.

Final verdict: keep. A launch acknowledgement says nothing about the background job, so the card must not show a state dot, an exit code or an empty-output line after it. The Go terminal partial takes the same two facts, Background and Running, and draws the same three cases; area C4 supplies them from the tool call. No job state is derived, as the note decides.

The rule is kept and generalised: no per-process value may enter the system prompt, and changing facts are delivered as context, so a new port or checkout cannot change a session's prompt. The package that applied it to two development-only values, and its projection for earlier-format sessions, are not built.

Kept: the sentence that tells the model to end its turn instead of sleeping stays in the delegation guidance unchanged. Go also makes it true below the root, where upstream releases a child that follows it before its own children report: a creator that is owed results stays resident and is woken by the notice.
summary: The delegation guidance keeps the sentence telling the model to end its turn when only waiting for subagent results remains.

reason: Kept in the driver's admission step: at a series start the prompt node is rewritten only when its effective text must move, which preserves the provider's cached prefix.
summary: At the start of a new request series the first system message is rewritten only when the effective prompt text must move.

reason: Kept: a tool instance registers once in the composition that owns it and agents on that preset inherit it. Changed in one point: the note accepts that an unknown preset id is found only when selected; Go checks preset ids when layers are composed and still resolves the id again at delegation.
summary: Each delegation tool instance registers once in the composition that owns it; agents sharing a preset revision inherit it.

reason: Kept: a malformed charset list is decoded strictly as UTF-8 only when it names UTF-8, and invalid bytes are rejected, not guessed. The byte-order mark and HTML meta declaration the note deferred are now read through the x/net charset package.

The read guidance sentence is carried word for word and pinned by a golden test. The note rests on an observed session that read line ranges with sed 60 times; its own benchmark measured the sentence as neutral.

Final verdict after reading the note: keep. Checkout inspection and every worktree command run through the session's subprocess provider under its resolved sandbox mode, a refusal is never retried with less confinement, and command-local configuration disables hooks, the filesystem monitor, lazy fetch and clean and process filters. The first verdict stands; added in Go is a Git version floor, because the note records that Git older than 2.31 ignores the filter overrides.

The rule is kept: a failed management operation always shows its diagnostic, and what the caller sees agrees with the log. It is met differently: there is no output stream that a diagnostic could be missing from, because every operation returns its problems and issues in its result.
This is pnpm deployment of the Node runtime that upstream embeds in its Python SDK. A Go host is one binary whose dependencies are pinned by `go.sum`, so there is no dependency tree to deploy.
summary: The Python package builder uses pnpm's default deployment, which derives a frozen production lockfile from the workspace lockfile, so the Node runtime bundled into the Python package has exactly the locked dependency versions.

reason: Final verdict after reading the note: its subject is the React changes view of a large diff (memoised file sections, drawing on approach, highlighting in the drawing render). The first verdict of replaced assumed a Go changes view; this area does not build one, so there is nothing for the measures to apply to. The note's finding about document-wide CSS :has() rules is general advice for the design-system area, not a decision of this one.

Final verdict: the goal stands and the mechanism goes. Upstream holds a session scope alive so that browser-held files survive a switch, and tells the user after a reload that they were discarded. In the Go design a file is stored on the host when it is added and the host-stored draft holds its reference, so a switch, a reload and another tab keep it; nothing has to be held alive in the browser. Area C3 designs the draft record.

The presentation mode with a guest runtime is overruled by DH-ADR-8; what survives is that nested calls pass the full pipeline, are scheduled under the same parallel and exclusive rule and are logged before the outer result.

Final verdict after reading the note: the closed four-outcome vocabulary, fail closed with no answerer, the never policy inside the service and the audit pair are kept, but the waterfall of answerer listeners is replaced by one registry with a binding per agent, because the note itself says sibling order is not deterministic and tells deployments to compose one terminal answerer.
Kept: opt-in per call, fail to exclusive, bounded pool, results committed in model order. Extended with optional read and write resource keys, which the note's tagged mode was kept to allow.
summary: Sibling tool calls may run in parallel when each tool's classifier says so; anything else is exclusive.

reason: The depth policy is kept and widened: an absolute cap checked at each start with the tool still visible, now applied by the manager for every provider, so the provider capability and the value provider-managed disappear. The persona and tool-filter half of the note exists only to restore children written by earlier upstream releases, which the Go store does not read (DH-ADR-2).
summary: maxDepth is an absolute cap on delegation depth; persona and tool-filter overrides are restored only for historical children.

reason: Final verdict: keep and extend. Owner-scoped persistent terminal sessions are kept with the same ownership and send rules; reading goes through the emulated screen, which lifts the line-only limit, and the six terminal tools are specified by the experimental area that owns their package.

Read in full. Kept: three exclusive tools, compare-and-set on id and revision, execution-time authority (human turn on a root agent; the exact goal round for complete and blocked), the blocked threshold, the wrap-up instruction, and resume of a paused goal reserved for the user.
summary: get_goal, create_goal and update_goal with compare-and-set updates and execution-time authority checks.

reason: Kept: a Go tool returns one typed canonical value; the tool endpoint returns it to a script as JSON and reports a failed tool as a distinct outcome that names the tool. The generated TypeScript declaration is not built.

summary: A runbook for moving required CI jobs from the hosted runner pools to an in-house pool by setting a repository variable, per platform, without a merge.

Upstream's bar (net deletion, health, fit) is a useful checklist for those specifications.
summary: Replacing hand-written infrastructure with a well-maintained external package is a legitimate simplification when it truly shrinks what the project owns, the package is healthy, and it fits the contract at the boundary. Settled seams are not reopened by this policy.

summary: The product packages, the vendored cordis packages and the native packages are published to npm as three independent version sequences with separate workflows and tags.

reason: Upstream writing and naming policy enforced by a repository script. The Go documents follow their own plain-English rule to name the exact concept.

summary: The Windows build of the Python SDK runtime always runs on GitHub-hosted Windows runners and no longer follows the failover switch to the in-house pool.

reason: CI practice: runner routing for the upstream GitHub workflows.
summary: A third-party runner provider can be selected as a CI failover target by a repository variable, never as the default.

reason: The note notarises an update archive and a disk image in parallel from two isolated copies of one application bundle. The lesson that still applies to any release pipeline is kept: a step that mutates an artifact works on its own copy, and every lane settles before cleanup.

The goal stands for any durable format: a change to what is written to disk must not land unnoticed. The mechanism is tied to the TypeScript compiler's type model. Inference: the Go design can reach it with a committed schema snapshot generated from the Go event types and compared in a test; the session area decides.
summary: The types of all persisted session events are normalized into one model with a digest per root type. A change to any nested type changes the digest, and the change must be acknowledged in a committed persistence-change record before it can merge.

reason: The rule stands: an experimental capability must not be part of the default product by accident. Upstream follows npm dependency edges and configuration files; with compiled-in components (DH-ADR-4) the Go check is that the default configuration enables no experimental component and that the default build does not import one.
summary: A check proves that nothing in the default product depends on, imports, or loads by configuration any experimental package; the bundles the launcher names as optional are the one declared exception.

reason: Kept as written: the command reference is generated from the real command tree and from each shipped profile's app, and a test fails when the committed file is stale. In Go it is the commands catalog (dsh catalog commands) rendered from the same Spec values the parser uses, so no help text is captured from a child process and no bilingual pairing is needed.

Final verdict: change. Shipped but switched off becomes a compiled-in component that no shipped layer mounts and that a layer edit can enable; the npm runtime-dependency rules and their isolation gate have no subject.

Recording reader promises next to the persisted field is worth keeping for the Go session format, but the mechanism here is an extractor over TypeScript declarations and comment annotations. Inference: Go struct tags or a hand-written schema file can carry the same promises; the session area decides the form.
summary: The persistence schema inventory records, beside each affected property, the compatibility promise a reader makes for it (for example, that unknown kinds are preserved), so a reviewer can tell a declared promise from an assumption. Promises are declared in source annotations and must be established and tested by the runtime owner first.

reason: Upstream build process: a cache that avoids re-signing thousands of unchanged bundled runtime files (Python, LibreOffice) with the hardware token on every desktop build. The Go release signs two executables on Windows and bundles no runtime, so there is nothing to cache.

The failure analysis holds unchanged for dsh.exe: a combined sign-and-timestamp command reports a timestamp-server error as a signing failure, and retrying it uses the private key a second time. The rule is kept as requirement DH-LIB-ELECTRONBUILDER-R6 under DH-ADR-ELECTRONBUILDER-2: a private-key operation is never retried automatically, and a timestamp request is retried at most three times. Whether the release tool's signing hook can run the two phases separately was not verified and is left to the toolchain.
TypeScript tooling: the rule is about a TypeScript type-assertion form that has no Go counterpart.
summary: New type assertions through `unknown` are forbidden in first-party code; existing ones are held in a baseline that may only shrink.

reason: TypeScript tooling: a syntax checker for JavaScript `catch` clauses. Go has no exceptions; the matching Go habit (never discard an error without a stated reason) is a lint setting, not a design decision.
summary: An empty `catch` clause must name the error, say why discarding it is safe, and wrap a single statement; a checker with a shrinking baseline enforces the form.

reason: npm tooling: it measures npm's dependency resolution of the published packages.
summary: The check that installs two releases side by side with npm decides pass or fail by a work budget computed from the dependency graph, not by a wall-clock timeout that depends on the runner.

reason: TypeScript and CI tooling: scheduling of `tsc` programs in upstream's workflows.
summary: Pull-request jobs that only need compiled artifacts build them without re-running the repository-wide TypeScript checks for tests and scripts, which the required build jobs still run.

reason: The goal, no dormant component that ships without a stated role, stands, and Go's compiler does not catch a component that is registered but never configured. Inference: the Go check compares the registry of compiled-in components (DH-ADR-4) with the shipped configurations, instead of walking npm packages.
summary: Every non-experimental package must either be used by a shipped profile, a runtime import or an optional capability, or carry an explicit classification (optional integration, SDK, build tool, test tool and so on) that records its role. A check fails on a package that is neither.

reason: npm tooling: the content of published npm tarballs. A Go module is published as source by construction.
summary: Every published npm package includes its TypeScript source, source maps and declaration maps, and bundles are compressed without renaming identifiers, so a plugin author can read the implementation and a stack trace names the original code.

reason: Read in full. The criterion that a version changes only when existing readers would misread the new data is adopted per event type: it decides whether a type's payload version rises, and the note beside the inventory records the reasoning.
TypeScript tooling: scheduling of `tsc` and the bundler. `go build` and `go vet` have no such split to manage.
summary: The build is split into a command that produces artifacts and a command that only type-checks the aggregate test and script programs; the full build runs both concurrently.

reason: TypeScript and npm tooling: all eight items concern `tsc`, pnpm symlinks or upstream's code generator.
summary: Eight changes that make a cold build faster without changing any output byte or diagnostic, such as declaring React type packages only at the root and making the remote-method generator parse package configuration lazily.

reason: Upstream development process: hook and check scheduling for its TypeScript toolchain.
summary: Eight changes that shorten local Git hooks, checks and test runs, such as generating declarations without bundling and capping the default number of local workers.

reason: npm tooling: `dependencies`, `devDependencies` and `peerDependencies` placement.
summary: Experimental packages follow the same rules as release packages for which npm dependency section a dependency belongs in; the group-wide exemption is removed.

reason: JavaScript tooling: module evaluation order is a JavaScript concern. A Go program always has an explicit `main`, so the checked rule has nothing to check; the readiness and exit-code conventions of each child process are restated by the area that owns that process.

summary: wait_agent ends only when a message arrives in its caller's own inbox, or on timeout or cancellation.

reason: DH-ADR-TOOLCHAIN-14 keeps the gate: opening a session of more than 100,000 events is a budget test that runs the built binary in a fresh process and fails over a reviewed constant (its workload table names this note). The goal, that test update material can never be offered to real clients or touch real user data, is met by a simpler mechanism: a test release is signed with a test update key, and a real binary trusts only the production key compiled into it (DH-ADR-ELECTRONUPDATER-1); scenarios use a private feed and a temporary harness home. A repair of two test cases in upstream's own suite, which exists only as part of the upstream build and test process. Its lesson, that a test waits on the state it asserts and not on the clock, is the virtual-time rule of the Go toolchain decisions.

A repair of two upstream test files after a CI host leaked Git command-line configuration into Git child processes, part of the upstream test process. The Go plugin manager starts no Git process at all.

Its lesson is general and is written into the browser lane's rules (DH-ADR-WEBAPP-6): an assertion must observe a change the action caused, never a state that was already true before it.

Its inventory was used as a checklist of UI behaviour that depends on host config (reconnect timing, the stop sequence, preview policy, notifications): each is rendered by the host from current config.

The first verdict kept the deferral. Lesson kept: approval for one version is never turned into installing another, so the command names the exact version before it asks.

DH-ADR-4 rules out loading code into the host, and a plugin process cannot intercept host events, so the Go design builds no such bridge and nothing in it depends on one.

The note itself recommends building nothing now, because the other project's plugin interface is unpublished and unstable, and describes six levels to revisit later. Go also builds nothing: every level above zero runs a JavaScript composition runtime in or beside the host, which DH-ADR-4 would make a separate process, and no Go deliverable depends on it.

Read in full. The proposal is not built upstream and is not designed here: source providers, the trigger layer and run records are deferred. This overrules the first verdict of ported.
summary: Proposal: automation tasks with pluggable sources, a model-free trigger layer and event content quoted as data.

A browser without scroll anchoring is recorded by the scenario.

Final verdict: confirmed. The note assigns history prefetch to client classes that do not exist when the host renders HTML. What a user sees is kept by the history route: turn-aligned older pages fetched on demand.

summary: Proposal: generate a checked-in public API report per package so that every change to an exported type shows up as a diff a reviewer must see.

summary: Proposal: mark individual APIs as stable in source, version each capability seam on its own, generate one API report per release, and let CI fail when a stable entry changes incompatibly without a deprecation period and a major seam version.

reason: Final verdict after reading the proposal: adopt it. The Go office queue has general resource limits only and no priority field, promotion, demotion, eviction of speculative work or background concurrency counter, because no caller submits background work. Priorities can be added when a real prewarming consumer defines what it needs.

Adopted. The proposal keeps serialized live configuration refresh, readiness coordination and disposal drainage and removes module replacement with its Node-loader coupling. That is the Go design: the layer source reloads configuration, and a code change is a new binary or a restart of one plugin entry.

Adopted: instruction files are found and read only through the filesystem seam, which is a required injection, so local, sandboxed and remote workspaces behave alike and there is one set of error and cancellation paths. Unlike upstream, a missing filesystem provider is a load error, not a silent no-op.
Adopted by omission: the Go stream record has the first-token reader that statistics and the trajectory view need and none of the five unused visibility queries.

The proposal's premise is false at the pinned commit: the SDK server sends approval/request and user-question/ask as requests (packages/sdk/server/src/server.ts:138, packages/sdk/server/src/user-questions.ts:48), so a one-directional client would lose approvals. Its intent is met another way: the generic next_request, respond, respond_error and notify API is removed in favour of typed handlers, and a frame with an id and a method can never complete a pending call.

Adopted by construction. The Go boot package has one way to locate configuration (the home and the profile name) and one environment loader (the layered launch environment); the older path resolver with its basename swap and the single-file loader are not built.
Adopted: the Go prompt registry emits no change event, because the prompt is rebuilt each step and an advertised event is a promise with ordering rules and tests to maintain.

Final verdict: not adopted. The proposal removes descriptions and list() because nothing reads them. The Go design generates catalogs from running registries, which gives the list a reader, so it keeps the descriptions and completes the list instead.

Adopted: the Go Query interface offers observations, batch titles, surface pages, event windows, traces, lineage, listing and search, and has no method that returns a whole log or a single-title convenience read.

Final verdict confirmed after reading the note: it removes one array copy and one deep-freeze pass in the JavaScript reviewer. Go has no freeze step, and the Go reviewer request is built by a pure function over the committed log, so there is no intermediate snapshot to copy or borrow.
Adopted: a policy crosses the wire as one typed message that the helper decodes once and passes on as a Go value.
Adopted: the world that owns the files resolves each root's real path once per start in the one root-derivation function, while extra roots are still re-checked on every start.
Adopted for this area: no test sleeps (virtual time), a replay helper runs after every driver test, and the inbox and driver tests run under the race detector with repetition.
summary: Proposal: tests wait for events instead of sleeping, every loop test's log is replayed, and a stress job repeats the loop tests.

reason: The upstream rejection is reversed, because Go has no declaration merging and a registry is the only way to extend the vocabulary. Upstream's objection that reads would depend on composition is met by declaring every compiled-in type statically and sealing the registry at boot.

Read in full. Upstream's rejection is kept: the storage contract stays in its own Go package, because the session, the SQLite store and the in-memory test store all import it and a consumer must not import a provider. The first verdict left the placement open; this settles it.

Read in full. Upstream's rejection is kept: an interrupted final turn is preserved and closed with an error result per unanswered call, a missing step end and a turn end marked interrupted, appended under the new lease epoch.

summary: Rejected proposal: more than thirty swaps of hand-written code for npm packages or Node built-ins. Each was rejected with evidence, and each entry names what the hand-written code does that the package cannot, such as a size bound on incoming messages, start-time identity for process trees, or wire faults in the mock model server.

reason: The Go module github.com/coder/acp-go-sdk v0.20.0 gives ACP framing and message types in both roles the harness needs (agent side for the ACP front end, client side for the ACP subagent provider and tests); it is pre-1.0, so only one harness package may import it.

It exists only because of npm: the Claude Agent SDK names it as a peer dependency, so the consuming package must declare it, and no upstream source file imports it. Go modules have no peer dependencies.

Its only caller prints a source excerpt when a hot-reload compile fails, and hot reload of code is dropped. The idea is kept as one small plain-text function used for rejected config layers and for a malformed argument document given to the dsh tool command (there is no embedded interpreter, so the harness reports no syntax errors in scripts).

The owner keeps the OAR runtime bridge. Upstream embeds a patched copy of the JavaScript library in its provider; the Go provider instead runs the OAR the operator installed as a host-owned child process and talks to it over a line-delimited JSON protocol, so all seven runtime ids keep a path, nothing of OAR is linked or patched, and the operator must install Node 24 or later, the OAR package and each native agent. It is declared only by the upstream website package, with an exact version and no import in website source, to pin a dependency of Mermaid for the site's npm bundler; it exists only because of npm resolution and the JavaScript bundler, and the Go site has neither: it vendors Mermaid's prebuilt browser file, which already contains its dependencies.

Stagehand's driver half (navigate, tabs, screenshot) is provided by a compiled-in, Node-free CDP provider built on chromedp; its AI half (act, observe, extract), which calls a second model outside the session log, usage accounting and cancellation, is not kept and is replaced by a page description plus plain input actions used by the session's own model.

The kit is a Node API that loads a LibreOffice engine into the host process. The Go design keeps the four operations (PDF, format conversion, recalculation, page images) behind an office engine seam and runs the engine as a located child process: by the owner's decision of 2026-11-18 it is the LibreOffice the operator installed, run headless, so the office tools work only where LibreOffice is installed.

The multi-provider client library is replaced by harness-owned drivers for the four provider wire protocols on net/http, with the model catalogue kept as harness data, because every piece of debt the library carries comes from it standing between the harness and the wire.

No upstream source imports it; it is declared only because the OAR library embedded in subagent-oar depends on it for an in-process Pi runtime that upstream does not test. The Go host links no coding agent as a library; an outside agent is a separate process.

It downloads the Electron runtime that is packaged into the application; the Go release is one executable per target in an archive, carries no engine and has no runtime prerequisite, because the user interface runs in the user's own browser.
Submission to Apple and waiting are done by GoReleaser's notarize step for the dsh binary; there is no bundle or disk image to staple, because no desktop application is built.

Upstream parses each config pattern as a Unicode and a non-Unicode JavaScript expression to decide whether the exported JSON Schema may carry it. The exporter and that comparison are dropped by the schema design; the guarantee that an exported pattern means the same to its reader is kept with Go's own regexp parser and a small portable-subset check.

The package is the data model and canvas drawing code of a React spreadsheet editor that upstream uses read-only. The Go interface has no React runtime and renders the spreadsheet preview as an HTML table from the host, so no grid model or canvas code is needed.

The package is the React Workbook component and its style sheet. A server-rendered table with sticky headings, native scrolling and tab requests replaces it; keeping it would need React and a bundler inside an island, against DH-ADR-3.

The plugin adds GitHub-flavoured tables and strikethrough to turndown. The chosen Go module provides both as its table and strikethrough plugins; the upstream replacement rules that ignore colspan become a pass that deletes span attributes before the table plugin runs.

It exists only to write a declaration source map for a TypeScript declaration file generated by the upstream build (typert.remote-client.d.ts); the Go design generates no declaration files, so there is nothing to map.

Upstream uses the Temporal polyfill only to turn a wall time in a named zone into an instant (earlier instant in an overlap, no instant in a gap), to read local calendar fields and to step dates; Go's time package does all of that except the gap and overlap choice, which a small harness resolver defines, with zone data embedded through time/tzdata.
It exists only so one upstream unit test can run the JavaScript editor under Node without a DOM; the Go design tests host handlers in Go and tests any browser editing behaviour in a real browser.

Kept: undo and redo with a paste as its own step and a picked reference as one step come from this package, registered on the island's editor; it is vendored unmodified, and its behaviour is shown in a real browser because the Go toolchain has no JavaScript test runner.

Kept: plain-text editing behaviour (typing, deletion, line breaks, clipboard) is this package's, registered on the island's editor as upstream does; it is vendored unmodified and loaded by the composer island.

Kept: its one use, recognising a reference typed as plain text and styling it without making a chip, stays in the island; the host parses the same token rules at submit so a typed token and a chip resolve to the same target.

Kept: its one imported function combines the unregister functions of editor listeners, which the island calls when its element is removed; it is also imported by the other vendored packages, so it ships with them unmodified.

Test-only glue that adapts the TypeScript SDK's web-standard HTTP handler to Node's http module for fixtures; it exists only because of Node. The Go SDK's HTTP server is already a net/http handler, so no adapter has a counterpart.

The stdio MCP server that cua-mcp builds on this package (a tool list computed per request, tool calls, instructions, form elicitation) and the fixture servers in tests are provided by the server half of the same Go SDK module.

A Node reference server used only by mcp-client end-to-end tests. Go tests use fixture servers written with the Go SDK, in process or as a child built from Go source, so the test suite needs no Node; the published server remains a candidate target for the owning area's real-environment scenario.

A Node reference server used only by mcp-client end-to-end tests for real filesystem operations. Go tests use Go fixture servers instead; the published server remains a candidate target for the owning area's real-environment scenario.

It exists only because of JavaScript: the experimental package that runs the host in a browser Web Worker needs synchronous SHA-1, SHA-256 and SHA-512 for its stand-in of node:crypto, and the browser's own hashing interface is asynchronous. Only its signature check is used; HMAC-SHA-256 over the raw body with a constant-time comparison is a few lines on crypto/hmac, crypto/sha256 and encoding/hex.

Upstream imports no code from this package; it only runs the bundled executable as 'app-server --stdio' and speaks JSON-RPC to it. The Go provider does the same with the Codex executable the user installed, over the harness's own NDJSON JSON-RPC codec.
Upstream imports it only for the Attributes type and never creates a tracer, meter or global provider; the Go channel takes attributes as slog.Attr values, so no OpenTelemetry API package is needed.

Its only use is ExportResultCode, which tells a successful export callback from a failed one; in Go the send returns an error value, so the package has no counterpart.

It provides the HTTP exporter shell, the Node HTTP agent and timeout and compression defaults read partly from OTEL_* variables; the own exporter posts through net/http with a harness-supplied client and reads nothing from the environment.

It encodes log records as OTLP JSON and is also called once per record just to measure size; the own exporter encodes each record once with encoding/json and keeps the bytes, which gives exact byte-bounded batching.

Its one function attaches service name, version and the anonymous user id to a channel; the Go channel takes a resource function that is evaluated at the first accepted record, so identity is not read before something is sent.

It provides the logger provider and count-only batch processor that upstream had to wrap with its own byte-bounded processor; one Go channel type with a bounded queue and count-and-byte batching replaces both.

It provides pan and zoom in the upstream site's diagram and image viewer; the documentation website is kept, but that viewer is a theme extension the decision does not carry over in the first version, with the browser's own zoom as the substitute.

Upstream installs this Node MCP server beside the harness and starts it with the harness's own Node program. A Go binary has neither, so the provider becomes a launch recipe for an external program the operator installs, reached through the harness MCP client.

Upstream uses this package only to locate an installed stable Chrome, start it and read its DevTools address (launch.ts:6, :26, :40, :54); it never downloads a browser. The per-language grammar files, loaded on demand in the browser and patched in memory for Go and Perl, are replaced by chroma's embedded lexers, each rule of which has a match time limit.

The types-only agreement that lets cordis accept any schema library is expressed by the existing cordis.Schema Go interface and ConfigError type in the cordis port; no package of shared type definitions is needed.
Formatting rules are replaced by gofmt, which fixes layout instead of reporting it.

Role and text queries over a simulated document are replaced by small query helpers over the parsed HTML tree.
It mounts React components in tests; the Go UI has no React components, so component tests render Go templates and assert on the HTML.

A Vite build plugin that compiles JSX for the React web client (apps/web/vite.config.ts:6, :174; development dependency only). It exists only because of the upstream JavaScript build: the Go design has no React components and no bundle step (DH-ADR-3).
