The package's composer, drafts and recognition of references in sent text are designed by area C3 (areas/ui-chat.md); this area keeps the session page, the composer's place and the regions around it.

The changed-files card, review tab, delivery cards and file links become transcript nodes and routes drawn from the logged workspace/changes and deliverables/presented events and the stored hunks, so they survive a restart. Native opening in a host desktop application is replaced by browser preview and one download route that requires the logged event to name the file.

The in-page dialog that lists, navigates and creates directories of the host machine (packages/client/ui-directory-picker-browse/README.md:12, :32) is kept as a host-rendered dialog over the host's directory browser. The Miller-column React view and client-side hidden filtering are replaced by one listed level per request with the filter applied on the host.

A renderless occupant that opens the operating system's folder chooser on the host's display or through the Electron preload bridge (packages/client/ui-directory-picker-native/README.md:12, :30). There is no desktop application, a chooser on the host's display assumes the person sits there, and the Windows dialog needs native code that a pure-Go binary cannot carry. The server-rendered picker is the only way to choose a directory.

The general docking engine (recursive split tree, invertible operations, replay, history, floating panes, drop zones) is replaced by a small pure planner for one or two side-by-side panes, a resizable divider and a small island that applies the host's layout to stable body cells. Kept from the kit: one settled intent per gesture, the tab strip with manual activation, and content that is not re-created when the layout changes. The loss is stated in the decision.

The shared content of three More menus, with hidden entries, Browse other plugins and Create your plugin (packages/client/ui-entry-customization/README.md:14, :31-33), is kept for the navigation column and the side panel's start page as host-rendered menus over stored hidden lists. Slot registration into three regions is React-specific; the conversation view's own menu belongs to the conversation area.

Download becomes a link to the host's byte routes with a download disposition, and copying an image writes a PNG the host produced to the clipboard, so no browser-side decoding or MIME normalisation is needed. Save as, the Chromium download adapter and reveal-in-folder exist only in upstream's desktop application and are dropped on record.

The transfer service that keeps an original File alive behind an application-local token is not needed: a draggable image carries a reference to its host object, a drop on a composer stages it by reference with no bytes re-uploaded, and a failure is shown in the host-rendered notice region. A few lines of first-party script set the drag data. Native desktop drag-out is dropped with the desktop application.

The goal strip becomes a state region beside the composer, drawn from the goal projection and the activation notice, with forms that carry the goal's id and revision and that can also edit the round limit. The bubble that showed a /goal command becomes the general row for every command/run event.

The trigger pipeline is kept: a slash or an at-sign at a word start opens a grouped menu that the keyboard drives without leaving the composer, Escape changes nothing and a dismissed menu stays closed. Detection, highlight and keys live in the composer island; the candidates and the menu's HTML come from host completion sources registered with complete.Registry, which may be scoped to one session.

The Background jobs section becomes the server-rendered views that area A19's job routes and its two stream interests draw, with chunks tinted by channel and a confirm form in place of the timed two-press stop. The client-only Clear is dropped because the registry bounds settled records.

The script that solves three column widths is replaced by one CSS grid on the page shell's landmarks that states the same rule (the side panel concedes before the centre, which keeps 400 px). The ctx.layout service has no counterpart: navigation is the URL and widths are host preferences. The theme presenter is replaced by the attribute and generated stylesheet of the theme component, and the desktop window-chrome seats are not built because there is no desktop application.

The rating pair and the dialog become a rating partial and a form fragment over area A17's feedback service. Recording a rating sends nothing; the form then offers keep local, export, or send after a preview of exactly what would be sent. Upstream's rule that the conversation log travels with every feedback event is dropped under the owner's opt-in decision. A rating is a log event, so every tab draws it.

The behaviour is kept: one provider-grouped, searchable list behind both the composer control and the /model command, selection by route, model and effort ids, applied at the next request, and a saved selection missing from the catalogue does not block sending. It is one server-rendered picker fragment over area A04's resolved model set, redrawn in every tab when the selection or the catalogue changes.

Open-in menus for a session's directory (packages/client/ui-open-in-app/README.md:12, :36) are kept as menu items that post to the host's open-path route and are drawn only where that route exists, which is for a local owner. The file half (open with an associated application, show file location, association caching, :42-44) is not built, because the host opens workspace directories only; a file is previewed, popped out, downloaded or its path copied.

The composer control and the picker become a host fragment and one form over area A17's preset service, which also states how many session grants a switch revokes. The default for new sessions is an ordinary field of the permission presets card in the General section.

The plan chip, the plan cards and the sidebar plan document become a plan control that is shown in both states, a plan card contributed to the end of the turn, a document route that renders the plan from the logged exit_plan_mode call through the safe-HTML renderer, and a review card with approve, request changes and dismiss.

The Plugins page becomes server-rendered pages over area A21's plugins.Manager, area A22's plugin descriptors and area A18's inventory. Installing by running pnpm, registry probing, install progress, versions and updates are not built; adding a plugin is inspecting a local directory, consenting to its report and granting capabilities.

The Discover tab browses index sources and installs or updates bundles from them. DH-ADR-13 decides that plugins come from local directories with no download, discovery or auto-update, so there is no index to browse; area A21 records the rules a later registry must keep.

The shared catalogue of controls, overlays, icons and output-card frames is kept as one library of typed partials: a Go parameter struct with validation, a named template and a stylesheet per part. Changed: overlays use the native dialog and popover elements, the Markdown, highlighting, diff and terminal renderers move to the host under area C4 and the library specifications, and labels are message keys or data by type instead of required props.

File, folder and session mentions are kept with upstream's rule that the canonical text is the reference's identity. Candidates come from area A14's file and session reference services under the caller's principal, files first; a pick is an atomic chip in the island; the host parses and validates the text at admission and records the confirmed spans, from which the sent-text view draws chips.

Mounting a React tree after the whole client plugin roster has loaded, binding slots to hooks and installing stylesheets per module have no subject in a server-rendered UI. A page is one complete response from typed views, regions are area C1's host-side registry, and stylesheets are static embedded files assembled once into one layered file.

The Automation tasks page, editor, records and session clock marks become server-rendered pages over area A13's schedule service. The browser copy of the recurrence evaluator and the browser's zone list are replaced by a host preview route that validates as the user types and lists the next occurrences with clock-change notes; a save stays compare-and-set.

Masking moves from one React text renderer to the host: a pure Go package recognises upstream's published credential formats and the values the host's secret store released, every host view prints user-written text through it, and the fragment holds only the masked text. The original leaves the host only through an owner-only reveal or copy request. The log and the model request keep what the user sent.

The package adapts the session catalog to React hooks and session-scoped slots and holds the highest-precedence pending interaction per session (packages/client/ui-session/README.md:11-13). The hooks and slots have no counterpart in a server-rendered UI; the one rule it owns, which pending interaction a row shows, is folded into the row status that the reading service composes on the host, and its access hooks are the shell's access helper.

A header toggle and a panel of contributed sections that docks in the transcript gutter or opens as an overlay (packages/client/ui-session-panel/README.md:12, :32-34, :41) are kept as a host-rendered fragment with regions for sections, indicators and environment rows. The resize observer, the dock probe and the Escape handling in script are replaced by the browser's popover attribute and a stylesheet container rule.

A host service that keeps reading state outside the session log and shares it with every browser (packages/client/ui-session-status/README.md:12, :59-61) is kept as reading.Service. Changed: records are stored per principal and session instead of held in memory, completion is read from the list summary folded from the log, and explicit marks carry a revision. The client half that merged three sources into a status table becomes one host function.

The browser mirror of the settings description, the per-entry write queue and the settings slot types are not built. A settings card is an effect of a host component registered with settingspage.Registry, or is generated from the entry's Go config type, and it reads and writes through area A07's settings.Forms with the revision check kept.

The account section, sign-in, sign-out confirmation, profile and balance become a host-rendered panel over area A17's account and authorization services, with sign-in started by a link the person clicks. The desktop introduction, the embedded vendor page and the prefilled third-party questionnaire are not built.

A browser package that exists to give one number a page, with an empty host half so the client loader has a row to serve. In Go the parallel cap is a live field of a config struct and gets a generated card with no UI code.

The Settings panel becomes the server-rendered page /settings with one address per section, and the General section becomes a region that features contribute rows to. The connection indicator and release prompt belong to area C1, version and first run to area A25, and the update-channel row and the native open-file action are dropped with the desktop application.

The Models page becomes a settings section rendered from the model runtime's route list, with a written card per route, a generated fold for every other live field and a separate write-only key form over the credential routes. The first-run credential step and the welcome notice move to area A25's setup page.

The upload switch is no longer a row among General preferences. It is one row of the sharing page, which lists every sender registered with area A18's gate, and it writes area A05's logupload setting.

A companion package for two shell fields. The composed shell entry's own Go config type (bash or PowerShell) is described by settings.Forms and rendered as a generated card, so no package or template is needed.

Depth and capacity are live fields on a generated card. The route selection is one written field whose options come from the model runtime's route list on each render, saved through the same revision-checked form.

The provider menus and provider settings become part of the connections section: menus list area A15's providers with each availability reason and show what automatic selection resolves to, and each provider's settings are a card on its own config entry.

The single reference dialog with grouped commands, subsequence search, inline recording from physical key positions, clearing and restoring is kept. The list is rendered by the host from area C1's command registry; a kit island merges the device's overrides and records a chord through the first-party script's list, set and reset.

The left column (brand, New Session, entry rows with a More menu, the seat for the workspace browser, the collapsed rail and the narrow-screen drawer, packages/client/ui-sidebar/README.md:14, :32, :42) becomes one host-rendered contribution to the shell's navigation region. Seats become regions, the JavaScript wheel splitting is replaced by a single scroller, and the Electron title-bar and macOS traffic-light layouts have no counterpart because there is no desktop window.

The package shows a web page inside a side tab, as a sandboxed iframe on the web and an Electron webview on the desktop (packages/client/ui-sidebar-browser/README.md:12, :63). The owner dropped the embedded browser pane: links open in the user's own browser. The page policy also allows frames of the host's origin only. No screenshot stream of the agent's browser is added in its place.

The fallback file tab with a renderer registry (packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/README.md:12, :37) is kept as the preview kind and preview.Renderers. Text, Markdown, code, images and spreadsheets are rendered by the host; PDF stays a JavaScript island on vendored pdf.js; Word and PowerPoint files go through the office service; HTML is a filtered document in a sandboxed frame. The browser-side spreadsheet grid and parsers and the client conversion cache are not built.

The files page and the workspace tree listed one level at a time, with host-side name search and exclusion rules (packages/client/ui-sidebar-files/README.md:12, :59, :80-84), are kept as the files kind over the workspace-file routes. Tree state moves from a per-pane client store to the session's side state on the host, watches become stream interests, and search preferences move from browser storage to host preferences per workspace root.

The per-session side surface, its tab-type registry with bands and address patterns, and the navigation service (packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/README.md:12, :85-95) are kept as side.Surface: kinds registered as effects, a stored tab list per person and session, selection in the URL. The dock engine, floating panels, the recorded operation sequence and the localStorage layout are not built; a pop-out page replaces floating.

An interactive shell tab drawn by xterm.js over the host's terminal service, with a shell picker, rename, reconnect, take control and agent terminals marked as such (packages/client/ui-sidebar-terminal/README.md:12, :32-40), is kept. The widget becomes a framed island fed by the one WebSocket; the tab list is the host's roster instead of a saved layout, and an agent terminal marks the toggle instead of expanding the panel.

The skill tool row becomes a card registered with area C4's card registry and drawn from the logged call and result only. The preview becomes a fragment over area A14's skill registry through the sanitising renderer, and a skills list with sources and diagnostics is added. Skill candidates in the slash menu are a completion source of area C3; the browser cache is not built.

The need is kept: a feature places UI in a place another feature owns, ownership mistakes fail at load, and removal leaves nothing behind. The mechanism becomes a host-side region registry with kinds One, List, Keyed and Wrap, election by phase and priority, and contributions that are cordis effects. Store seats, derived props and component factories have no counterpart; a reusable assembly is a view with fragment parameters.

The Subagents section, breadcrumb switcher and the at-sign source are redrawn on the host from area A12's tree ledger in one bounded read, with every stop reason shown and owner-only interrupt and dismiss routes. The client catalog cache, per-level discovery and the sidebar resource type are not built.

The three token tiers, the light, dark or system choice, the three font sizes and font lists, the icon sprite and theme registration are kept. Changed: one plain stylesheet in cascade layers with both schemes in one light-dark value, the scheme as an attribute the host renders with no boot script, appearance stored per principal as a host preference, and themes registered by compiled-in components with validation.

The React call tree and the keyed slot tool.call.toolview become a host-rendered card: a frame owned by the conversation area, six closed kinds, and a registry in which the component that owns a tool registers its card by tool name. Cards are still derived from the raw logged call, result and meta, are still pure, and still fall back to the generic card on malformed input.

The React Trajectory tab becomes a server-rendered page of its own, built from the session log by a pure fold on the host: closed steps are fetched by cursor in step-aligned pages, the open step is a state region, and the overview is server-rendered SVG. The package's host half (live raw tool values) becomes the values component with count and byte bounds. Client virtualisation and pointer gestures are not built.

The question card, its timed wait, the answer bubble and the plan-review card become host-rendered views in one interaction region and in the transcript. The host owns the deadline and the question; forms post to the interaction route; every pending question is listed instead of one at a time; unsent answers stay in the tab.

The chat node for a workflow run becomes a transcript node kind registered with area C4's node registry over the four workflow session events, plus a detail fragment that shows limits, sandbox facts, the script, endings and live narration, which upstream left out.

Grouped, tree and flat session lists, sort modes, search, rename, fork, pin, archive with a stop dialog, and workspace add and delete (packages/client/ui-workspace/README.md:14, :40, :48, :58, :68) are kept as host-rendered fragments over the list projection, the workspace ledger and the session and workspace routes. The browser-side catalog, the browser-stored session order, retained recent views and drag-and-drop are not carried; session deletion is added.

The boot kernel builds the module system, activates every client plugin and only then lets the renderer draw; a boot page keeps failures visible. In Go a page is one complete HTTP response rendered in the page shell, readable before any script runs, and a component that failed to load is listed in the notice area instead of a console.
The human /compact command is kept as a host-side command that calls Engine.Now as a maintenance task; it now waits for idle, takes a focus text and a keep count, and is reachable from every carrier.

The contract stays a separate package: the Engine interface, the compaction event types, the SummaryFailed event and the balanced-edge helpers. The log bracket becomes a record because the driver goroutine and the session lease already exclude a second compaction.

The threshold policy and model-written summary are kept as the basic provider; the result commits as one group, the summariser call is logged before it is sent and settled by one event per attempt, and failure is bounded per trigger.

The durable image/offload event and its pure rewrite are kept, bound statically to the payload version as area A01 requires; where a route declares an image budget the offload is planned before the request is sent.

Head, marker and tail pruning of oversized tool results is kept as a model-free reducer that appends a cited replacement; cuts now fall on line boundaries and the marker says how much was removed and where the full text is.

The exclusive provider slot is kept. The Go service adds a provider interface, one fixed tool catalogue in which the application is always an argument, the profile an external MCP server must meet, application grants, refused targets, a desktop lease and a fixed unavailable message; it contains no provider of its own.

The service that holds registered vendor CLIs is kept: it tells the model the absolute path in runtime context and runs account commands one at a time through the host starter, with per-registration limits.
A package per hosted service is replaced by one generic hosted-connector component whose presets are embedded data; the linear preset supplies the URL, the display name and the naming sentence.
The Notion package differs from Linear's in a URL and a name, so it becomes the notion preset of the same generic hosted-connector component.

The pin by repository, commit, size and digest and the verification before publishing are kept, but the download when a plugin loads is replaced by an explicit operator install command or a local directory.

Workspace and user instruction files are kept as a contributor that enters sourced user-role messages; reads go only through the filesystem seam, loaded files are watched, links out of the project root are refused and each chain keeps a guaranteed budget.
The path-candidate service and the @file mention grammar are kept as one component over the workspace's filesystem seam; a mention stays text and content enters only through a logged read.

The host-local provider is folded into the fileref component: the filesystem seam is already the swappable part, so a second seam with one provider would add nothing. The bounded index, ranking and prompt section are kept.

The package exists only for developing upstream itself: its prompt text names the upstream checkout, its pnpm watcher and its client reload, and most of its code keeps earlier-format upstream sessions byte-stable. The general rule it applied (no per-process value in the system prompt) is kept as a rule for every contributor.

Session mentions and bounded, untrusted snapshots are kept as a resolver service and a required contributor; discovery and capture now take the caller's principal, and a truncated capture is saved through the spill store.
The clock reading is kept as a contributor with a fixed-size fold; the sampled instant is recorded in the message so a replay calls no clock, and the component is mounted per preset.

Terminal location is an opt-in user feature for a command-line session inside tmux, not a development aid, so it is kept as an off-by-default contributor at P2 that runs one read-only command through the shell seam.

The Agent contract, the live registry, the factory seat and the agent event vocabulary are kept as Go package internal/agent; the AsyncLocalStorage initiator becomes a serialisable reference carried in context.Context.

The default model stays a small component with live config; it is one global service read with the agent scope key, a preset registers its own default as a scoped registration, and saving goes through config.Service.Apply of the boot area, whose result is returned.

The one shipped driver is kept as component agent.driver: one goroutine per agent runs the turn and step state machine, the durable inbox, creation, resume and teardown, with a turn budget and a bounded final flush added.

The package is a deprecated selector between native schemas and the run_code form. The owner decision removes the run_code form, so one tool form remains and the executor is chosen by composition; nothing is left to select.

Scoped registration is kept as the leaf package session/scope: an opaque key from a table, a tagged registration context on its own cordis fiber, layered registries with nearest-wins shadowing and scope-filtered dispatch. The single parent becomes an ordered list of enclosing scopes and the scope fiber no longer inherits its creator's services.

The append-only session log, its envelope, the surface fold, derived history, fork seeds and crash closers are kept in Go form as the packages session, session/event, session/surface and session/core. Storage is called directly through the contract owned by area A05 instead of being a listener, and the live session holds folds instead of the whole event list.

The registry of prompt sections, variables, runtime contexts and the per-step assembly is kept as the prompt component; the whole-assembly waterfall and the change event are replaced by three closed operations.
The native executor is 35 lines that select the shared batch scheduler for a scope; in Go the scheduler is a fixed part of the tools component because the replaceable executor seam is dropped.

Running model-written TypeScript programs is not built (owner decision DH-ADR-8); its purpose, many tool calls in one model step with every call checked and logged, is served by the tool endpoint that scripts reach through the dsh tool command line.

The scoped tool registry, restrictions, step-time activation and the guarded invocation pipeline are kept as the Go tools component; the in-house schema language is replaced by one Go declaration per tool whose types yield the schema, the validator and the catalogue.

Flows keyed by the record they write, one attempt per key and success only after an observed commit are kept; prompts become interaction registry items addressed to the starting peer and a flow can declare revocation.

References and owner-scoped records, per-operation resolution and a describing call that never returns a value are kept as the secret contract; a redacting value type, leases with a revocation signal and enumeration of references are added.

The managed store over the launch environment and two .env files, with the stored value winning, is kept; the hand-editable YAML file becomes one machine-written file encrypted under a key held in the operating-system keychain, with an owner-only key file as the reported fallback.
The fixed guidance paragraph becomes a prompt section of the deliver/present component, rendered only for a carrier that declares it shows file links.
The present tool and its log-only event are kept. A declaration additionally records a digest and keeps a bounded copy in the blob store.

The per-turn changed-files recorder is kept with its Git snapshots and file-tool captures. The summary moves into the event and the hunks into the blob store, and a manifest covers directories without Git.

The shared office service is kept: bounded admission, job sharing by content digest and generation, a transient cache, classified failures and an unavailable answer when no engine exists. What changes: the engine is an operator-installed LibreOffice run as one confined child process per job instead of an npm kit loaded into the host, priorities are not built, source and result bytes are files instead of memory, queue waiting is bounded, and the private output store is not built.

The three on-demand tools office_render, office_convert and office_recalculate are kept as one tools component separate from the service. Activation is read from a fold over the session log instead of an in-memory mark, and converted or recalculated files are written to a path the model names through the filesystem operation service instead of being left in a private store for a shell copy.

The package turns a fenced action-card block in an answer into a card with state, user actions and a status notice. The Go design does not build this mechanism: the one surviving offer (turning on an optional feature) is a tool call that the guarded pipeline sends to approval, which already guarantees that nothing runs before the user's yes and that the model learns the answer. The cost of dropping is that an offer is no longer deferred below the answer.

The remote consumer that exposed the provider catalogue, preparation and one transcription call is folded into three host routes of the x.speech component: a transcription route that takes an audio/wav body under a byte limit instead of base64 in a remote call, a settings fragment and a selection route. Preparation calls have no counterpart because the harness downloads no model.

The auto permission preset is kept as one default-off component, x/autoreview: a tools.Decide listener that asks the session's own model for a verdict before every tool body. Two things change: the reviewer request and its verdict are committed session events, and unloading the component moves live auto sessions to read-only instead of full access.
The bundle only switches the badge skill on. It follows its feature: with no badge skill there is nothing to switch.

Upstream starts a pinned chrome-devtools-mcp npm package under its own Node and passes the server's tools to the model. The Go design keeps the server only as an optional recipe of one browser MCP adapter that implements A16's browser.Provider behind an unexposed MCP handle; the operator installs Node and the server, usage statistics stay off, and the recipe ships only if it passes the browser conformance suite.

Upstream starts a pinned @playwright/mcp npm package under its own Node and passes the server's tools to the model. The Go design keeps the server only as an optional recipe of one browser MCP adapter that implements A16's browser.Provider behind an unexposed MCP handle; the operator installs Node and the server, and the recipe ships only if it passes the browser conformance suite.

The library's two jobs go to two owners. Per-session browser ownership, ordered calls and exclusive attachment are the browser service of area A16. Mounting an MCP server per agent is an agent-scoped entry of area A15's MCP fleet used by the browser MCP adapter. What remains for this area is the launch package of the cdp provider: finding an installed browser, a private profile, start, stop and a sweep of orphans.

The provider's purpose is AI-assisted act, observe and extract through a second model inside a browser extension, which the owner dropped: the harness's own model drives plain browser actions. Its other part, a host-owned Chromium with a private profile, is rebuilt in the cdp provider, over a pipe instead of a debugging port.

A mod is a JavaScript module whose register function must run inside the host process with the $ interface as live objects (README lines 28 and 99). The Go host loads no code and embeds no interpreter, and the plugin protocol offers no interception. Guarding tools, adding context and reacting to a stop are covered by hooks; tools and commands by a plugin process.

The browser half draws the card frame and hides every action-card block. With no cards there is no frame to draw and no block to hide; an approval is rendered by the interaction region that areas A17 and C4 own.

The package only draws the band a mod renders above the prompt and sends button presses back to mod code. With the mods bridge not built there is nothing to draw, and a plugin process cannot add UI in the Go design.

The React wrapper around the reasoning body and its remote controller become server-rendered fragments: a toolbar and translated paragraphs contributed to the reasoning body, two host routes and a view preference. The host, not the browser, splits the text and names what is translated.
This is the card body of the personalized-page feature: location picker, cost notice, progress, Undo and Restore. It has no subject once the feature itself is not built.

Upstream's largest client package (1.37 MB of source: a host Remote plus a React client) becomes one Go component that renders three fragments on the host: a session-panel section with checkout and change-request cards, a worktree control with its card, and a session-list glyph. Its changes view, review threads and writes, Code review page and lens extension interface are dropped by decision DH-ADR-XFORGE-5; its merge and other host actions by DH-ADR-XFORGE-1.

The card body shows a bundle's title and description with Enable and Not now. In Go the same choice is the approval prompt for one set_enabled call, rendered by the host; the catalogue text reaches the user through the model's answer and the settings page.

Upstream folds the browser's loaded event window into turn and step rows with six client-side definitions. Go registers one row projection, stepStats, in A06's projection registry, so the figures cover the whole log and survive paging, and renders the Statistics page on the host from those rows with totals from A06's stats view and A04's tokenUsage. The same fold is offered to the trajectory view so that both show the same per-step numbers.

The microphone control between the model selector and Send is kept as an unframed browser island contributed to the composer's controls region: it records, shows levels, offers Cancel and Stop, converts to a 16 kHz mono WAV in the browser, posts it and inserts the returned text only into an unchanged draft or on an explicit click. The React plugin, its slot wiring and the model download prompts are not carried.

Starting an operator-installed cua-driver with the argument mcp is kept and is the only route to computer use. What changes: the driver's tools are no longer passed through under mcp__cua-driver-mcp__ names; an adapter maps the eight methods of A16's computer.Provider to an allow-list of driver tools behind an unexposed MCP handle, checks the tool list at start-up and reports unavailable on a mismatch.

Same driver and same operations as the MCP provider with a different transport: an npm native addon loaded into the host process. A Go binary cannot load it and desktop drivers never run inside the host, so it is folded into the external Cua Driver provider.
The bundle becomes the embedded optional bundle reasoning-translation: one disabled group that inserts four entries. Unlike upstream it preselects no provider, so turning it on sends nothing.

On a click the package has a Creator subagent write a JavaScript plugin with a host half and a browser half, validates it and installs it into the profile for every session. The Go host loads no code into its process (DH-ADR-4), has no client plugin runtime (DH-ADR-3) and a plugin process cannot add UI, so there is no artifact the feature could produce.

The shared library exists to serve the two first-party native helpers: retained application and window objects, the cua and cua_run_code tools, saved application grants and a permission page. With no first-party helper and no program runtime nothing uses it. Its rule that consent is asked per application before any operation survives in A16's seam with A17's session grants.

The bundle is a switch that mounts the host platform's native provider and the permission page. Neither exists in the Go design; computer use is enabled by three configuration entries described in the spec.

A Swift helper application with its build, signing, notarisation, permission guide and private-symbol input routes. The owner decided that the Go project ships no native helper; desktop control on macOS comes from the operator-installed driver.

The profile serves cua_run_code, an API reference and a reset to other agent harnesses over MCP from the first-party provider and the program runtime. Both are gone, so there is nothing to serve; another harness can start the external driver itself. The profile would also not fit A16's provider profile, because its one action tool takes a program and its consent arrives by elicitation.

A .NET helper over Windows UI Automation with its build and helperPath set-up. The owner decided that the Go project ships no native helper; desktop control on Windows comes from the operator-installed driver.

The importer of DeepSeek chat website exports is kept as a default-off P2 component, x.chatimport, separate from the deferred upstream-session import of DH-ADR-11. Kept: newest conversations first, one branch per conversation, original times, pinned titles, cold writes without an agent, per-conversation isolation. Changed: the archive is a staged file or a directory read with archive/zip instead of an in-memory buffer, a command-line entry exists beside the upload form, each session is published only after it is complete, re-import is detected, and searches are imported as text and not as fabricated tool calls.

The provider registry and shared polling loop are kept with upstream's cadence, backoff and one-fetch-per-family rule, as component x.forge under forge.Key. The provider interface shrinks from 27 operations to six reads and a description, because the harness never writes to a code host; the last snapshot per change request is now stored.

The bundle is seven configuration rows and an icon. In Go it is an optional bundle file, x.forge, holding one disabled group, beside a separate x.worktree bundle, so the two no longer collide when both are selected; enabling the group is the user's opt-in to contacting the listed hosts.

The GitHub provider keeps upstream's mechanism: it runs the operator-installed gh on the host and holds no token. It is started through the one process starter instead of execa, and is reduced to status reads, head lookup, readiness and address mapping; diff, commit, review, viewed-mark and write operations are not built.

The GitLab provider keeps running the operator-installed glab on the host with the redirecting variables removed and a scratch working directory, including the batch halving when GitLab refuses a query as too complex. It is reduced to the same read-only operations as the GitHub provider.

Bindings of change requests to sessions are kept, with track, dismiss, branch discovery and session watches under bind.Key. The mechanism changes: a listener writes an explicit forge/binding event when a shell call settles, and the fold reads only those events, where upstream re-parses tool text on every fold.

The shared engine is kept in Go form inside x/hooks: the exit-code and JSON outcome decoder, the two matcher modes, the most-restrictive merge and the paired hook/invoked and hook/result events. The runner uses area A09's process starter, runs matched hooks concurrently, and treats a hook that could not answer as a denial at the two gating points.

The Claude Code bridge is no longer a package of its own: it is the claude-code dialect of the one x/hooks component (a file reader, payload shapes and matcher rule), and its seven points are listeners on agent.Created, agent.PreStep, tools.Decide, tools.Shape, agent.OnTurnStopping and the two subagent events.

The Codex bridge becomes the codex dialect of the same x/hooks component: its own file reader, snake_case payloads without a trailing newline and always-regular-expression matchers. It shares every listener with the other dialect, so it gains the subagent points it lacked.

Upstream hosts a Chrome DevTools debugging target in a worker thread: console evaluation and breakpoints in the host, the cordis tree as the Elements panel and unredacted fetch capture as the Network panel. A Go process has no JavaScript engine to attach to and the DevTools frontend is already dropped, so the target, code evaluation and client inspection are not built (DH-ADR-XINSPECT-1). The two harness-specific views become owner-only host pages with command-line twins (the runtime tree and a masked ring of recent HTTP exchanges), and CPU, memory and scheduler inspection comes from Go runtime profiles behind a second switch.

The package is only a profile patch that switches on the inspector with fetch capture, the session inspector and the statistics view. In Go it is the devtools optional bundle, one disabled group of the x.inspect and x.stats entries in area A27's optional list, with profiling as a separately disabled entry inside it; no package of its own remains.

The need (another person watches a session live) is kept and folded into the host's ordinary multi-client surface: one default-off component adds a share-viewer principal, a one-time invitation and a read-only policy, and the session page, event stream and access decision of the route and listener areas do the rest. Not carried over: the relay registration and gateway worker, owner sign-in at the relay, the two driving tiers, forks and their tool ceilings, viewer uploads and the plugin-method picker.

The package holds what the owner bundle and the separately deployed relay must agree on: owner-to-worker frames, gateway frames, the carrier script injected into the relayed page, and the relay's identity contract. The Go design has no relay and no relayed client application: the viewer's browser is a client of the owner's host, so no frame, carrier or identity contract remains. The viewer-state vocabulary shrinks to one refusal page and the ordinary problem page.

The package is a bundle patch that inserts six rows: the card service, the card frame and two features with their card bodies. Nothing in it personalises anything. Go ships the optional bundle feature-guide with one entry, the successor of the plugin-recommendation rows; the other four rows are dropped with cards and personalized pages.

The bundle switches on the plugin-index reader and its Discover tab. DH-ADR-13 decides that plugins come from local directories with no discovery or download, and area A21 builds no index reader, so there is nothing for the bundle to mount.

Upstream gives the model a local catalogue of shipped optional bundles through a skill and enables one from a card click. The source shows no remote service and no dependency on a plugin market (src/skill.ts:11-22). Go keeps the skill and the local catalogue as the feature-guide component and replaces the card click by the approval of a plugin_manager set_enabled call.

The bundle exists to mount the ralph tool beside a workflow engine isolated for it. The Go loop uses no workflow engine, so the bundle reduces to the x.ralph component's default-off optional bundle entry.

Upstream is a React sidebar page that tabulates the session records and the chat engine's node objects already loaded in the browser. The Go host renders a session log page from A06's Query: every event paged over the whole log, grouped by turn and step, filtered by type and surface class, with event detail and a panel of fold states at the cut. The chat-node presentation, object-reference navigation and the click-to-pick mask are not built because the Go UI has no client object graph; a row links to the transcript and trajectory by seq instead.

The bundle exists to give the query tools a private in-memory SQLite index, because upstream's shipped bundles turn search off. In Go the search index is rows in the session store written with each event and is on by default (DH-D-VIEW-6), so nothing of the bundle remains except the switch: the session-recall optional bundle that mounts the x.recall tools.

The package is a second title provider with a different cadence. It is folded into the title seam of area A06 as the provider all-prompts: two prompt texts and an unchanged-title rule, with A06's generator making, logging and settling the call.

The bundle swaps title providers by disabling another bundle's row, which a Go optional bundle may not do because it may only insert. Its job is folded into one config field, title.Config.Provider, with the provider mounted as an ordinary entry.

The package is one fixed skill that tells the model to add a powered-by-dsh badge, with upstream's project address, logo and a remote image address, to documents and to every pull request. A reimplementation does not ship another project's attribution as its own, and a SKILL.md in a user or project skill directory gives the same ability.

The provider registry is kept as the speech contract package and the x.speech component: providers register under an exact id with a processing location, a request resolves exactly one provider, a missing provider or unsupported language fails, and no failure falls back to another provider. Preparation methods are not carried because nothing is downloaded.

Upstream runs SenseVoice through the sherpa-onnx-node binding in a managed Node subprocess and downloads pinned model files. The Go design replaces it with a command provider that runs a recognition program the operator installed on one temporary WAV file under a read-only, no-network policy, with the same bounded queue, deadline and cancellation; the sherpa-onnx prebuilt runtime is the documented example and no runtime or model is downloaded by the harness.

The OAR runtime bridge is kept by owner decision. x/oar registers one Runner per configured instance on area A12's subagent seam and drives the operator-installed OAR as a bridge child the host owns, as the library specification sets out; nothing of OAR is embedded or patched.

The bundle mounts a private terminal registry with the panel backend and the tools. The Go design has one terminal service in every profile (area A09), so the bundle reduces to the x.termtools component's default-off optional bundle entry.

Its backend made agent terminals into sidebar terminals so a person could watch them. In Go a browser already attaches to area A09's one terminal service, so no second backend is built. What remains is the control rule (the first typed input passes control to the person, with no hand-back), specified here, and the two user-terminal read tools, which move into x/termtools and are off by default.

Timeline is kept as a compiled-in, default-off component under internal/x/timeline: five model tools, ten typed durable event types holding whole values, a projection for trees and discussions, replacement of todo_write through A03's Restrict and deny-only guard, owner edits, tree export and import, and timed reports as report rows. Changed: each report call is requested by a flushed event and settled by exactly one attempt event, there is no repair call, reports are paged by day with no seven-day window, and the UI is host-rendered regions instead of a React sidebar.

The ralph tool is kept as x/ralph. The fixed JavaScript workflow script becomes a Go loop that calls the subagent runtime once per round; the human-turn rule and the recursion ban are enforced by a guard, and time and token budgets and one retry of a failed round are added.

The five read-only history tools are kept with their names as a default-off component, x.recall, that translates arguments into A06's Query calls with the calling agent's visibility. The package's own authorisation by cwd string, its failure sanitiser and its exclusive scheduling are not carried over: visibility, bounds, stable cursors and error codes are properties of Query. The fixed guidance section is kept.

The selector tool maps model-visible aliases to provider instances and nothing else. Area A12's delegation tool already accepts operator-declared targets (alias, provider, description), so subagent_oar is a mount of that tool with a target list and no package of its own.

The six terminal tools are kept as x/termtools: thin declarations over area A09's terminal.Service with the calling agent as owner. They gain named keys and full-screen reads, and report who controls each terminal.

The two model tools are kept as component x.worktree.tools, separate from the service so that an agent preset without them pays no prompt tokens. They move a session only through workdir.Service.SetForCall, which the working-directory owner (DH-ADR-VIEW-8) limits to the anchor; in addition a target must lie inside the session's current write roots and exit returns to the directory the session entered from.

The translation service is kept as a seam with a provider registry: a model provider (an auxiliary logged call on a configured route) and the two web endpoints. Requests and results stay in the session, now as declared event types with exactly one outcome per request, a fold as the lookup index, and text read by the host from the committed event.

The bundle is a static patch that adds four rows and selects a default recogniser. In Go a bundle is a named set of entries embedded in the binary; the speech and voice-input components are default-off entries of the experimental bundle and no default provider is selected.

The runtime is kept as x/webhook: it matches a verified delivery against rules and creates an ordinary root session in upstream's order with rollback before the prompt is admitted. Rules become configuration or a host-owned command instead of in-process callbacks, and a delivery record removes duplicate sessions.

The GitHub adapter is kept as x/webhook/github with upstream's check order and status codes: method, content type, bounded body, three headers, secret, signature over the raw bytes, then parsing and 202. The signature check is standard-library code and the route is the only mount of a listener separate from the UI.

The package is the build tool that packs built JavaScript packages into the file-system image the browser worker mounts. With the in-browser runtime dropped there is no image to pack, and a Go binary already links every component, so nothing of the packer has a counterpart.

The package runs the whole JavaScript host inside a browser Web Worker for the no-install Preview, per-pull-request previews and a packaging regression test. The owner dropped the in-browser runtime: a Go host could only do this as a WebAssembly build, a second target with its own storage, sandbox and network answers. No replacement is designed; section 3.4 of the specification records what is given up.

The worktree service is kept as component x.worktree under worktree.Key: create, enter, exit and restore run Git under the session's own policy and move the session through the working-directory service. Added: rollback of a failed attempt, a journal of operations in flight, cleanup on deletion as well as archive, and a retained grant to the common Git directory. Dropped: the Node helper process.

It evaluates a plugin's browser half inside the page and mounts it through the client loader; the Go UI is rendered by the host and has no client plugin runtime, and a plugin contributes no UI in protocol version 1. 83 percent of its source is two generated catalogues of the React slot surface.

The registry of dynamic packages and the node:vm host half become a plugin host component that runs each plugin as a confined, supervised process whose contributions are effects of its fiber; the inspect registry half moves to the inspect component. Nothing is evaluated inside the host.

The read-only inspection tool is kept as harness_inspect over host-only providers that read live registries and schemas derived from Go types; 98.1 percent of the upstream source (879,589 of 896,186 bytes) is a generated catalogue of in-process APIs that a plugin process cannot call, so it is replaced by a provider that serves the plugin protocol itself.

The panel's rows become rows of the server-rendered plugins page built from the plugin descriptor, its approve and decline controls become area A17's consent fragment, and the cards for cordis_define, cordis_run, stop and undefine have no tools left to render; an attach is shown as a transcript notice from its own logged event.

The session remark event, the category list and the /feedback command are folded into the one feedback component together with message ratings; recording no longer prints or creates the anonymous identifier.
Ratings and notes on assistant messages as log-only events with per-item versions are kept; current items come from a registered projection instead of a scan and every event records the actor.
The filesystem contract is kept as a Go contract package: one interface, typed service keys, the error table and three typed events. Each operation takes the unresolved path and the per-call policy.
The local-disk provider is kept: identity, atomic publication, per-target serialisation and guards. It is rebuilt on the fsx helpers and rooted handles, and its version token gains a content digest.

Read-before-edit stays an optional listener with no service of its own. Its state becomes a projection over logged observation events instead of an in-memory map, and it ships disabled as upstream does.

The pure patch parser and text applier become the sub-package textdiff/patch of the shared textdiff package, ported rule for rule from the pinned Codex behaviour, with line-ending handling moved inside.

The fence is no longer a subclass that replaces the provider. Enforcing the per-call policy is part of every provider's contract, and the local provider does it with os.Root handles on the write roots.
The read, write, edit, apply_patch and read_image tools keep their names, arguments, result envelopes and guidance. They become thin front ends over one operation service.
The glob and grep tools are kept, but the child rg process is replaced by the in-process search package reading through the filesystem provider, and the pattern dialect becomes Go RE2.
The single-editor tool is kept as an optional, default-off tool with the same commands and schema, implemented as a front end over the operation service so it cannot skip the fence or the policy.

The /goal command and its grammar are kept as component command.goal. Every operation is also a plain service call, so the server-rendered goal panel, the SDK protocol and the command line reach it without the command registry.

Event-sourced goal state with whole-value goal/change events, a strict fold, compare-and-set mutations and in-memory arming is kept as component goal.service. The state gains optional token and time budgets.

The driver that opens one follow-up turn per round at idle, with a reservation and a pre-step fence, is kept as component goal.rounds. Automatic stops become logged blockers with codes, and budgets plus a bounded retry of transient failures are added.
get_goal, create_goal and update_goal are kept with the same arguments and the same execution-time authority rules (human turn on a root agent, or the exact goal round for terminal reports).

The advisory repeat-call reminder is kept with the same thresholds and texts; its chain becomes a session projection folded from the log instead of an in-memory map, and an optional deny guard is added.
The optional deadline wrapper becomes part of the execute stage of the pipeline, which gives every call a budget and enforces it without a separate component.

The provider exists to keep a credential out of the Electron renderer by passing it over the desktop shell's private channel. The owner removed the desktop application, so there is no shell, no private channel and no second credential path to verify.

The launch token exchanged for a signed, audience-bound, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie is kept, with the durable signing secret. Changed: a token works once and expires, each browser has its own peer and can be signed out, all browsers can be revoked without a restart, and the /connect exchange for API clients is not built because there is no RPC gateway.

The seam is kept as one contract package, dirbrowse, whose only interaction is the server-side browser. The capability union that let a backend be either a native chooser or a browser is gone because only one interaction remains; a remote world may still provide the same interface for its own machine.

The chooser existed to guess at boot whether the operator sits at the host's display and to mount a native or a browse backend accordingly. With one server-side browser there is nothing to choose between, and the guess could not be proven from launch-time signals.

One-level directory listing and single-segment child creation are kept with the same bounds, sorting, link handling and fully-qualified path fence. Added: the Windows hidden attribute, a roots level that lists drives or configured roots, and optional roots enforced through os.Root handles.

A native folder dialog opens on the host machine's display, which a browser user may not be looking at, and the Windows dialog needs a native COM binding that a pure-Go binary cannot carry. The owner's decision on the desktop application already turns native folder dialogs into a host-rendered picker.

Upstream serves a built single-page application from a directory and renders start-up data into its index. The Go host renders pages itself and serves only the files those pages reference, from an embedded file system, with the harness media-type table, nosniff, a build-hash ETag and 404 for every miss.

Opening a workspace directory in an installed editor, Git client, terminal or file manager is kept, with the fixed catalog, verified launchers, argument lists without a shell, a scrubbed environment and the owner-only rule. Tightened: the route exists only in local mode with a display and outside SSH, the path must lie inside a registered workspace, and operator-defined entries come from config. Icon extraction is not built.

The read-only projection of what is composed in the host is kept and still reads the loader on each call. It gains the supplying layer per entry, rows for plugin processes loaded from local directories with their manifests and grants, an explicit availability flag for presets, a change event and a bounded history of phase changes.

Upstream offers one emit call for caller-selected records to a compiled-in collector. The Go design replaces it with two typed reporting channels, analytics and telemetry, whose events come from a closed catalog, which are off until the user turns them on, have no endpoint compiled in, and attach no account or device identity.

The one web listener is kept: one concrete bind address, optional TLS that fails closed, opt-in gzip that never touches the event stream, and a shutdown that ends open streams. Changed: admission is a fixed pipeline inside the listener instead of cordis events, handlers attach as mounts that state each request's class, the route table itself is area A19's and is one such mount, a network bind without TLS is refused unless flagged, and there is no fallback seat or index injection.

One random identifier per harness home is kept, but it is created only at the first use by a sender the user opted in to, stored in a key-value namespace in one transaction, and can be reset for every process at once.
The registry of human commands, global and agent-scoped registration and the logged run and done pair are kept; commands gain typed arguments and one dispatch entry that every carrier can call.
A preset stays a named pair of sandbox mode and approval policy with a derived custom label; the table becomes live configuration and a switch is an owner action that revokes session grants.
The model-facing ask_user_question tool is kept under the same name as one tool declaration with an optional timeout, replacing the two schemas selected by configuration.

The one-shot approval service with closed outcomes, the session policy and the asked and decided audit pair is kept; the answerer waterfall becomes ownership through the interaction registry, the decided record names who answered, and session grants are added.

Blocking and timed questions, late answers as user messages and the derived question projection are kept; delivery moves to the interaction registry, the claim stream becomes a host-owned deadline with a hold, and the approval intent is removed.

The registry contract is kept as package delegate/jobs: job types, owner-fenced calls, the two session records and the jobs projection. Changes: no unowned jobs, kinds are registered as effects, producers push output, and the model read is Peek then Commit.

The in-process registry is kept as component jobs.registry: admission before start, one bounded ring per job, first-wins settlement. Go adds a stop grace that forces settlement, settlement before the owner's final flush, a cap on settled records and closing of jobs lost with the host.

The three model tools, the controller and completion notices are kept as component tool.jobs. Notice delivery becomes one waking send with a refilling wake budget, and the unread output stays in the registry until the notice is claimed.

The registry of extra request body fields becomes the request-contribution service of the shared transport, available to any route and listed per route, with every contribution off until the user opts in.

The message, block, chunk and failure vocabulary, the adapter registry, call preparation, failure normalisation, the assembler and the compact stream record are kept as the contract package llm and the runtime component; the open, plugin-extensible sets become closed Go sets.

The vendor's Messages transport is kept as the shared transport, the Anthropic Messages driver and the vendor provider package; the Files upload path, listing and version gate are kept with a time-based upload cool-down and a stored listing.

The account route keeps its single credential source, per-account listing and sign-out cancellation; cancellation no longer depends on the route component being loaded because the request header records the credential reference.
The API-key route is the first working provider; it follows the official listing through a keyed model overlay instead of comparing the configured list with the built-in one.

The library-backed multi-provider adapter is replaced by three more harness-owned protocol drivers, a keyed-route provider component and an embedded catalogue; its role as the second twin is replaced by a conformance rule.
Retry stays a listener outside the adapter that logs each retry before waiting; it now decides by failure class, has no unlimited mode, and shares one attempt cap per step.
There are no npm plugin packages in Go; the field is replaced by an opt-in installation inventory contribution that reports the build version, enabled entry ids and plugin manifests.
The meter service and its three projections are kept as deterministic folds of the log with no model call; projection state is bounded and estimates are scaled by a per-session calibration factor.
The language-server seam is kept as a contract package with a provider registry keyed by extension and four closed operations, with a route table and a status query added.

The generic stdio provider is kept: one process per provider, world and workspace root, started lazily through the host's starter under a sandbox policy, with overlapping read-only queries and an idle stop.
The lsp tool is kept with the same four operations and output caps; its position arguments change to a character column or a symbol name.
The adapter that mapped manager states to an account section becomes a read-only account view computed by the fleet from configuration and saved grants; the page is rendered by the settings UI area.

The per-server bridge is kept in Go form: the mcp/conn wrapper over the official Go SDK, a child fiber per server that supervises the connection, and a bridge that registers tools under the same mcp__server__tool names with whole-generation swaps.

The live fleet with configured and registered entries, status, restart and probe is the mcp component itself; there is no separate manager above client instances because a child fiber per server gives the same lifetimes.
The scoped provider registry disappears because resource reads are methods of the server handle; the three shared tools are kept as a separate tool component over the fleet service.

Logged per-agent plan state, the guidance section, /plan and the reviewed exit_plan_mode tool are kept as component plan.mode. Go changes soft guidance into an enforced read-only mode, appends the state at once and captures it per step.

The declaration row is kept as the component agent.preset. Its child list becomes a map keyed by child id inside the entry's config, so a layer merges into one child, and a declaration may extend another. The packaged dsh-doc skill directory, located upstream by Node module resolution, becomes an embedded harness-docs skill addressed by name and mounted by the creator preset.

The registry is kept as the component agent.presets with service key agentpreset.Key: eager activation, broken declarations that stay listed, revisions retained by leases, selection only while a session is blank, and the session record. Changed: the realm of a revision is built automatically from declared provides instead of hand-written isolate groups audited for leaks, and every binding is logged with a digest.

Kept as the component agent.persona: it registers a scoped persona prefix and suffix that shadow the global ones for one preset, a complete-prompt mode and suppression of optional runtime context, through the prompt service of area A03. Added: suppression of named contexts. It still refuses to load outside a preset.

The abstract program-runtime seam (ctx.ptcRuntime with resolve, run, release and an environment initializer) is not built. The owner removed the guest runtime, so there is one way to run model-written code, an ordinary sandboxed command, and a seam with no provider has nothing to abstract. Its three consumers are restated separately: run_code by area A03, workflows in this spec, the computer-use program tool by its own area.

The Node child process with four evaluation forms, an RPC control pipe and retained memory is not built. Its purpose, model-written code that runs confined in a child process and calls tools, is given by a different mechanism: an ordinary script started by a hosting tool under the sandbox, calling tools through the dsh tool command line. This area supplies the mode switch and the generated prompt contract; the endpoint is area A03's.

The seam vocabulary (three modes, a policy per call, reported enforcement, fail closed) is kept as the Go contract package; the argv-returning confine call becomes a Launch the one process starter applies, and enforcement is computed instead of returned by the provider.

The per-platform backend chain and its profiles are kept (bubblewrap then Landlock, Seatbelt, Windows token); every backend is probed at start, the C launcher and stderr failure rules are replaced by the launch stage and its status channel.

The resolver keeps upstream's precedence, the sandbox/mode session event, effect-scoped extra roots and the model-visible policy section, and gains the network setting, the scratch directory and a required-enforcement field.

The write-restricted Low-integrity token and the three-edit grant are kept and made from typed golang.org/x/sys calls in the host; the runner process and the PowerShell diagnosis skill are replaced by an in-process token build, a grant journal and owner commands.

Host-owned schedules with seven timing kinds, three targets, latest-only catch-up and bounded history are kept as component schedule.service. Storage becomes two typed tables in the home database, and firing uses a per-occurrence claim plus a deterministic message id so that several processes on one home deliver once.

The four schedule tools stay a per-preset consumer of the host service. Go adds enforced rules: a session sees only its own schedules, a mutation needs a human turn or an approval, and a delegated agent is not shown the tools.

The TypeScript client library is replaced by a public Go client package for Go programs and the harness itself, and by TypeScript declarations and stubs generated from the protocol schema file for a TypeScript consumer; the result interval and tree scoping it computed are now host facts.

The newline-delimited JSON-RPC transport and the named SDK message types are kept as two packages of the standard-library-only module src/sdk: the bounded codec sdk/jsonrpc and sdk/protocol, which adds a method table, an integer protocol version and one error table.

The stdio serving plugin becomes the cordis component wire.sdk: explicit session create, resume, close and cancel, history reads, host-scoped notifications, a run result per claimed turn, and approvals and questions answered through the interaction registry.

The ZIP archive and Markdown transcript are kept as functions that write to any writer, with a manifest and a final status; the routes, the command and the UI controls belong to areas A19, A24 and the UI areas.
The query service is kept as the Query interface: listing, one-cut observation, bounded event windows, traces and lineage, now with a required visibility and no method that returns a whole log.

The separate derived search database with per-search reconciliation is folded into the store-backed query component: search documents are a row projection committed with their events in the session database.
The two read-only listing tools are kept as a separate query-tools component, with keyset cursors, a blank filter, a title state and visibility limited to the caller's workspace by default.

A quote stays ordinary Markdown: Go functions encode selected text as blockquote lines and recognise them at render time; the selection action and display belong to the composer and conversation UI areas (C3, C4).

The three durability checkpoints (before a model attempt, before a top-level tool body, at each step boundary) and the fail-closed rule are kept as checkpoint.Policy, called by the driver and the tool pipeline at the three points, failing closed; with no policy mounted the callers flush directly.

The stage machinery exists only to run a chain of adjacent format migrations over old files. The Go store reads only its own format and evolves each event type by a payload version, so there is no chain to run.
The build-time catalogue of codecs and migration edges exists only to keep formats 0 to 3 readable. No Go package reads an upstream format generation in the store's read path.
A frozen reader of upstream format 0 and its edge to format 1. Formats 0 to 3 are never read by the Go harness; their holders upgrade them with upstream first.
A migration edge that folds stream chunks and renumbers every event of an upstream format 1 file. Formats 0 to 3 are never read by the Go harness, and the Go store never renumbers.
A migration edge that moves the system prompt into events and renumbers an upstream format 2 file. Formats 0 to 3 are never read by the Go harness.
The edge from format 3 to 4 is not built. The package also holds the format 4 codec; the deferred import command specifies its own reader for format 4 files and is not a port of this package.
The bounded incremental upload with an acceptance watermark is kept as a component, but it is off until the user opts in and obeys the one off-switch, which reverses upstream's default.
The service-plus-handle contract is kept as a Go contract package with a conformance suite; readers and writers become two interface types and no listener routes events into storage.

Per-session files with generations, Zstandard frames, torn-tail recovery and exclusive publication are replaced by one SQLite database whose transactions give the same guarantees; the readable one-file-per-session artifact survives as the export.

The package exists at the pinned commit as an optional provider. Its WAL mode, group commit with savepoints, append-only triggers and identity pragmas are carried into the one Go store; its 64-event frames, linked segments and import of JSONL on first open are not.

The registry of pure folds is kept: one driver, typed handles, snapshots at one seq, a change event per committed event. Reference identity as the change test and single-thread consistency are replaced by an explicit changed result and folding under the session append lock.

The separate JSON checkpoint store with timers and identity matching is folded into the projection registry: checkpoint rows live in the session database and commit in the transaction of the events they cover.
The whole-log statistics fold is kept as the stats view, with steps split by outcome and every settled attempt timed from the hot part of its event; it is local state and is never exported.

The capture coordinator, live capture mode, operational records and in-memory hand-off cursor are replaced by a session-upload component whose consent and delivery progress are session events; redaction is an ordered registry with a built-in baseline.

Upload after explicit own feedback is kept as a rule, but it is off by default, needs a confirmed preview per submission, and sends through the harness's own OTLP channel owned by area A18 instead of the OpenTelemetry SDK.
Log-backed latest-wins titles, the deterministic fallback, rename and refresh are kept; Unpin is added and the single-provider registry becomes a registry seam with one active provider chosen by id.
The first-prompt strategy becomes a title.Provider (prompt framing and cadence only) registered by the title-llm component; scheduling and the model call belong to the generator.

The shared execution policy becomes the generator inside the title component: it logs and flushes the request event, builds the request from that event, sends it, and settles it with exactly one attempt event under one acceptance rule.
The turn outline is kept as the turnIndex row projection: one derived row per turn with typed previews, so a change updates one entry instead of pushing the whole outline.
One logged directory per session with Get, Ensure and Set, recovery to the original project, an access coordination key and a required context entry is kept; only host operations move it.

The settings service is kept as forms over the live fields of composed entries, validated against the whole config and written only through config.Service.Apply of the boot area, which owns the one writable layer. The legacy settings.yaml import is not carried because no Go release wrote that file.

The fresh bash -c executor is kept with its budgets and first-cause classification. It is no longer an unconfined variant: the one bash provider asks the sandbox seam for a launch plan on every call, and it resolves bash on Windows as well.

A separate sandboxing executor exists upstream because confinement is chosen by which package is mounted. In Go confinement is a required field of every spawn for an agent, so this package folds into the one bash provider and the confined-launch path of the process package.

The fresh pwsh -Command executor is kept with its resolution order, UTF-8 preamble and budgets. Commands that must begin with param, using or #requires are run from a private script file, and the provider always requests a launch plan.
As with the bash twin, the sandboxing PowerShell executor exists only because confinement was a choice of provider. It folds into the one pwsh provider, which obtains a launch plan for every call.

The shell executor contract is kept (request resolved to an explicit spec, one execution with foreground and background views) and becomes a registry by dialect so bash and pwsh can both be mounted. The text exit-marker parser is replaced by structured result fields.

The managed DSH_ environment registry is kept with declared keys, conflict detection and refusal of undeclared output. Built-in variables become the first contributor so the list is complete, and DSH_NODE_EXECUTABLE becomes DSH_EXECUTABLE because there is no Node runtime.

The one-shot bash tool is kept with the same arguments, job registration and promotion on timeout. Its result gains structured fields for exit code, stop cause, working directory, truncation and sandbox facts, from which the text markers are rendered.

The per-agent persistent bash tool is kept. Commands are delivered by file and bracketed by a nonce instead of being typed into the line editor, the result is read from the emulated screen, and a timed-out shell is interrupted and verified before it is reset.

The one-shot pwsh tool is kept as the PowerShell twin of the bash tool, sharing one tool package and the structured result. The Windows sandbox facts in its description come from what the backend reports instead of a hard-coded gate.

The per-agent persistent PowerShell tool is kept as the twin of the persistent bash tool and uses the same file delivery, nonce brackets and interrupt-then-verify rule, which removes its echo, ESC and prompt-redefinition limits.

The provider registry is kept with one registration path, concurrent provider queries under a deadline, a kept last-good catalogue per provider, per-skill diagnostics and an inspectable list of shadowed definitions.

The local provider keeps the same roots, front matter and one-level layout; it reads through the filesystem seam, uses the shared watch service instead of private chokidar and polling code, and contains a failure to the one skill that caused it.

The router and three authoring skills are kept as data embedded in the binary and served by a provider; their text names the Go office tools of area A16 and points at the user's Python or one configured interpreter.

The catalogue, the skill tool and explicit user invocation are kept; the catalogue becomes a fold with deltas, the tool enforces invocation policy and a size cap in the pipeline, and plain-text invocation is limited to the first token of a message.

The package reports paths into a Python, Node.js and pnpm payload that upstream's desktop application and SDK wheel carry. The Go product is one pure-Go binary with nothing bundled or downloaded, so the tool would describe an artifact nobody builds; the Office skills point at the user's Python instead.

The spill storage seam is kept as a Go contract package. The one-method interface grows to reserve, create (a writer for text or a stream), open, stat and delete, so that retention and access by session lineage are part of the contract.

Private files with random names and exclusive owner-only creation are kept. Files always live under the harness home instead of a per-process temporary directory, and the start-up sweep becomes part of the timed maintenance duty.

The policy that replaces an oversized tool result with a head and tail preview and a notice is kept as a listener on the pipeline's shape-and-bound stage. Its budget has no off value, it bounds the result even when saving fails, and it marks the result with a structured field.

The remote filesystem provider is kept as a thin forwarder to the helper, which runs the local filesystem provider where the files are; file content moves to its own stream so the 8 MiB frame cap disappears.

Upstream needs a separate provider that asks the helper for a wrapped argv; in Go a remote start runs the same seam on the remote host and returns the confinement as data, so the provider is part of the remote world component.

The OpenSSH alias, batch mode, strict host keys, helper identity check, lease and no-replay rule are kept; the control master, forwarded Unix sockets and TLS pre-shared keys are replaced by one channel with a stream multiplexer, because Go's crypto/tls has no pre-shared-key mode.

The package exists to pack Node, the helper and worker entry points into one executable with loose native files; the Go helper is a hidden mode of the one static dsh binary, so there is no carrier, no resolution hook and no worker dispatch.

The remote process and terminal provider is kept as a forwarder to the helper's local starter; standard streams and terminal bytes are multiplexed streams owned by the process handle instead of forwarded sockets.
