The hub is a name-to-backend table plus a map of mounted data forms and does no I/O itself. With one database and no interchangeable backends there is nothing left for it to register, so it is not built.

The typed API that product code uses (declared domains, validated records, one write queue, a change event) is kept in substance as the kv package: namespaces in one table, a version per record, one transaction per update, and a change notice that also covers writes by other processes.
The JSON file backend rewrites a whole unit per write, has no cross-process lock and no crash-atomic batch. Machine state moves to tables in the one database, so no JSON state backend is built.

Its document-per-row idea survives as the kv table, but inside the one harness database opened by the session store's driver package, not as a second database with its own open sequence and layout version.

The named-provider registry and the single activation manager are kept as component subagent.manager in internal/delegate/subagent. Each activation becomes a fiber under a per-tree fiber owned by the root agent's scope, the per-parent catalog becomes one tree ledger in the root's log, and settlement gets one fixed order with a durable record before anyone is told.

The ACP provider is kept as a Runner on the shared external run lifecycle: one agent process per task, started through the one spawn helper, driven by the client role of the acpwire wrapper. It gains a third permission policy, ask, that forwards the agent's permission request to a person.

Upstream drives a bundled Claude Code executable through the vendor's npm SDK. The Go provider gives the same one-shot delegation by starting the claude executable the user installed in print mode and reading its streaming JSON, as the library specification decided; the provider contract, the operator-fixed permission mode and the fixed-word diagnostics are kept.

The Codex provider keeps upstream's shape: one app-server process, one unsaved thread and one turn per task over a minimal hand-written client. The executable is the one the user installed, not a bundled one, and a fourth permission mode, ask, routes approval requests to a person.

The provider that runs a task in a second dsh process over the SDK protocol is kept on the shared external lifecycle. By default it starts the running executable, it may share the harness home because sessions are leased, and it passes preset, depth and creator at initialize.

The fork provider is kept as a Preparer that returns the creator's completed-turn prefix and never sees the child agent; it lives with spawn in internal/delegate/subagent/local. The prefix rule is protected by a test that compares the request head byte for byte.
The spawn provider is kept as a Preparer that returns an empty seed; the manager creates the child agent, applies the delegation boundary and mounts the inherited or named preset.

The delegation tool (one component per configured instance), the model discovery tool and the live route setting are kept in internal/delegate/subagent/tools. Added: several operator-declared targets behind one tool, a wait argument that returns the bounded result, preset descriptions in the schema and a composition-time check of preset ids.

send_message, wait_agent, interrupt_agent and list_agents and the identity context are kept as component subagent.tools. Listing is paged and reads one projection, a wait is keyed on the inbox's log position, and a settled child can be dismissed.

The subprocess seam is kept as a Go contract package: lookup, Start and StartTerminal from a fully explicit spec, never a shell string. It changes in three ways: a required launch plan, a stop ladder inside the seam, and an outcome that records why a run was stopped.

The local provider is kept as the component that wraps the single process package. Tree owners are held by the host itself (job object, control group, process group) instead of a helper Node process and a systemd-run scope per command; collectors spill to the storage area; terminals are allocated by own code instead of node-pty.

The package exists to bind Win32 process, stdio and job-object calls through the koffi foreign-function library. Go calls the same functions through golang.org/x/sys/windows inside the process package, with no binding table, layout probe or separate library package.

The task board and the per-session Team mode are kept as component team.board with service key team.Key: whole-task snapshots in the root's log changed by compare-and-set. Added: one change notice per task, a user as actor, and release of a task whose owner's run failed.

The four task tools and the team policy prompt section are kept as component team.tools, shown for a whole tree only while the root's Team mode is on, with the same schemas for the root and every member.

The channel factory built on seven OpenTelemetry SDK packages and a second HTTP client is replaced by one harness exporter on the standard library, as the library specification decided. This area adds that a channel needs a sharing permit, reports each batch's outcome, and drains for three seconds on unload.

The owner-scoped session service is kept: ids minted by the service, publication only after backend setup, one send at a time, every operation fenced to the owner, awaited cleanup. It gains Resize and Attach so a browser can view a session.

The persistent shell backend for bash and pwsh is kept, with two changes: the model reads the emulated screen instead of a hand-written byte filter, and readiness compares screen text and command brackets instead of raw bytes after a marker.

Mounting the loop's prerequisites and driving a production agent is the compose package of the test kit, which boots real components through the real loader with a scripted model; the two Inbox stubs are not carried because fakes exist only at seams.

The jsdom slot bench and whole-client tier test a React client that the Go design does not have; server-rendered fragments are tested with golden files and HTML query helpers through the real handlers.
The scriptable fault server is kept as testkit/faultserver with upstream's behaviour list, per-key script cursors, and a deterministic scripted refusal at the egress seam.

Keyless replay of recorded model streams is kept as the llm.replay component: a listener on area A04's stream interception point plus a stub route registration, with scripts bound to child sessions by lineage and the live request compared with the recorded one.

Booting a fixture's real entry point in a child process is done by testkit/dshbin, which builds the dsh binary once per run and runs it with a private home, capped output and whole-tree termination; the source-versus-built mode switch has no Go counterpart.
The package mocks Typert Remote traffic between upstream's JavaScript browser client and its host; the Go design has no Typert layer and no client program, so there is nothing to mock.

Recorded-session testing is kept in the Go design's own formats: the test/replay runner with one driver per surface, typed normalisation tokens, a typed scenario manifest, workspace comparison and fixture guards.

Fixture tools and tool execution without a full turn are kept in the test kit: a fixture tool is declared like any tool and called through the pipeline's direct-caller entry on a real in-memory session, and a conformance helper checks that a body honours cancellation.
The todo_write tool, the todo/write whole-list event and the todos projection are kept with the same contract as a Go component.

The build-time TypeScript analyser and artifact generator exists to recover erased types; Go derives schemas from its types by reflection when they are registered, and the one remaining emitter is the protocol schema document derived from the method table and held equal by a test.

It exists only because of npm and generated JavaScript: it imports each mounted npm package's generated ./typert export at run time. The Go design generates no artifact and loads no package, so there is nothing to discover or register.

What survives is folded into the codec and the protocol package: the single failure type with domain/reason codes becomes jsonrpc.Error and the shared error table, and the invocation descriptor idea becomes the method table. The Remote decorators, lookup maps and browser event forwarding are not built because no browser application calls host methods.

The runtime registry of generated reflection, schema factories and invocation descriptors is replaced by the schema package, which derives and caches a schema per Go type, and by static method tables; no service holds them because compiled-in types are never unloaded.

Atomic file replacement and the writer lock are provided by the fsx package that area A08 owns: Replace stages, optionally syncs and renames, and the lock is a kernel file lock instead of a lock file holding a process ID.

Branded string and number types exist because TypeScript types are structural; each confusable identifier becomes a defined Go type declared by its owner, which the compiler keeps distinct, so no helper package is needed.
The persistent chunked list gives frozen projection state cheap appends; in Go a fold owns an append-only slice and hands readers a capped view, which is an immutable snapshot at no copying cost.
The extension-to-language table becomes the Language function of the mediatype leaf package, beside the media-type table, and gains whole-file-name rules; the host-side highlighter reads it.

The UUID helper exists because browsers lack randomUUID on plain-HTTP pages; the Go host mints every identifier through the ident leaf package on crypto/rand, and base64 comes from the standard library.

The circular deque avoids linear-time array shifts in JavaScript; a Go queue is a bounded channel or a bounded slice ring inside its one owner, and its declaration states what happens when it is full.

The dependency-free error base with a stable machine-readable code is kept as the herr leaf package: an error value carrying a domain/reason constant declared by the package that owns the failure, found with errors.As.
Safe export file names from a declared media type become SafeName in the mediatype package; the native drag requests served the desktop application, which the owner removed.

The one resolver for the harness home (explicit path, DSH_HOME, then ~/.dsh, blank counted as unset), tilde expansion and symbolic display are the homedir leaf package; the layout under the root is area A07's and watch-path canonicalisation moves inside the watch service.

The one outbound proxy policy is kept and becomes the egress service: every HTTP client, WebSocket dial and telemetry export is built by it from values resolved once at launch, instead of replacing a process-wide dispatcher.

The frozen, layered launch environment with a recorded source per value is the launch.Env value that area A21 builds before the tree; egress and other readers receive a lookup over it and nothing reads the process environment directly.
Caller-relative lazy loading of CommonJS modules exists only because of Node's module system; a Go binary is linked statically and a deferred initialisation is sync.OnceValue.

The shell-free run-and-capture wrapper is the capture helper of the one process package that area A09 owns; of the path-opening functions only the default-browser hand-off is kept, and revealing a file or listing its applications is not built because the web UI has no native shell integration.

The compiled-in lists of npm bundle packages become the embedded bundles, profile layers and optional list of the boot family (areas A27 and A21): every component is already in the binary, so a list entry is a default-off loader entry.
The bounded-retention primitive is kept as the retain leaf package, with head, tail and head-and-tail windows for both text and items, rune-safe cuts and an exact omitted count.

The shared TypeScript declarations of package.json plugin fields become the one plugin manifest struct that area A22 owns; a Go struct with schema validation is declaration and validator at once, and a plugin is a local directory, not an npm package.

The fixed, localised fallback order for a plugin's long description is kept over the local plugin directory and belongs to area A22; the npm file CDN and repository sources go because nothing is downloaded.

The market index validator has no reader: the owner decided that plugins come from local directories and that nothing is discovered or downloaded; a later registry would define its own format behind the same manifest.
Resolving and spawning a packaged rg executable is replaced by file search in process, in pure Go, in the search package area A08 owns; there is no executable to locate.
The tiered multilingual filter for in-memory lists is kept as the textsearch leaf package with an own scorer; lists are filtered on the host.

The shared time vocabulary is kept as two leaf packages: caltime (strict instant and zone parsers, the gap and overlap resolver) and recur (cron, RRULE, interval and wall-time rules behind one Rule interface with Next and Resolve).

Deadline arithmetic, signal fusion and timeout-versus-cancel classification are context.WithTimeoutCause and context.Cause in the standard library; the idle watchdog becomes egress.IdleBody; termination stays with each capability as upstream decided.

Lossless-JSON checks, snapshots, deep freezing, structural equality and exhaustive-switch helpers compensate for untyped, shared JavaScript objects; Go uses typed values, copies and the schema package. The lazy reader of streamed tool arguments is kept as the jsonscan leaf package.

Browser-safe lexical path helpers exist because client code cannot touch a file system; the host resolves paths and renders titles (area A07) and file addresses become HTTP routes (area A19), so no shared package remains.
web_search and web_fetch are kept with the same names, arguments and result texts, the HTML converter of the turndown library specification, and partial success for multi-query searches.

The web seam is kept as a contract and service with two provider registries and execution-time selection; availability and readiness become one context-taking check and the route preference becomes configuration.

The vendor Search and Fetch API providers are kept behind the seam with the same provider ids and billing settings; the user's prompt is no longer sent by default and a fetch result no longer invents a status.
The anonymous HTTP fetch provider is kept with its caps and same-origin redirect rule, built on the egress client factory, and gains the destination guard and charset detection.
The model-backed search provider is kept at lower priority, with its auxiliary request logged before it is sent, its endpoint derived from the route by default and no literal key in configuration.

The model-facing workflow tool keeps its name, its meta block, its usage guidance, its foreground result and its background-job path. Changed: the script is text for a named interpreter (or a file) instead of a JavaScript body, the result is the script's standard output with a spill locator when cut, and the durable record is written by the service instead of mirrored by the tool.

The workflow contract (start request, run, closed stop reasons, result, observe-only events) is kept as a Go contract package with one service key. Changed: the service owns and tracks every run, the events are durable session events plus one live narration event, and the stop reasons gain timeout and interrupted.

The engine that evaluated a JavaScript body in a vm context inside the PTC Node process, with five helper functions, cannot exist without the guest runtime. A different mechanism gives the result: the engine starts a named interpreter on the script file as one supervised sandboxed process, the agent() helper becomes the blocking tool workflow_agent reached through dsh tool call, and the other helpers become the script's own language, an argument, standard error and standard output.

The workspace registry is kept: canonical-path records, a session ledger, order, pin and archive with the rule that archive never hides running work. It moves to real tables with one transaction per mutation, and activity providers become a Go interface.

The Python client is kept as a pure-Python subprocess client with the same model (lazy start, sessions, run results, approvals, questions, close ladder), but it is redesigned: types are generated from the protocol schema, the run result and notification scoping come from the host, and approvals become a callback.

The carrier package for a single-file Node executable is replaced by platform wheels of the one distribution that hold the ordinary Go dsh binary; the 159-entry closure manifest, the Node bootstrap, the sidecars and the download manifest have no counterpart.

The workspace root holds only build configuration (package scripts, six tsconfig files, eight vitest configurations, the tsdown configuration, a Makefile); in Go that job is done by go.mod and go.work, go test lanes and one small sequential gate runner.

The gate scheduler, 51 verify scripts, 17 generators and the release scripts become Go tests, go/analysis checkers, one registry-driven catalog generator and GoReleaser; gates that guard npm publication, bilingual documents and contributor process are not carried over.

These scripts build, sign, notarize, verify and stage the macOS computer-use helper application and reuse earlier signed artifacts. The owner decided that the Go project ships no native helper and that computer use works only through an external MCP server the operator installs, so there is no helper to build, sign, verify or stage and the release tooling is not ported.

The scripts build, inspect and release the Node single-file helper for four targets; the Go release already builds dsh for every target, dsh ssh install uploads and pins it, and the handshake probe survives as the hello check and the real-host scenario.
The recorded-session replay system is kept, but the 2,039 fixture files are in upstream's session format and are not reused; the Go corpus is recorded from the Go product in its own format.

The framework core already exists in Go as package cordis in src/go, tracking upstream 86f59e4, which is 51 commits ahead of the harness's vendored rc.12. Seven of the 54 API rows the harness uses are gaps; six deliverables close them, and the JavaScript-only parts (proxy context, mixins, accessors, decorators) are replaced by typed keys.

Sixteen of the 22 helper names imported anywhere map to Go built-ins or the standard library (maps, slices, reflect.DeepEqual, encoding/base64, encoding/hex, time); the other six are the volatile config reference, which is not built: a live setting reaches a component through its update hook (DH-ADR-COSMOKIT-2, DH-ADR-LOADER-7).
The package is a three-line re-export of the loader's Group plugin; in Go a group is a kind of entry inside the loader with children, inject and isolate, not a separate plugin.
Config reload is kept through the loader's watched layer source; in-process code reload is impossible for compiled-in components and becomes a restart of the entry that owns a plugin process.
File binding, patches and the journal are replaced by a codec seam, first-class layer composition with one writable layer, and the existing snapshot three-way merge refined to fields.
The entry tree, reconciliation and write-back already exist in src/go/loader; the design adds intercept, full validation with source positions, an expression seam and a mutation API to it.
The Go cordis logger already has console and slog exporters; a harness logging component configures them, and the cosmetic formatting options are not carried over.

Plugin config is declared as a Go struct with defaults, tag constraints and a Validate method, checked through the cordis port's Schema interface; the vendored, locally patched schema builder is not ported.
src/go/timer already provides fiber-owned timeout, interval, sleep, throttle and debounce with tests, and the design uses it unchanged.

The owner keeps the documentation website: the VitePress projection of docs/ is replaced by a static site that Hugo, a Go generator pinned as a docs-only tool in its own module and workflow, builds from the same Markdown without copying it; the second locale and the theme extensions (viewer, table filter, code groups, Markdown twins, search) are not carried over in the first version.

ctx.actionCards registers card kinds, records decisions and takes user actions on cards. The card mechanism is not built, so no service key replaces it; approvals go through area A17's interaction registry.
Replaced by service key defaultmodel.Key with Current (by scope key), Register (a scoped default) and Save; Save calls config.Service.Apply of the boot area and returns its result.
The Go driver exposes no service of its own: it fills the registry's factory seat and reads its limits from its component config, so consumers cannot depend on the driver.

ctx.agentPresets becomes the service key agentpreset.Key with interface agentpreset.Service: List, Resolve, Default, Acquire, AcquireFrom, Of, Select, Lookup and Inventory. A lease object replaces the user counter, and Lookup replaces serviceFor.
Replaced by service key team.Key with interface Board: Mode, SetMode, Create, Get, List and Update, each taking an actor that is an agent or an owner principal.
Replaced by service key agent.Agents and the Registry interface (Create, Resume, Get, Resolve, List, SetFactory), with the owner passed explicitly.
ctx.approval becomes approval.Service under approval.Key: Request, the session policy and the session-grant operations.
ctx.attachments becomes the service key attachments.Key with the interface attachments.Store, a direct seam whose provider is the local store component.
ctx.authorization becomes authz.Service under authz.Key: flow registration, one attempt per record, sign-out with revocation and the list of records with their claim state.

ctx.browserUse becomes the service key browser.Key with interface browser.Service: Register(provider) as an exclusive effect, Status, and For(session), which returns that session's browser. Registration now carries a provider that implements browser.Provider instead of a bare name.
ctx.claudeCodeMods is the registry and band stream of the mods bridge, which is not built, so no Go service key replaces it.
The service key cliaccount.Key provides Register for a CLI and its account operations, as an effect on the caller's fiber.

ctx.clientModules composes the boot graph of client bundles and serves them. The Go service that stands in its place is shell.Key (interface Shell): it owns the layout, the region registry and the island table, and composes no bundle graph because pages are rendered on the host.
ctx.commands becomes command.Registry under command.Key: scoped registration, discovery and one Execute entry for every carrier.
Replaced by the service key compact.Key with the interface Engine: Consider for automatic triggers, Now for an idle session and Region for an explicit span.

ctx.computerUse becomes the service key computer.Key with interface computer.Service: Register(provider) as an exclusive effect and Status. Registration carries a provider that implements computer.Provider instead of a bare name.
ctx.config exists in the browser to read another package's synced config. No Go service replaces it: there is no browser plugin, and a component reads only its own typed config struct on the host.

Replaced by service key config.Key with interface config.Service: Tree, Preview, Apply and Status. It keeps validate-then-write-then-reconcile and the refusal of a shadowed edit, and adds a preview that starts nothing, a revision check, merge operations and a cross-process lock.

ctx.connection joins the transport, the source check, peer creation and the authentication registry. On the host those are area A18's listen.Key and its listen.Authenticate key; in the browser the connection is the stream client of the first-party script, which is not a service.

No service key replaces ctx.connectorAccounts in this area. Its registration contract is area A15's connector package (AccountView, AccountSource) and its listing is mcp.Service.Accounts(); the connections section renders those values and calls the fleet's own operations.

ctx.cordisInspect becomes the service key inspect.Key with the interface inspect.Service (Register as an effect, List, Query); the client manifest mirror and the client query round trip are not carried over.

ctx.cotTranslation is a remote controller with two methods for the browser. There is no service in Go: limits becomes the settings read by the view, and translate becomes a host route that names an event and a block instead of carrying text.
ctx.credentials becomes secret.Store under secret.Key: leases for references, description without the value, one-way writes, records, enumeration and masking.
No service key replaces it. Its three operations are routes of the settings route component, which calls area A17's credential store and renders presence and a masked preview only.

ctx.cuaAccess gave the browser system-permission status, permission requests, saved application grants and revocation. In Go, application grants are session grants listed and revoked through area A17; the driver's permission status is a line of A16's computer.Status that the adapter fills by one promptless call; the harness never requests a system permission or opens system settings.
ctx.cuaPrograms releases an agent's retained cua_run_code environment and reports screenshot request targets for programs. There is no program environment in the Go design.
ctx.deepseekAccount becomes account.Service under account.Key: sign-in, sign-out, on-demand profile and balance, and host-only release of request headers.
ctx.deepseekAuth becomes the account.Authorizer interface under account.AuthKey in the account package; it returns ready headers for one kind and never tries a second.

ctx.deepseekChatImport becomes the service key chatimport.Key with the interface Importer (Limits, Plan, Run). The upload route and the command are carriers that call it; the owner-only rule is the route's access rule and the command's admin class.
ctx.deepseekLlmApiExtensions becomes the service key transport.ContributionsKey, where a component registers a named contributor that prepares a field and accepts delivery after HTTP 2xx.

ctx.directoryPicker becomes the service key dirbrowse.Key with interface dirbrowse.Service (List and CreateDirectory). The capability method that told a consumer which interaction a backend offers is gone because there is one interaction.
No service key replaces it. Directory picking is the route directory.browse of the workspace route component, a server-rendered picker over the host filesystem, owner only.

ctx.dynamicCordisRunner becomes the service key plugin.Key with the interface plugin.Service (Inspect, Plugins, Run, Attach, Detach, Restart); define, run, stop and undefine of source text and every browser-facing remote method have no counterpart.
Replaced by the service key fileref.Key with one method, List, which returns ranked candidates and a truncated flag for one agent's workspace.

ctx.fileUploads owns the streaming route and an in-memory table of staged receipts per session. The route is A19's session.upload over A07's attachments.Store, and the receipt table becomes the session's draft record in A07's store, so no separate service remains; this area supplies the upload control.

ctx.forge becomes the service key forge.Key with interface forge.Service: Register and Watch as effects of the caller's fiber, Resolve, Latest, Refresh, FindByHead and Readiness. The write and review methods of upstream's service are not carried.

ctx.forgePanel is a typed remote surface for the React client. In Go the component x.forge.ui registers HTTP routes and one stream source with the API area and contributes fragments to UI regions; it offers no service, because no other component calls it.

ctx.forgeSession becomes the service key bind.Key with interface bind.Service: ChangeRequests, Watch, Track, Dismiss and DiscoverBranch. registerCommands is not carried as a runtime call: command rules are compiled-in data declared by each provider package.
ctx.fs becomes the service key fs.Key holding the fs.FileSystem interface, a direct seam. Model-facing tools use a second key, fs.OpsKey, for the operation service.
ctx.goals becomes service key goal.Key with interface goal.Service (Get, Create, Update, Disarm); mutations name an exact id and revision and carry the caller's authority.

No service replaces it in this area. The parsed command-line values stay inside area A24's cli.headless component; if a config field must read one of them, that component declares an expression view in the catalogue, as boot.md describes for carrier start-up values.

No Go service takes its place. Its exclusive queue is the layer source's serial loop reached through config.Service.Apply, its configuration watch is the loader's layer watch switched on by the boot.reload component, a restart of one entry is the loader's Restart, and its module methods have no subject.

The service hosts a DevTools debugging target and a cordis tree query interface for the experimental inspector. The target is not built in Go; tree queries are the loader's lookup interface and process inspection uses the Go profiler endpoints.
No service key replaces it. The job routes and their two stream interests call area A13's job registry directly.
ctx.jobs becomes service key jobs.Key with interface jobs.Registry (Start, List, Get, Peek, Commit, ReadAt, Kill, Wait, Remove, Subscribe, RegisterKind, AttachController).

ctx.liveshareShares (twelve owner-only remote methods) is replaced by the service key sessionshare.Key with the interface Shares: Create, List, Stop and StopAll. The methods that manage the relay address, the owner's relay identity, plugin capabilities, the relay's audit trail and the two relay tests have no counterpart because there is no relay; tier and fork changes have none because a viewer cannot act. Audit is a local table read by the list page.
ctx.llm becomes the service key llm.RuntimeKey with the Runtime interface: register routes, list routes and models, prepare a call, and complete a buffered one-shot call.
The service key lsp.Key provides lsp.Service with Register, Query and Status.
There is no separate account service: mcp.Service.Accounts returns the account view of every OAuth entry and saved grant.
The host service existed so that the manager could mount client plugin instances; in Go the fleet calls the connection package directly and offers Register and Probe itself.
The service key mcp.Key provides mcp.Service: Servers, Register, Restart, Probe, Authorize, CancelAuthorization, SignOut and Accounts.
Resource listing and reading are methods of the server handle that mcp.Service gives out, so no scoped resource registry is needed.
ctx.messageFeedback is folded into feedback.Service under feedback.Key, which serves message ratings and session remarks from one projection.

ctx.officeKit becomes the service key office.Key with interface office.Service: Status, PDF, Convert, Recalculate and Images. The engine is a second key, office.EngineKey, so the engine can change without touching the service's consumers. The two remote methods are not carried: the preview route calls the service in process.

ctx.otel becomes the service key otlplog.Key with interface otlplog.Service. Its two factory methods for ordinary and session-log channels become one NewChannel that takes a sharing permit and options, and providing the service still allocates nothing.
ctx.permissionPresets becomes permission.Service under permission.Key: the catalogue, the current selection and the owner-only switch.

ctx.planMode becomes service key plan.Key with interface plan.Controller (Get, Set); the state it returns distinguishes the logged value, the value captured for the open step and whether plan mode was ever active.

Replaced by service key plugins.Key with interface plugins.Manager: List, Inspect, Add, SetEnabled, Restart and Remove. The package, registry, version, exemption and detail-document methods are gone under DH-ADR-13.
The service reads and searches market indexes. No index reader is built.

ctx.pluginRecommendations has one remote method, describe, which returns catalogue text for a card. With no card there is nothing to describe; the feature-guide skill reads the catalogue from area A21's plugins.Manager directly.
The service races the response time of two public npm registries to recommend one for an installation. The Go harness installs nothing from a registry, so there is nothing to recommend.

ctx.productAnalytics takes events from the renderer and the desktop shell and adds identity and machine facts. Its replacement is area A18's report.Key (interface Reporter): a typed, closed catalogue that route handlers report to and that sends only with a permit.

ctx.productTelemetry.emit becomes the service key report.Key with interface report.Reporter, whose two methods take events declared in a closed catalog under the analytics or telemetry kind and drop them when that kind has no permit.

Replaced by service key launch.Key holding the immutable launch.Data (profile, home, working directory, version, terminal flag, overlay paths, app words), with launch.EnvKey and launch.AppKey beside it. The package-manager invocation and the installation anchor are gone, and the telemetry opt-out value moves to the launcher layer.

There is no Go service key for a program runtime. The owner removed the guest runtime, so there is one way to run model-written code and nothing for a seam to select between; consumers use the subprocess seam and the tool pipeline directly.
Replaced by the service key access.Key with the interface access.Service: RegisterKind, RegisterPolicy, Decide, Allows and Invalidate.

ctx.sandbox becomes the service key sandbox.Key with the interface sandbox.Service (Describe, Reprobe, Prepare); Prepare returns a launch plan that the one process starter requires and executes, instead of an argv each consumer spawns and classifies.
ctx.sandboxPolicy becomes the service key policy.Key with the interface policy.Resolver (Resolve, Escalate, ForPlugin, GrantRoot, SetMode), the only constructor of a policy value.

ctx.schedule becomes service key schedule.Key with interface schedule.Service (Create, Edit, Get, List, History, RunNow, Status); every method takes the caller so that scoping is enforced in the service.
Replaced by conversation.Key with the interface Commands (Create, Prompt, Continue, Fork), which holds the ordering rules a carrier needs; reads go to area A06's query service and to the stream.
ctx.sessionFeedback is folded into feedback.Service under feedback.Key together with message ratings; it works on a closed session by taking the lease for the append.
No service key replaces it. File-reference completion is the route session.complete, which searches through the filesystem seam of the session's world without waking the session.
ctx.sessionLogDeepSeek becomes the service key logupload.Key, whose interface keeps the registration of upload exclusions owned by the registering fiber.
ctx.sessionPersistence becomes the service key store.Key with the interface store.Store: create, open for read or write, stat, paged list, delete, flush and follow.
There is no separate cache service: checkpoint reads and writes are part of the projection registry behind projection.Key.
The service key projection.Key with the Registry interface (Snapshot, Rebuild, Status) and the generic Register function replace ctx.sessionProjections.
The service key query.Key with the Query interface replaces ctx.sessionQuery; every method takes a Visibility and search is concrete.
Replaced by the service key sessionref.Key with the interface Resolver: Candidates and Prepare, both taking the caller's principal.
No service key replaces it. Skill completion is the same route session.complete, reading area A14's skill catalog without waking the session.

ctx.sessionStatus stores the owner's reading acknowledgements and manual unread marks outside session history and streams them to clients (docs/capability-seams.md:741). It becomes the service key reading.Key with interface reading.Service (Status, Seen, Mark). The follow stream is replaced by the shell state of the event stream, and records are stored per principal instead of kept in a process map.

The service key upload.Key with the Uploads interface (Status, Preview, Authorise, Cancel) replaces ctx.sessionTelemetry; there is no emit method, so no caller can send a record outside a confirmed upload.
The service key title.Key with the Titles interface (Get, Rename, Unpin, Refresh) and the title.Providers registry replace ctx.sessionTitle.
ctx.sessions becomes the service key session.Key with the interface session.Service (Prepare, Create, Open, OpenRead, Fork, Get, Live), provided by the component core.Component.

ctx.settings becomes the service key settings.Key with the interface settings.Forms, provided by a component that reads the composed tree from config.Service of the boot area and writes only through config.Service.Apply.
No service key replaces it. The settings routes call area A07's settings.Forms (Describe, Apply) and render the forms; a stale write is a 409.

ctx.shell becomes the service key shellexec.Key (shell.Key is the page shell's key in the UI area), a registry of Executor values by dialect (Dialect, Resolve, Start), so bash and pwsh providers can be mounted together.
ctx.shellEnv becomes the service key shellenv.Key with Register, Collect and a complete List; a contributor's entries leave with its fiber.
Replaced by the service key skill.Key with the interface Registry: RegisterProvider, Snapshot and Load. The separate direct-registration method is replaced by the skill.Static provider helper.

The remote methods catalog, follow, configure and transcribe become the speech.view, speech.select and speech.transcribe routes and the speech.StatusChanged event of the x.speech component; prepare and cancelPreparation have no counterpart because nothing is downloaded.

ctx.speechToText becomes the service key speech.Key with the interface speech.Service: Register by exact id as an effect of the provider's fiber, Catalog, Transcribe through exactly one resolved provider, and Select.
ctx.spillStore becomes the service key spill.Key with the interface spill.Store, a direct seam whose provider is the local spill component.

ctx.ssh becomes the service key ssh.Key with the interface ssh.Connection, which reports connection state; its component mounts the filesystem, process and sandbox providers of the remote world together, and request and stream calls are internal to it.
ctx.storage is the hub's registration table for backends and data forms; no hub exists in the Go design, so no service replaces it.
ctx.storageDomain becomes the service key kv.Key with the interface kv.Store, which opens typed namespaces in the one database instead of domains over routed backends.
Replaced by service key subagent.RoutesKey, whose Allowed method reads the live host setting subagent-model-selection at every call and returns the authorised routes or that selection is off.

Replaced by service key subagent.Key with interface Runtime: Register, Start, Send, Prompt, Interrupt, Dismiss, Tree, Resolve, RootOf and WaitQuiet. drainDescendants has no counterpart because root teardown is structural.

ctx.subprocess becomes the interface subprocess.Service (World, Lookup, Start, StartTerminal) under the key subprocess.Key for the execution world and subprocess.HostKey for children that must run on the host machine.
Replaced by the Go interface prompt.Service under the service key prompt.Key: Section, Variable, Context, Suppress, Assemble and Render.
Replaced by userterm.Key with the interface userterm.Service for the person's terminals (create, list, rename, close, hold, reclaim); agent terminals are area A09's terminal.Key.
ctx.terminals becomes the interface terminal.Service under terminal.Key: Open, Send, Read, Signal, Resize, Attach, Close and List, each taking the owner.
ctx.tokenMeter becomes the service key meter.Key with Measure, Pressure and EstimateMessage.
Replaced by the service key prune.Key with the interface Pruner: Measure, PruneContent and PruneSession.
Replaced by the Go interface tools.Service under the service key tools.Key: registration, step view, the three entries into the pipeline and the catalogue.

ctx.translator becomes the service key translate.Key with the interface Service: Providers, Lookup and Translate. resolve and translate merge into one call that takes a fragment reference instead of text, and availableProviders becomes Providers with a reason for each unavailable one.

ctx.typert has no Go service key. Its jobs are done by the schema package function schema.Of (schemas by reflection, cached per type), by the static method table protocol.Methods (invocation descriptors) and by each registry's own catalog output.
There is no typed call dispatcher: a handler is a Go function registered as a route and calls services directly. web.Key registers routes and dispatches no remote calls.
The service key skillset.Key provides Register, Install and Verify for pinned skill directories.
ctx.userQuestions becomes question.Service under question.Key: ask with a deadline through the interaction registry, the hold, and Reply for a late answer.
The service key web.Key provides web.Service: provider registration, Search, Fetch, Check and Providers.

ctx.webApp offered one method, the advertised URL. That value is owned by area A18's host.launch component, which prints it, opens it and exposes it; the web layer mounts that component instead of a bundle-owned service.

ctx.webServer is split in two. The socket's facts (Origin, Secure, Mode, Ready, Done) and the Mount call that attaches a handler behind the admission pipeline become the service key listen.Key with interface listen.Listener. Registering a UI route is area A19's web.Key, which mounts its table on the listener. registerFallback, readResource and the index rendering methods have no counterpart.

ctx.webhookRuntime becomes the service key webhook.Key with the interface webhook.Runtime. Dispatch records a verified delivery and runs matching rules in the background; register is gone because rules are configuration, and Records lists delivery states.

ctx.workflowEngine becomes the service key workflow.Key with the interface workflow.Service (Start, Lookup, List, Cancel, Admit): a direct seam with one provider component. Unlike upstream the service, not the caller, owns and tracks runs.
The service key workdir.Key with the Service interface (Get, Ensure, Set) replaces ctx.workingDirectory.
ctx.workspaceChanges becomes the service key deliver.ChangesKey holding the deliver.Changes interface (Summary and Diff), answered from the session log and the blob store instead of host memory.
No service key replaces it. The workspace routes call area A07's workspace.Registry, which already serialises mutations, and the shell stream source renders its changes.
Replaced by wsfiles.Key with the interface wsfiles.Service: Stat, Text, Open, List, Search and Watch, each taking a session and bounded by wsfiles.Config.
ctx.workspaceRegistry becomes the service key workspace.Key with the interface workspace.Registry, which also holds the registry of activity providers.

ctx.worktrees becomes the service key worktree.Key with interface worktree.Service: Create, Enter, Exit and Restore as upstream, Of for the folded state, and Pending for journal rows in place of the process-local cleanupOf.

The tool asks a second model to choose and perform an action from an instruction. That layer is dropped; the session's own model reads browser_snapshot and calls the plain click, type, key and scroll tools of A16's catalogue, each of which is logged.
The tool asks a second model to extract structured data from a page. That layer is dropped; the session's own model reads the page description returned by browser_snapshot.
Navigation is A16's browser_navigate tool, the same for every provider, implemented by the cdp provider through the page domain with the navigation guard on every document request.
The tool asks a second model which actions a page offers. That layer is dropped; browser_snapshot returns a bounded page description with element references and the session's own model decides.
Screenshots are A16's browser_screenshot tool, implemented by the cdp provider and stored as an attachment before the result that references it.
Listing, opening, selecting and closing tabs is A16's browser_tabs tool, implemented by the cdp provider through the target domain.

The Go harness exposes no separate tool definition: subagent_oar is area A12's delegation tool mounted under that name with operator-declared targets, each mapping an alias to an OAR provider instance. The model still picks an alias and cannot change launch arguments.

The Go harness exposes enter_worktree with the same name, the arguments name and from, and the result fields path, branch, baseCommit, repositoryRoot and created. Changed: the move goes through workdir.Service.SetForCall, so a target outside the anchor is refused as workdir/outside-anchor (DH-ADR-VIEW-8); a target outside the session's current write roots is refused as worktree/outside-roots; a failed creation is rolled back.

The Go harness exposes exit_worktree with the same name, no arguments and the same result fields. Changed: it returns the session to the directory it was in when it entered, recorded as from, not to the repository's top-level directory, and the move goes through workdir.Service.SetForCall, so leaving can never widen the write boundary or move the anchor (DH-ADR-VIEW-8).
The Go harness exposes the same tool; its server argument becomes optional and it is offered only while a connected server advertises resources.
The Go harness exposes the same tool; without a server argument it lists every visible resource-capable server in bounded sections.
The Go harness exposes the same tool with server and uri; an image blob is projected as an image and other binary content as a description.

Same name and argument (a Markdown plan starting with a heading), offered once plan mode has been active. It opens a typed plan-review interaction; approve, keep planning, dismiss, no reviewer and interruption each have a defined result. The plan is bounded by maxPlanBytes.

The Go harness exposes a changed tool of the same name with four actions: list and inspect read, attach and detach call area A22's session-scoped plugin attachment for the calling agent's own session. The install, bundle-selection and version-exemption actions are gone with pnpm and registries, and the tool has no action that changes the profile, because A22's rule (DH-ADR-EXT-8) and DH-ADR-16 forbid a consent given at a prompt from outliving the session. The tool body asks nothing; the one consent an attachment needs is an interaction asked by A22.
The tool lists the plugins of configured market indexes. With no market and no download there is nothing for it to read, so the Go harness exposes no such tool.
The same read-only tool, over the user-terminal service of area A19. Changed: it is registered only when readUserTerminals is set, which is off by default, and it is hidden from delegated agents.

The same read-only tool: it returns the newest screen lines of one of the person's terminals, bounded, and never waits or writes. Changed: off by default, because that text is logged and sent to the model provider.
The Go harness exposes the same tool with the same arguments (subject, description, blocked_by, write_scopes), shown only while the root's Team mode is on.
The Go harness exposes the same tool; the task view adds whether the owner is resident.
The Go harness exposes the same tool with the same filters and the same page limit of 100.
The Go harness exposes the same tool with the same eight actions and the required expected_revision; a stale revision returns the current one and only the root reassigns.

The Go harness exposes the same tool name with one schema: questions as upstream plus an optional timeout in seconds where -1 waits; a timed call returns pending and a later answer arrives as a user message.
The Go harness exposes a persistent bash tool under the same name, mounted instead of the one-shot component. It keeps the command argument and adds optional timeoutMs and restart.

The Go harness exposes a one-shot bash tool with the same arguments (description, command, timeoutMs, workdir, and run_in_background and the escalation pair when available). The result adds structured fields beside the text markers.

The Go harness exposes a changed tool, harness_inspect, with the same two-step shape (no argument lists providers, a query reads one). The platform argument and the client providers are gone, and the providers are Entries, Config, Tools, Events, Plugins, PluginProtocol and Runtime.
The Go harness exposes no run_code tool because it has no embedded interpreter; the model runs an ordinary script with the shell tool and the script calls tools through the tool endpoint.

The Go harness exposes glob with the same name and arguments plus an optional offset. It runs in process, walks only where the pattern can match, and still includes hidden and ignored files but not version-control directories.

The Go harness exposes grep with the same name and arguments plus optional output and offset. The pattern dialect changes from ripgrep syntax to Go RE2, which the description and the invalid-pattern error state.
The Go harness exposes apply_patch with the input argument, whole-patch preflight and ordered commit without rollback. It is on by default, following the upstream defaults note.
The Go harness exposes edit with the same arguments and result sentence. It is always fenced, bounded in size and re-checks the file before publishing.
The Go harness exposes read with the same arguments, envelope, footers and limits. A directory is listed instead of refused, and a non-text file is answered with the tool that reads it.
The Go harness exposes read_image while an attachment store is mounted. The file signature decides the type, and the tool also accepts an attachment reference and an optional region.
The Go harness exposes write with the same arguments and result envelope. It is always fenced, and content above the text size bound is refused.
Same name and arguments (objective, max_goal_rounds). Exclusive, direct reach only, allowed only in a human turn on a root agent, as upstream.
Same name and result: the current goal as compact JSON or null. The objective is bounded by maxObjectiveBytes.

Same name, actions and compare-and-set arguments. Authority rules are kept; a completion may additionally be rejected by a goal.Completing listener, and a terminal report from a goal round adds the closing instruction to its result.

Same name and arguments (job_id, reason). Requests cancellation and returns one snapshot; the job settles when its producer has returned or the stop grace has passed. Declared with direct reach only and denied in plan mode.
Same name, no arguments. Lists the caller's jobs one per line, parallel-safe, bounded to the per-owner live limit plus the settled-record cap with labels cut at 120 characters.

Same name and arguments (job_id, wait, timeout_ms). Returns output since the last read and a status line, exclusive, bounded by the ring size, the producer's output limit and the pipeline ceiling; a wait ends on settlement, timeout or the shared steer watch.
The Go harness exposes lsp with the same four operations; the cursor is given as a line with a character column counted in characters or a symbol name, instead of a UTF-16 column.

The Go harness exposes office_convert with the same name, formats and sheet rule. Changed: a required output path and an optional overwrite flag; the file is written there through the filesystem operation service and the result holds no temporary path.

The Go harness exposes office_recalculate with the same name and the xlsx and ods output formats. Changed: a required output path and an optional overwrite flag, as for office_convert; a LibreOffice version that ignores the recalculate-on-load setting gives office/unsupported-format instead of stale numbers.

The Go harness exposes office_render with the same name and the upstream arguments input, pages, sheet, range and dpi. Changed: an optional save_dir also writes the PNG files, a spreadsheet without a range is rendered as its printed pages, the result names the engine version, and a worksheet range fails as office/invalid-request until its scenario passes.
The Go harness exposes present with the same arguments and result lines. A declaration also records a digest and keeps a bounded copy.
The Go harness exposes a persistent pwsh tool under the same name, mounted instead of the one-shot component, with the command argument and optional timeoutMs and restart.
The Go harness exposes a one-shot pwsh tool as the PowerShell twin of bash, with the same arguments and structured result; its description states the resolved shell edition.

The Go harness exposes ralph with the same two arguments, objective and maxRounds, and the same three terminal statuses. Changed: the call is denied outside a human turn and for a delegated agent, and the result names the bound (rounds, time or tokens) that ended the run.

Same name; arguments title, prompt, rrule and target, plus an optional expire_after_seconds. Changed: allowed only in a human turn or after an approval, bounded by per-session and per-home caps and a prompt size limit, and the result says whether a firing host is live.
Same name; update, pause, resume or delete with a compare-and-set revision. Changed: scoped and authorised like schedule_create, and a delete reports whether a still-queued message was retracted.
Same name and arguments. Changed: it lists only schedules the calling session created or receives, returns summaries without prompt bodies, and its page limit is 20 by default and 100 at most.
Same name and argument. Changed: scoped to the caller's schedules, and the result adds host time, the next occurrence and the last five deliveries with their state.

The Go harness exposes list_session, changed: a keyset cursor replaces offset, include_blank is added, the result is an object with items, next_cursor and as_of, each item carries a title_state, and only sessions the caller's visibility admits are returned.

The Go harness exposes list_workspace, changed: a keyset cursor replaces offset and the result is an object with items and next_cursor, read from the workspace registry of area A07 under the caller's visibility.

The Go harness exposes session_event_read, changed: it calls Query.Event and returns the hot part of one event with at most ReadWindowMax neighbour summaries per side, and the pipeline's result bound applies last, where upstream returned the unabridged event inline.

The Go harness exposes session_event_search when the session-recall bundle is on, changed: it calls Query.Search inside one visible session, ends before the step that made the call when the target is the current session, and adds mode and cursor arguments.

The Go harness exposes session_event_trace unchanged in purpose: it calls Query.Trace and returns what replaced one event and what cites it, read from A06's derived class and link rows without replaying the log.

The Go harness exposes session_search when the session-recall bundle is on, changed: it calls Query.Search grouped by session with the agent's visibility, never returns the caller's own session, and adds a mode argument (ranked or literal) and a cursor with next_cursor; the availability filter is dropped because one store has no live-or-stored source. Every other upstream argument is kept under its upstream name: query, session_ids, created_at_from, created_at_to, parent_session_ids, include_root_sessions, event_seq_from, event_seq_to, event_time_from, event_time_to, event_types and event_surfaces.

The Go harness exposes session_trace unchanged in purpose: it calls Query.Lineage and returns the ancestors and descendants the caller may see, bounded by LineageMaxNodes, with a marker that carries no id where a boundary is hidden.

The Go harness exposes the same tool, skill with one name argument, declared once in the tool registry. Changes: the result states the source class and lists bundle files, the invocation policy and a size cap are enforced in the pipeline, and the body digest is recorded.
The Go harness can expose str_replace_editor with the same commands and schema. It is off unless a preset enables it.

The Go harness exposes the same tool: an ancestor asks a descendant to stop its current work, a local target keeps its queue, an external run stops for good, and an absent target is an accepted no-op.

The Go harness exposes the tool with a changed schema: optional cursor, limit and include_dismissed, and the statuses running, inactive, settled and missing. It reads one ledger projection instead of one catalog per member.
The Go harness exposes the same tool with the same two arguments. It steers the target, resumes a cold local member, and returns the durable receipt; the message size is bounded by maxMessageBytes.

The Go harness exposes the same tool with the same timeout range and the same one-field result. It observes only the caller's next-step inbox and is keyed on the inbox's log position, so an edited message ends a wait.
The Go harness exposes the same discovery tool, reading the live host route setting at each call; its result is paged at 100 rows.

The Go harness exposes the same delegation tool under each instance's configured name, with description, prompt and optional name. It adds target (several operator-declared providers behind one tool) and wait (return the bounded result instead of a notice); route and preset fields stay optional and authorised.
The same tool with the same argument. It ends the shell and waits for its process tree, or reports released when a person has taken control and the shell must keep running.
The same tool: it lists the calling agent's own sessions. Changed: each entry also reports who controls the terminal.
The same tool with type, name and cwd. Changed: the shell is the execution area's one backend, started with history disabled, and the start-up output is the emulated screen.
The same tool with sessionId, offset and count. Changed: it reads the host-side emulated screen and scrollback, so a full-screen program is readable.

The same tool with sessionId, text, submit and run_in_background. Changed: a keys argument sends named keys, the wait reason is the execution area's, the background field appears only with the job tools, and a send fails with an explanation once a person controls the terminal.
